level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

summary.description: Statement of the defect

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

severity.description: Set when the review instructions ask for it. important: a bug the change adds or makes worse; pre_existing: a bug that was there before the change; nit: a minor issue

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

(If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. Set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). Use ListPlugins for plugins they already have.

After the card, continue the task. Example: "ship this to staging" and a deploy plugin that is not enabled → contextLabel "For your deploys".

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a plugin would help, when SearchPlugins returned nothing relevant (then continue the task without mentioning the search), or if you already rendered a plugin or skill suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

schema.description:

Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

content.text:
The US-01 spec is approved at Gate 1 and committed as `df000c1`.

**Clarify answers (5 of 5)**, all in [spec.md](specs/002-us-01-policyholder-vehicle-form/spec.md) › Clarifications:
1. **RUT:** checked by format and by its check digit, through a named rule `rut`. This adds a new requirement, FR-014.
2. **When errors show:** after the person leaves the field or presses "Continuar". Once shown, an error updates as they type and clears when the value is valid. Fields nobody has touched show no error (FR-005).
3. **Seed fields:** Colombia gets 10 and Chile gets 9, all required (FR-013).
4. **When values are saved:** as the person types, even incomplete or invalid ones. This removes a contradiction in FR-009, which said only valid data was kept.
5. **Legal age:** set once on the Country (18 for both), as ADR 0001 says. The birth-date field's `legalAge` rule reads it (FR-007). That settles the first of the three ADR 0001 conflicts.

**What changed in the spec:** I added the Clarifications section and edited FR-005, FR-007, FR-009, FR-013, the edge cases, the assumptions and the ADR 0001 conflicts section, and added FR-014.
- The spec is 148 lines.
- The quality checklist still passes 16 of 16.
- The checklist's notes still list these points as open for clarify; I didn't edit them.
- No Spec Kit extension hooks are configured.

**Left for Gate 2:** the other two ADR 0001 conflicts. One is whether a field needs only a section, or also a step. The other is that the content manager must reject a field saved without a country.

# 0001 — Multi-country content strategy (Strapi + Angular)

- **Status:** Accepted (Gate 2, US-00 — 2026-11-22)
- **Date:** 2026-11-21
- **Related:** US-00, US-01, US-02, US-03

## Context and problem

The same application and the same build must sell car insurance in Colombia and Chile. Each country has its own regulations, identity documents, currency, coverages, terms and copy, and the business team (non-technical) must be able to change form fields and plans from Strapi without a deployment.

So we need to decide two things:

1. **Strapi:** how content is differentiated by country.
2. **Angular:** how the app knows which country to render.

## Decision drivers

- Add a new country without touching code or schema.
- Each piece of content (a field, a plan) can be edited and published on its own.
- No country data hardcoded in Angular: currency, format, legal age and terms live in Strapi.
- One build for every country.
- Easy to test per country (e2e).

## Part 1 — Strapi: Country as a collection with relations

### Decision

Let's take a **Country as collection** approach, and **FormField** and **Plan** as collections too, with a many-to-one relation towards Country. All three use native draft/published.

- **Country** saves `code`, `name`, `icon` (media), `order`, `active`, `currency`, `numberLocale` (e.g. `es-CO`), `legalAge` and `termsAndConditions`. Each story adds the fields it uses (US-00: `code`, `name`, `icon`, `order`, `active`).
- **FormField** saves `key`, `label`, `type`, `required`, `helpText`, `errorMessage`, `order` and `step`/`section`, plus two components:
  - `validations`: `min`, `max`, `pattern`, and `validators` with name and value.
  - `options`: for selects.
  - `key` is the stable technical name of the field (e.g. `documentNumber`, `vehicleYear`, `birthDate`). Angular uses it as the form control name, and the summary (masking) and the price rule use it to find values. Labels can't play this role because the business edits them. Unique per country.
  - `type` is an enumeration: `text`, `number`, `select`, `date`, `checkbox`.
- **Plan** saves `name`, `shortDescription`, `basePrice`, `order`, `recommended`, `active`, and `coverages` and `benefits` as repeatable components.
  - **No `currency` on Plan, on purpose:** the user story lists currency as a plan attribute, but a plan can never be sold in a currency different from its country's. Keeping it only on Country removes a source of inconsistency (a Chilean plan in COP) and one field editors could get wrong. The plan's currency is always `plan.country.currency`.

The queries would be:

```
GET /api/countries?fields[0]=name&fields[1]=code&sort=order:asc
    &populate[icon][fields][0]=url&populate[icon][fields][1]=alternativeText

GET /api/form-fields?filters[country][code][$eq]=CO&sort=order:asc
    &populate[validations][populate][validators]=true&populate[options]=true

GET /api/plans?filters[country][code][$eq]=CO&filters[active][$eq]=true&sort=order:asc
    &populate[coverages]=true&populate[benefits]=true
```

Strapi's REST API returns only published documents by default, so "only published" needs no extra filter. Components aren't returned unless populated, so `populate` is explicit (never `populate=*`).

A country is **available** when it is published **and** `active`. The `active` filter is enforced by the Country `find` controller, not sent by the browser, so no client can list inactive countries by omitting it.

Icons are Strapi media served under `/uploads/`, which is proxied like `/api/` (nginx in Docker, the dev-server proxy locally), so the browser still talks only to its own origin.

### Public role permissions

The browser only reads, so the Public role gets exactly:

| Content type | Action | Why |
|--------------|--------|-----|
| Country | `find` | List the selection screen, validate the URL prefix, get currency, locale, legal age and terms. |
| FormField | `find` | Build the step 1 form. |
| Plan | `find` | Show the step 2 plans. |

Nothing else: no `findOne` (the filtered list is enough), no `create`/`update`/`delete`, no tokens. Permissions are granted in code at bootstrap, so a fresh database gets the same setup.

### Why like that?

- **Scalable, supports future countries:** create the Country and its fields and plans, without touching code or schema.
- **Independent publish cycles:** each plan and each field has its own publish cycle.
- **No hardcoded data:** currency, format and terms and conditions have a place in Strapi.
- **Country on/off switch:** a country is offered only when it is published and `active`. Editors can switch it off with `active` without unpublishing its content, or unpublish it. Changes to the terms and conditions also go through draft and publish instead of going live on save.

### Consequences and tradeoffs

- **Duplication:** each common field, like email, exists as many times as there are countries. On the other hand, that also gives a clear separation of data per country.
- **No atomic publication:** everything has to be published one by one, not all at once for a country. Mitigation: Strapi's Releases (only on paid subscriptions).
- **Risk of forgetting to assign new fields to their country:** Strapi 5 can't mark a relation as required, so it doesn't force fields or plans to be assigned to a Country. An unassigned field just never shows up anywhere, silently. Mitigation (recommended): validate in Strapi on save, using Document Service middleware, rejecting a FormField or Plan without a country.
- **Extra code for validations:** Angular must parse Strapi data into code validations, because Strapi only sends data, and Angular should apply strict, typed validations in code, especially for forms and input values.
- **Named validators need code:** rules relative to today (legal age, vehicle year) and algorithms (RUT check digit) can't be expressed with fixed `min`/`max`/`pattern`, so they are named validators with a value, e.g. `{ name: "maxYearsAgo", value: 20 }`. Each name has a function in Angular.

### Limits of configurability

What we found: Strapi only sends data, so every validation rule ends up as code in Angular.

- **No deployment needed:** add, remove, reorder or relabel fields; change required flags, help texts, error messages, options, `min`/`max` and `pattern`; use any named validator Angular already implements; add, edit, sort, highlight or deactivate plans.
- **Needs a developer (and a deployment):** a new kind of rule, e.g. another country's document check digit. That is new behavior, not configuration, so it stays within the requirement "change the form fields and the offered plans from Strapi without requesting a deployment".
- **Known risk:** an editor can type a validator name that Angular doesn't implement. Angular ignores it and logs a warning, so the form keeps working, but that rule is not applied.

## Part 2 — Angular: country from the path prefix

### Decision

How does Angular know which country to render? Let's take the **path prefix** approach for its simplicity, e.g. `/co/quote` and `/cl/quote`. The path must always have the prefix.

- The prefix is the country `code` in lower case (`/co` ↔ `CO`).
- `/` is the **country selection screen** (US-00): it lists the countries returned by `GET /api/countries` in their configured order, with the last country the user was visiting (saved in `sessionStorage`) preselected, if it is still active and available. No country code is hardcoded.
- Any unknown, inactive or unpublished prefix (e.g. `/pe/quote`) **redirects** to `/` with a message explaining that the country is not available.
- **Session per tab:** one `sessionStorage` key per tab holds the active country and its wizard data, so a tab works with one country at a time. Changing the country from the wizard, or opening another country's link in the same tab, asks for confirmation before discarding the data. A link opened in a new tab starts its own session and leaves the other tab untouched.

### Advantages

- **Scalability:** a resolver or guard checks the code against `GET /api/countries`, not against an enum in code.
- **Separation of domains:** a `CountryContext` with a signal can feed each country separately, loading fields, plans and currency, while the tab's `sessionStorage` session keeps the data of the active country.
- **Easy e2e per country:** just open each prefix.
- **Close to a production-ready solution:** in production, subdomains could be better and preferable, and they could be implemented without changing the current approach much.

### Tradeoff

- Changing the country in the middle of the wizard restarts it, after the person confirms that their data will be discarded.
- A mistyped country in the URL sends the user to the selection screen instead of showing an error. Acceptable because the user picks the country again in one click.

## Considered options (not taken)

### i18n in Strapi with a locale per country
- **Good:** built into Strapi, manageable from the admin panel, easy to publish and filter via API by locale.
- **Not taken because:** i18n is not designed for this business case; it is for translating the same content. For example, the Chilean RUT is not a translation of the Colombian cédula.

### Enum field for country
- **Good:** the simplest approach, easy to filter.
- **Not taken because:** it has a big problem for this business case: we can't save unique values per country (currency, locale, legal age, terms), which would force us to hardcode data in Angular. That doesn't make any sense.

### A single document per country
- **Good:** everything in one request (a strength, but also a weakness) and atomic publishing per country.
- **Not taken because:** it brings everything at once even if you only need one field, and it doesn't let editors use the draft/publish pattern per plan, only for the whole country document.

# Implementation Plan: US-00 – Country selection

**Branch**: `001-us-00-country-selection` | **Date**: 2026-11-22 | **Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md) (Approved Gate 1)

**Status**: Approved (Gate 2) — 2026-11-22

**Artifacts**: [research.md](research.md) · [data-model.md](data-model.md) · [contracts/](contracts/) · [quickstart.md](quickstart.md)

## Summary

Add a `Country` collection in Strapi (name, code, icon, order, active; draft & publish), seeded with Colombia, Chile and an inactive Perú, readable by the Public role through a `find` that always returns only active, published countries. In Angular, add the selection screen at `/`, the country-prefixed wizard shell at `/:country/quote` (header with active country and "Cambiar país", step 1 placeholder), a guard that resolves the country from the URL, and a per-tab session that remembers the last country and asks before discarding data.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: TypeScript 6, Angular 22.3 (standalone, zoneless, signals); Strapi 5.63 on Node 22
**Primary Dependencies**: none new — Angular router/HttpClient, native `<dialog>`, Strapi upload plugin (built-in)
**Storage**: SQLite (CMS); `sessionStorage` per tab (browser)
**Testing**: Vitest (unit), Playwright (approved E2E only)
**Target Platform**: Web, mobile-first (≥320 px) to desktop
**Project Type**: Web app — `frontend/` (Angular) + `cms/` (Strapi)
**Performance Goals**: selection screen usable < 2 s on a local stack
**Constraints**: same build for every country; no token in the browser; only `/api` and `/uploads` proxied
**Scale/Scope**: a handful of countries; 2 screens (selection, wizard shell)

## Constitution Check

| Principle | Status |
|-----------|--------|
| KISS / ask before over-engineering | ✅ One session key, native dialog, no state library; Country gets only US-00 fields (R8) |
| No new dependency without approval (§3.2) | ✅ None |
| Feature-first, cohesive files | ✅ `features/country-selection`, `features/quote-wizard`, `core/country`, `core/session` |
| High-value tests only | ✅ See Test plan; no tests for styles or scaffolding |
| BEM | ✅ Per ui-ux-guidelines recipes |
| Breaking API contract (§3.3) | ✅ New endpoint only |
| spec/plan ≤ 150 lines | ✅ |

Re-check after design: ✅ no violations, Complexity Tracking not needed.

## Project Structure

```text
cms/
├── src/api/country/            # schema.json (Country), controller with active filter (R1), routes, services
├── src/seed/                   # countries.ts + assets/co.svg, cl.svg (R2, R7)
└── src/index.ts                # bootstrap: Public find permission, seed, dev admin (R7)
frontend/
├── proxy.conf.json, nginx.conf # + /uploads proxy (R3)
└── src/app/
    ├── core/country/           # country.model.ts, country.mapper.ts, country.service.ts (cached list)
    ├── core/session/           # quote-session.store.ts (sessionStorage, R5)
    ├── shared/ui/confirm-dialog/  # native <dialog> wrapper (R6)
    ├── features/country-selection/   # selection page: list, states, Continue
    └── features/quote-wizard/  # shell (header + outlet), country guard (R4), switch-confirm guard (FR-012), step-1 placeholder
```

# Research — US-00 Country selection

Each entry: **Decision**, **Rationale**, **Alternatives considered**.

## R1. Who enforces "active" — the frontend filter or Strapi?
- **Decision:** Strapi. The `country` controller's `find` always adds `active = true` (published-only is already Strapi's REST default). The frontend never sends the filter.
- **Rationale:** With a client-side filter, anyone calling `/api/countries` without it would see inactive countries, and every client would have to remember it. Enforcing it on the server makes "only published and active" (FR-002) a property of the API, not of a query string.
- **Alternatives:** Filter in the query string (simplest, but not enforced); a separate route policy (more code for the same result).

## R2. Country icon: media field or text?
- **Decision:** Single media field `icon` (images only), served by Strapi under `/uploads/...`. The seed uploads two flag SVGs drawn for this project (`cms/src/seed/assets/`).
- **Rationale:** The business wants to manage "flag or icon" from Strapi (story context). A media field is the editor-friendly way; emoji flags do not render on Windows.
- **Alternatives:** Emoji (broken on Windows), icon key mapped to bundled assets (needs code per new country — violates SC-003).
- **To verify during implementation:** whether the Public role needs `plugin::upload` `find` to populate `icon`. If it does, grant only that action and document why.

## R3. How do media URLs reach the browser without exposing the CMS host?
- **Decision:** Proxy `/uploads/` like `/api/` (nginx in Docker, `proxy.conf.json` in dev). The app uses Strapi's relative `url` as-is.
- **Rationale:** Keeps the "browser talks only to its own origin" rule from ADR 0001 and avoids CORS.
- **Alternatives:** Absolute CMS URLs (leaks host, breaks in Docker), copying icons into the Angular bundle (not CMS-managed).

## R4. How is an unavailable country detected and reported?
- **Decision:** A route guard on `:country` loads the active countries, compares codes case-insensitively, and:
  - available but not lower case → redirect to the canonical lower-case URL;
  - unknown/inactive/unpublished → redirect to `/?unavailable=<code>`, and the selection screen shows the fixed "not available" message.
- **Rationale:** One place decides availability (FR-005, FR-006); the query parameter makes the message state shareable and testable without extra storage.
- **Alternatives:** Dedicated `/not-available` page (story requires the selection screen), router state (lost on reload).

## R5. Session data model per tab
- **Decision:** One `sessionStorage` key, `quote-session`, holding `{ countryCode, data }`. `countryCode` doubles as "last visited country" (FR-011). A tab holds one country at a time (FR-012).
- **Rationale:** `sessionStorage` is already per tab, so the "new tab opens directly, original tab keeps its data" rule (Clarification Q5) needs no code. One key is simpler than one per country and matches "one country per tab".
- **Alternatives:** One key per country (ADR 0001 original) — keeps data for countries the person left, which FR-007/FR-012 now discard anyway.

## R6. Confirmation before discarding data
- **Decision:** A shared confirm dialog on the native `<dialog>` element (`showModal()`), used by the header's "Cambiar país" (FR-007) and by a guard that runs when a tab with data for country A navigates to country B (FR-012).
- **Rationale:** Native modal dialogs give focus trapping, `Esc` to cancel and the right ARIA semantics without a new dependency.
- **Alternatives:** `window.confirm` (unstyled, not brandable), Angular CDK Dialog (new dependency — constitution §3.2).
- **Note:** In US-00 there is no form yet, so `data` is always empty and the dialog never appears in real use; it is verified with unit tests and becomes reachable with US-01.

## R7. Strapi bootstrap: permissions, seed and admin
- **Decision:** `cms/src/index.ts` bootstrap, idempotent:
  1. Grant Public `api::country.country.find` (only).
  2. If no countries exist: seed Colombia (`CO`, order 1), Chile (`CL`, order 2), both active and published with icons, and Perú (`PE`, order 3) published but **inactive**, to demo FR-006.
  3. If no admin exists: create one from `ADMIN_EMAIL` / `ADMIN_PASSWORD` (dev-only defaults in `docker-compose.yml`, documented in the README).
- **Rationale:** `docker compose up` must give a working app and admin with no manual steps (brief), and a fresh database gets identical permissions (strapi-conventions).
- **Alternatives:** Manual setup in the admin panel (not repeatable), Strapi data transfer files (opaque in review).

## R8. Fields beyond this story
- **Decision:** Country gets only what US-00 uses: `name`, `code`, `icon`, `order`, `active`. `currency`, `numberLocale`, `legalAge` and `termsAndConditions` (ADR 0001) are added by the stories that use them.
- **Rationale:** KISS; avoids seeding values no screen shows yet.

# Project Constitution


## 1. Engineering Principles

- **KISS & Pragmatic Reusability:** Keep solutions simple (KISS). Favor clear, specific code over premature abstractions; extract reusable pieces when a pattern repeats (Rule of Three) and genuinely reduces maintenance.
- **Intentional Naming:** Write code for human understanding. Names must express *what* something is or does, not *how*. Start functions with meaningful verbs and use clear nouns for variables.
- **Modular & Cohesive Files:** Avoid large, monolithic files. Split code into focused, single-responsibility components and functions.
- **Feature-First Architecture:** Organize folders and files by domain/feature rather than technical type to keep the repository clean and scalable.
- **Ask Before Over-engineering:** When facing trade-offs in complexity or architecture, pause and ask for alignment before introducing new abstractions or dependencies.
- **High-Value Testing:** Test business logic, validation rules, calculations, API integrations, data transformations, edge cases, and critical user interactions. Never write tests for CSS/styles, static layouts, configuration files, or initial scaffolding.
- **Atomic Conventional Commits:** Make small, atomic, and functional commits following the Conventional Commits specification; each commit must represent a complete, working unit.
- **BEM for CSS:** Follow the BEM (Block, Element, Modifier) methodology for CSS classes and HTML styling hooks.



## 2. Agentic Workflow Rules
- **Low Friction:** Keep `spec.md` and `plan.md` concise (maximum 150 lines each). No corporate fluff.
- **Autonomous Execution:** Once `plan.md` is approved, generate `tasks.md` and execute the implementation straight through without asking for confirmation between tasks.
- **Parallelism:** Use subagents (Agent tool) to execute independent tasks marked with `[P]` in `tasks.md` in parallel.
- **Self-Correction:** Run tests, typecheck, and linter after each block; automatically fix failures before reporting back to the user.

## 3. Human-in-the-Loop Boundaries (When to Stop and Ask)
Stop execution and ask for explicit approval ONLY if:
1. There are business ambiguities in `spec.md` (maximum 5 specific questions).
2. A new external dependency not included in the stack needs to be added.
3. There are breaking changes to public API contracts.
4. A test or build fails after 3 consecutive self-correction attempts.

- **Decision:** `cms/src/index.ts` bootstrap, idempotent:
  1. Grant Public `api::country.country.find` (only).
  2. If no countries exist: seed Colombia (`CO`, order 1), Chile (`CL`, order 2), both active and published with icons, and Perú (`PE`, order 3) published but **inactive**, to demo FR-006.
  3. If no admin exists: create one from `ADMIN_EMAIL` / `ADMIN_PASSWORD` (dev-only defaults in `docker-compose.yml`, documented in the README).
- **Rationale:** `docker compose up` must give a working app and admin with no manual steps (brief), and a fresh database gets identical permissions (strapi-conventions).
- **Alternatives:** Manual setup in the admin panel (not repeatable), Strapi data transfer files (opaque in review).

## R8. Fields beyond this story
- **Decision:** Country gets only what US-00 uses: `name`, `code`, `icon`, `order`, `active`. `currency`, `numberLocale`, `legalAge` and `termsAndConditions` (ADR 0001) are added by the stories that use them.
- **Rationale:** KISS; avoids seeding values no screen shows yet.
# Quickstart — validate US-00

## Prerequisites
Docker Desktop running. Fresh data: `docker compose down -v`.

## Run
```bash
docker compose up --build
```

## Scenarios

| # | Do | Expect | Spec |
|---|----|--------|------|
| 1 | Open http://localhost:4200/ | Colombia, then Chile, with flags; Perú is not listed; "Continuar" disabled | FR-002, FR-003 |
| 2 | Select Chile (keyboard: Tab to the group, arrows, Space), press "Continuar" | `/cl/quote`, header shows Chile + "Cambiar país", step 1 placeholder | FR-004, FR-005, FR-009 |
| 3 | Reload `/` | Chile is preselected, "Continuar" enabled | FR-011 |
| 4 | Open http://localhost:4200/co/quote in a new tab | Colombia wizard directly, no selection screen | FR-005 |
| 5 | Open `/pe/quote` and `/xx/quote` | Selection screen with "not available" message | FR-006 |
| 6 | Open `/CL/quote` | Redirects to `/cl/quote` | Edge Cases |
| 7 | Stop the `cms` container, reload `/` | Error state with "Reintentar"; start `cms`, press it → list appears | FR-010 |
| 8 | Admin: http://localhost:1337/admin with README dev credentials; set Chile `active = false`, reload `/` | Only Colombia listed, no deployment | FR-001, SC-003 |
| 9 | `curl -X POST http://localhost:4200/api/countries` | 403 | Security |

Confirmation dialogs (FR-007, FR-012) have no reachable data in US-00; they are covered by unit tests and checked again in US-01.

## Automated
```bash
npm --prefix frontend run verify
npm --prefix cms run build
npm --prefix frontend run e2e:docker   # approved E2E candidates only
```
# Contract — Countries API (Strapi → Angular)

Source of truth: `cms/src/api/country/content-types/country/schema.json`. Angular model: `frontend/src/app/core/country/country.model.ts`.

## Request (browser, same origin, no token)

```
GET /api/countries
    ?fields[0]=name&fields[1]=code
    &populate[icon][fields][0]=url&populate[icon][fields][1]=alternativeText
    &sort=order:asc
```

- The server **always** returns only published countries with `active = true` (research R1); clients do not send an `active` filter.
- Public role permission: `find` on Country only.

## Response 200

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "documentId": "a1b2c3",
      "name": "Colombia",
      "code": "CO",
      "icon": { "id": 1, "documentId": "x9", "url": "/uploads/co_123.svg", "alternativeText": "Bandera de Colombia" }
    },
    {
      "id": 2,
      "documentId": "d4e5f6",
      "name": "Chile",
      "code": "CL",
      "icon": null
    }
  ],
  "meta": { "pagination": { "page": 1, "pageSize": 25, "pageCount": 1, "total": 2 } }
}
```

- `icon` may be `null`.
- `icon.url` is relative and served through the same-origin `/uploads/` proxy.

## Errors

| Case | Response | App behavior |
|------|----------|--------------|
| CMS down / network error | 5xx or no response | Selection screen error state with "Reintentar" (FR-010) |
| No available countries | 200 with `data: []` | Selection screen empty state (Edge Cases) |
| Write attempt (`POST/PUT/DELETE`) by Public | 403 | Never done by the app |
# Project Constitution


## 1. Engineering Principles

- **KISS & Pragmatic Reusability:** Keep solutions simple (KISS). Favor clear, specific code over premature abstractions; extract reusable pieces when a pattern repeats (Rule of Three) and genuinely reduces maintenance.
- **Intentional Naming:** Write code for human understanding. Names must express *what* something is or does, not *how*. Start functions with meaningful verbs and use clear nouns for variables.
- **Modular & Cohesive Files:** Avoid large, monolithic files. Split code into focused, single-responsibility components and functions.
- **Feature-First Architecture:** Organize folders and files by domain/feature rather than technical type to keep the repository clean and scalable.
- **Ask Before Over-engineering:** When facing trade-offs in complexity or architecture, pause and ask for alignment before introducing new abstractions or dependencies.
- **High-Value Testing:** Test business logic, validation rules, calculations, API integrations, data transformations, edge cases, and critical user interactions. Never write tests for CSS/styles, static layouts, configuration files, or initial scaffolding.
- **Atomic Conventional Commits:** Make small, atomic, and functional commits following the Conventional Commits specification; each commit must represent a complete, working unit.
- **BEM for CSS:** Follow the BEM (Block, Element, Modifier) methodology for CSS classes and HTML styling hooks.



## 2. Agentic Workflow Rules
- **Low Friction:** Keep `spec.md` and `plan.md` concise (maximum 150 lines each). No corporate fluff.
- **Autonomous Execution:** Once `plan.md` is approved, generate `tasks.md` and execute the implementation straight through without asking for confirmation between tasks.
- **Parallelism:** Use subagents (Agent tool) to execute independent tasks marked with `[P]` in `tasks.md` in parallel.
- **Self-Correction:** Run tests, typecheck, and linter after each block; automatically fix failures before reporting back to the user.

## 3. Human-in-the-Loop Boundaries (When to Stop and Ask)
Stop execution and ask for explicit approval ONLY if:
1. There are business ambiguities in `spec.md` (maximum 5 specific questions).
2. A new external dependency not included in the stack needs to be added.
3. There are breaking changes to public API contracts.
4. A test or build fails after 3 consecutive self-correction attempts.

6-# Angular conventions (Angular 22, standalone, zoneless)
7-
8-## Folder layout (feature-first)
9-```
10-frontend/src/app/
11-  core/                 # app-wide singletons: country context, http, error handling
12-  shared/ui/            # reusable presentational components (no business logic)
13-  features/<feature>/   # one folder per feature, e.g. country-selection, quote-form, plan-list, summary
14-    <feature>.page.ts   # routed container component
15-    components/         # presentational components of this feature
16-    data/               # API service + models (*.model.ts) + mappers
17-    state/              # signal-based store for the feature, if needed
18-    *.spec.ts           # tests next to the code they test
19-```
20-
21-## Components
22-- Standalone only, `changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush`, no NgModules.
23-- `input()`, `output()`, `model()` signal APIs; `inject()` instead of constructor injection.
24-- Templates use `@if`, `@for` (always with `track`), `@switch`. No `*ngIf` / `*ngFor`.
25-- Container (page) components talk to services/state; presentational components only receive inputs and emit outputs.
26-- Every async view handles three states: loading, error (with retry), empty.
27-
28-## State
29-- `signal()` / `computed()` for state; `linkedSignal()` / `resource()` / `httpResource()` when they simplify async data.
30-- RxJS only where streams are genuinely needed (e.g. debounced input). Convert at the edge with `toSignal()`.
31-- Wizard state that must survive back-navigation or refresh lives in one store per wizard, persisted to `sessionStorage` through a single persistence helper. Never store tokens there.
32-
33-## HTTP and contracts
34-- Call only relative URLs (`/api/...`). No hosts, no tokens, no `environment.ts` secrets.
35-- Strapi responses are mapped to app models in `data/*.mapper.ts`; components never see raw Strapi shapes.
36-- Models mirror the Strapi schema (source of truth). Any schema change updates the model in the same commit.
37-
38-## Forms
39-- Typed Reactive Forms (`FormGroup<{...}>`, `nonNullable`) or Signal Forms if stable in the installed version — decided once in the plan, then consistent.
40:- Dynamic form: config from CMS → typed field descriptors → validators built by a pure function (`buildValidators(field)`) that is unit-tested per rule.
41-- Error messages come from configuration, shown next to the field, linked with `aria-describedby`.
42-
43-## Accessibility (mandatory)
44-- Every control has a visible `<label for>`; help text and errors linked via `aria-describedby`; invalid fields get `aria-invalid="true"`.
45-- The whole wizard is operable by keyboard; on step change, move focus to the step heading.
46-- Use native elements (`button`, `input`, `select`) before ARIA roles.
47-
48-## Styling
49-- BEM class names: `block__element--modifier`. SCSS per component; design tokens as CSS custom properties in `styles.scss`.
50-- Mobile-first; layouts must work from 320px width.
51-
52-## Testing
53-- Vitest unit tests for: validators, mappers, price rules, stores, critical component interactions.
54-- No tests for styles, static templates or scaffolding.
55-- Name tests after requirements: `describe('US-01 · FR-003 vehicle year range', ...)`.
56-- Prefer testing pure functions; for components use `TestBed` with harness-free DOM queries by role/label.

7-
8-Visual language derived from research of the public car-insurance sites of a reference LatAm insurer operating in Colombia and Chile (2026-11-21). We reuse its **patterns and token values**, never its assets: no third-party logos, fonts or images in the repo. The product is a fictitious insurtech with its own text wordmark.

10-## 1. Design tokens
11-
12-Defined once as CSS custom properties in `frontend/src/styles.scss`. Components use tokens only — no raw hex values.
13-
14-```scss
15-:root {
16-  /* Brand */
17-  --color-brand: #0033a0;          /* navy: header, wordmark, info */
18-  --color-action: #2d6df6;         /* buttons, links, plan names */
19-  --color-action-hover: #26328c;
20-  --color-cta: #e3e829;            /* main CTA background only */
21-  --color-cta-hover: #d7de17;
22-  --color-on-cta: #26328c;         /* text on yellow */
23-  --color-accent: #00aec7;         /* DECORATIVE ONLY, never text (2.7:1) */
24-
25-  /* Text & surfaces */
26-  --color-text: #1c1c24;
27-  --color-text-muted: #53565a;
28-  --color-surface: #ffffff;
29-  --color-surface-alt: #f8f8f8;    /* cards */
30-  --color-surface-highlight: #dfeaff; /* recommended plan, badges */
31-  --color-border: #cdced9;
32-  --color-disabled-bg: #e7e7e7;
33-  --color-disabled-text: #666666;   /* 4.6:1 on disabled-bg (Sura's #878789 was 2.9:1) */

93-- Focus: `--focus-ring`. All text states ≥ 4.5:1.
94-
95:**Form field** — `.form-field`, `__label`, `__control`, `__help`, `__error`, `--invalid`
96-- Label above the control, 14px/500; required marked with `*` and announced (`required` attribute).
97-- Control: min-height 52px, `--radius-sm`, 1px `--color-border`, 16px text (prevents iOS zoom). Focus: `--focus-ring` + border `--color-action`.
98-- Placeholder only as an example (`Ej: ABC123`), never as the label.
99-- Error: icon + text in `--color-error` below the control, `aria-describedby` linked, `aria-invalid="true"` on the control.
100-- Yes/No and short choices: segmented toggle built on native radio inputs (`.segmented`, `__option`, `--checked`).
101-
102-**Form card** — `.form-card`: `--color-surface`, `--radius-md`, `--shadow-card`, padding `--space-6`, max-width 560px, centered. Title 20px/700 `--color-action`.
103-
104-**Plan card** — `.plan-card`, `__badge`, `__name`, `__price`, `__section`, `__item`, `__item--excluded`, `--recommended`, `--selected`
105-- `--color-surface-alt`, `--radius-md`, padding `--space-6`, 1px ring `--color-border`.
106-- Badge: pill, 14px, `--color-surface-highlight` bg, `--color-brand` text, top-right.
107-- `--recommended`: `--color-surface-highlight` background + 1px ring `--color-action` + badge text from CMS.
108-- `--selected`: 2px ring `--color-action` + check icon + "Seleccionado" text (not color alone).
109-- Sections: Coberturas, Beneficios, and optionally "No incluye" with a muted cross icon.
110-- Price: large, formatted in country currency, with period ("/año").
111-- Selectable as a native radio group (`role` comes from `<input type="radio">` inside a `<label>`), one choice only.
112-
113:**Stepper** — `.stepper`, `__step`, `--current`, `--done`: numbered steps with text labels; current step has `aria-current="step"`. On mobile show "Paso 2 de 3" + current label.
114-
115-**Summary block** — `.summary-section` with a title + "Editar" secondary link per section (data, vehicle, plan). Masked document shown as `•••• 5678`.
116-
117-**States**
118-- **Loading:** skeletons shaped like the final content (cards, fields); `aria-busy` on the region.
119-- **Empty** (e.g. no plans): flat illustration or icon, friendly headline, one-line explanation, one action.
120-- **Error** (e.g. payment rejected, CMS down): `--color-error-bg` panel with icon, what happened, what to do, and a retry button. Never lose user data.
121-- **Success** (confirmation): `--color-success` check icon, headline, quote number prominent and copyable.
122-
123-## 4. Accessibility (non-negotiable)
124-
125-- Contrast: text ≥ 4.5:1. `--color-accent` never carries text; white on `--color-action` only at ≥16px bold.
126-- Visible `:focus-visible` on every interactive element (`--focus-ring`). Never `outline: none` without replacement.
127-- Touch targets ≥ 48×48px.
128-- Information never by color alone (selected, recommended, error all have text/icon).
129-- On step change, move focus to the step heading; announce async errors with `role="alert"`.
130-- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` (no transitions).
131-
132-## 5. Layout
133-
134-- Mobile-first. Breakpoints are Bootstrap's: sm 576, md 768, lg 992, xl 1200 px. Custom media queries use the same values.
135-- **Layouts use Bootstrap 5.3 grid and utilities** ([ADR 0003](../../../docs/adr/0003-bootstrap-grid-for-layouts.md)) on every screen. Bootstrap is for layout only:
136-  - Page width: every screen's content sits in a `.container`, capped at 1140 px (global override), with Bootstrap's gutters.
137-  - Structure: `.row` / `.col-*` (`.col-12 .col-md-6`, …) for columns that stack on mobile.
138-  - Alignment and spacing: `.d-flex`, `.flex-column`, `.justify-content-*`, `.align-items-*`, `.gap-*`, `m-*` / `p-*`, `.text-center` / `.text-md-start`, `.d-none .d-md-block`.
139-  - Never use Bootstrap colour, typography, border, shadow or component classes (`.btn`, `.card`, `.bg-*`, `.text-primary`, `.fs-*`…). Those come from our tokens and BEM recipes.
140-  - Component SCSS holds component styling only (look, states, internal spacing with `--space-*`), not page layout.
141-- Plan cards: stacked < 768px, 3 columns ≥ 992px (2 columns in between).
142-- Header: navy bar with text wordmark; no navigation beyond the wizard.

---
name: strapi-conventions
description: Project conventions for the Strapi 5 CMS in cms/ — schemas in code, country-differentiated content, Public role permissions, seed procedure and API contract rules. Load before writing or reviewing CMS code.
---

# Strapi conventions (Strapi 5, TypeScript, SQLite)

## Content types live in code
- Every content type and component is defined as schema files under `cms/src/api/<name>/content-types/<name>/schema.json` and `cms/src/components/<category>/<name>.json`.
- Never rely on changes made only through the admin Content-Type Builder: they are not reviewable. If one is made in dev, commit the generated files.
- Use `draftAndPublish: true` for business-managed content so only published entries reach the app.
- Field names in camelCase; descriptive names (`basePrice`, not `price1`).

## Country differentiation
- The strategy is defined in the multi-country ADR in `docs/adr/`. Read it before modelling any content type and follow it exactly. Do not introduce a second mechanism.

## Querying (Strapi 5)
- Server code uses the Document Service API: `strapi.documents('api::x.x').findMany({ filters, populate, status: 'published' })`.
- REST responses in Strapi 5 are flat (no `data.attributes`); entries are identified by `documentId`.
- Populate explicitly what the frontend needs; never `populate=*` in production paths.

## Security and permissions
- The browser only reads. The Public role gets `find` / `findOne` on exactly the content types the wizard reads — nothing else, no `create/update/delete`.
- Permissions are granted in code at bootstrap (`cms/src/index.ts`), so a fresh database is configured identically. List each granted action with a comment saying why.
- No API tokens are created by code. No token of any kind reaches the frontend.
- Never read, print or commit `.env`; document new variables in `.env.example` only.

## Seed data
- Seed runs at bootstrap only when the database is empty, is idempotent, and lives in `cms/src/seed/` (one file per content type, data per country).
- Fictitious data only (no real people, documents or plates).
- Seeded entries are published so the app works right after `docker compose up`.
- An admin user for local development may be created from `.env` variables; defaults are dev-only and documented in the README.

## Contract
- The schema is the source of truth for the API contract. When a field is added/removed/renamed, report it so the Angular models in `frontend/src/app/features/*/data/` are updated in the same commit.
- Breaking changes to an existing contract require human approval (constitution §3.3).

## Verification
- `npm --prefix cms run build` must pass before reporting.

# Research — US-01 Policyholder and vehicle data form

Each entry gives the **Decision**, the **Rationale** and the **Alternatives considered**.

## R1. FormField schema: section only, or step and section?
- **Decision:** `section` is an enumeration (`policyholder`, `vehicle`), and there is no `step` attribute. Every FormField belongs to step 1.
- **Rationale:** Only step 1 is a configurable form. Step 2 (plans) and step 3 (summary) have fixed layouts, so `step` would always hold the same value (YAGNI). The order of the sections is fixed in code (policyholder first, then vehicle; FR-002), and fields are sorted by `order` within each section.
- **Alternatives:** `step` + `section` as in ADR 0001 (a dead attribute); free-text section names (typos would create stray sections).

## R2. Rejecting a field with no country, or a duplicate key, on save
- **Decision:** A Document Service middleware, registered in `register()`, runs on `create`/`update`/`publish` of `api::form-field.form-field`. It rejects the save with a validation error when:
  - the field has no country, or
  - another FormField of the same country already uses the same `key`.
- **Rationale:** Strapi 5 cannot mark a relation as required, and `unique` on `key` would be global rather than per country. The middleware is the mitigation ADR 0001 already recommended. The spec now requires it (Edge Cases).
- **Alternatives:** Lifecycle hooks (deprecated in favour of Document Service middlewares in Strapi 5); a custom admin plugin (over-engineering).

## R3. Reading form fields: query and enforcement
- **Decision:** `GET /api/form-fields?filters[country][code][$eq]=CO&sort[0]=section:asc&sort[1]=order:asc&populate[validations][populate][validators]=true&populate[options]=true`. The `form-field` `find` controller forces `status: 'published'`, as Country does since the US-00 review, so `?status=draft` cannot leak drafts. Public gets only `api::form-field.form-field.find`.
- **Rationale:** One request per country, and nothing extra is populated. The country filter is not a security boundary: every published field is public anyway.
- **Alternatives:** Populating the fields from Country (one request, but it couples the two caches and cannot be sorted by order).

## R4. Legal age
- **Decision:** Country gains `legalAge` (integer, min 0, required, default 18). It is seeded with 18 for CO, CL and PE. Because the country seed runs only on an empty database, a small idempotent step fills `legalAge` on existing countries that lack it. The country request adds `fields[2]=legalAge`.
- **Rationale:** Clarify Q5, which follows ADR 0001.

## R5. Forms API in Angular
- **Decision:** Typed Reactive Forms: a `FormGroup<Record<string, FormControl<string | boolean>>>` built at runtime from the descriptors, with `nonNullable` controls.
- **Rationale:** Stable and well known. Errors are shown on leaving the field or pressing Continuar (FR-005), which is a plain `touched || submitted` check. Signal Forms in Angular 22 would mean adopting a newer API for no gain in this story.
- **Alternatives:** Signal Forms (newer API, team unfamiliar, risk); a hand-written signal form (re-implements validation state).

## R6. Validators: a pure builder and a named-rule registry
- **Decision:** `buildValidators(field, context)` is a pure function that returns `ValidatorFn[]`:
  - `required`, `min`/`max` (numbers), `pattern` (anchored);
  - named rules from a registry: `rut`, `legalAge` (reads `context.legalAge`), `maxYearsAgo` (value 20), `maxYearsAhead` (value 1).
  - An unknown name is skipped with a `console.warn` naming the field and the rule (spec Edge Cases).
  - Each failing rule returns the error key `invalid`, and the UI always shows the field's single configured `errorMessage`.
  - Dates are compared with the person's local "today" (`yyyy-mm-dd` from `<input type="date">`).
- **Rationale:** ADR 0001 "Named validators need code". One function, unit-tested rule by rule (angular-conventions). One message per field matches the story ("the error message configured for it").
- **Alternatives:** One message per rule (needs a schema change, which the story does not ask for).

## R7. RUT check digit
- **Decision:** Normalise the value (remove dots and the hyphen, upper-case K), require 7–8 body digits plus a check character, then compute modulo 11 with weights 2..7 (11 → `0`, 10 → `K`). The seed pattern stays permissive (`^[0-9.]{7,10}-?[0-9kK]$`), and `rut` does the real check.
- **Rationale:** Clarify Q1.

## R8. Session persistence while typing
- **Decision:** `QuoteSessionStore` gains `readStep1()` and `saveStep1(values)`, stored under `data.step1` (`Record<string, string | boolean>`). Saving is wired to `form.valueChanges` (synchronous, so no debounce is needed). `hasData()` becomes "some saved value is non-empty", so an untouched form never triggers the US-00 discard dialog. Keys that no longer exist are ignored when the form is rebuilt.
- **Rationale:** Clarify Q4. One store and one key, as in US-00 R5.

## R9. Routes and step 2 placeholder
- **Decision:** These are children of `/:country/quote`:
  - `''` → `Step1FormPage`.
  - `'plans'` → `Step2PlaceholderPage`, which has a "Volver" link back to `''`.
  - The plans route has a `step1CompleteGuard`. It redirects to step 1 unless the session holds `data.step1Completed === true`. That flag is set by a valid "Continuar" and cleared by any later edit.
- **Rationale:** "No invalid data reaches step 2" (SC-002) has to hold for a typed URL as well, not only for the button.
- **Alternatives:** Re-validating against the CMS config inside the guard (a second request, duplicated logic).

## R10. Unknown field type or select without options
- **Decision:** The mapper drops fields whose `type` is not in the enum (with `console.warn`). A select with no options is rendered disabled with its help text, and its `required` validator still applies (spec Edge Cases). `checkbox` is supported, though the seed has none.

## R2. Rejecting a field with no country, or a duplicate key, on save
- **Decision:** A Document Service middleware, registered in `register()`, runs on `create`/`update`/`publish` of `api::form-field.form-field`. It rejects the save with a validation error when:

- **Rationale:** Clarify Q5, which follows ADR 0001.

- **Decision:** Typed Reactive Forms: a `FormGroup<Record<string, FormControl<string | boolean>>>` built at runtime from the descriptors, with `nonNullable` controls.
- **Rationale:** Stable and well known. Errors are shown on leaving the field or pressing Continuar (FR-005), which is a plain `touched || submitted` check. Signal Forms in Angular 22 would mean adopting a newer API for no gain in this story.
- **Alternatives:** Signal Forms (newer API, team unfamiliar, risk); a hand-written signal form (re-implements validation state).

| `name` | string | required. One of `rut`, `legalAge`, `maxYearsAgo`, `maxYearsAhead` (R6). An unknown name is skipped |
| `value` | integer | optional, e.g. 20 for `maxYearsAgo` |

### Component `form.option`
| Field | Type | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| `label` | string | required, shown to the person |
| `value` | string | required, stored in the session |

Options keep their order in the component list.

## Quote session (changed, `sessionStorage` key `quote-session`)

```text
{ countryCode: "co", data: { step1?: Record<key, string | boolean>, step1Completed?: boolean } }
```
- `step1` is saved on every change (R8). `hasData()` is true only if some value is non-empty.
- `step1Completed` is set by a valid "Continuar" and cleared on any edit (R9).
- Changing country discards `data` (US-00 FR-007/FR-012, unchanged).

## Seed (FR-013): all fields required and published

| # | CO key · label · type | CL key · label · type | Rules |
|---|----------------------|----------------------|-------|
| 1 | `documentType` · Tipo de documento · select (CC, CE) | `rut` · RUT · text | CL: pattern + `rut` |
| 2 | `documentNumber` · Número de documento · text | — | pattern `^[0-9]{6,10}$` |
| 3 | `fullName` · Nombre completo · text | same | pattern: letters and spaces, 3–80 |
| 4 | `birthDate` · Fecha de nacimiento · date | same | `legalAge` |
| 5 | `email` · Correo electrónico · text | same | email pattern |
| 6 | `mobilePhone` · Celular · text | same | CO `^3[0-9]{9}$` · CL `^9[0-9]{8}$` |
| 7 | `city` · Ciudad · select | `region` · Región · select | 5 fictitious-use options each |
| 8 | `plate` · Placa · text | `plate` · Patente · text | CO `^[A-Za-z]{3}[0-9]{3}$` · CL `^([A-Za-z]{4}[0-9]{2}\|[A-Za-z]{2}[0-9]{4})$` |
| 9 | `vehicleMake` · Marca · select | same | 6 common makes |
| 10 | `vehicleYear` · Año del vehículo · number | same | `maxYearsAgo` 20, `maxYearsAhead` 1 |

Rows 1–7 are in the `policyholder` section and rows 8–10 in `vehicle`. Colombia has 10 fields and Chile 9. A field can be in both countries with the same key, because keys only need to be unique within a country.

# Contract — Form fields API (Strapi → Angular)

The source of truth is `cms/src/api/form-field/content-types/form-field/schema.json` together with `cms/src/components/form/*.json`. The Angular models are in `frontend/src/app/features/quote-form/data/form-field.model.ts`.

## Request (browser, same origin, no token)

```
GET /api/form-fields
    ?filters[country][code][$eq]=CO
    &sort[0]=section:asc&sort[1]=order:asc
    &populate[validations][populate][validators]=true
    &populate[options]=true
    &pagination[pageSize]=100
```

- The server always returns only published fields. The `find` controller forces `status: 'published'` (research R3).
- Permission: Public role gets `find` on FormField only.

## Response 200 (excerpt)

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": 11, "documentId": "f1", "key": "birthDate", "label": "Fecha de nacimiento",
      "type": "date", "required": true, "helpText": "Debes ser mayor de edad.",
      "placeholder": null, "errorMessage": "Debes tener al menos 18 años.",
      "order": 4, "section": "policyholder",
      "validations": { "id": 3, "min": null, "max": null, "pattern": null,
        "validators": [{ "id": 1, "name": "legalAge", "value": null }] },
      "options": []
    },
    {
      "id": 17, "documentId": "f7", "key": "vehicleMake", "label": "Marca",
      "type": "select", "required": true, "helpText": null, "placeholder": null,
      "errorMessage": "Elige la marca.", "order": 3, "section": "vehicle",
      "validations": null,
      "options": [{ "id": 1, "label": "Chevrolet", "value": "chevrolet" }]
    }
  ],
  "meta": { "pagination": { "page": 1, "pageSize": 100, "pageCount": 1, "total": 10 } }
}
```

- `validations` may be `null`, and `options` may be empty.
- The sort puts `policyholder` before `vehicle`, which happens to be alphabetical. The frontend still groups fields by section explicitly and does not rely on the sort.

## Countries API change (additive, not breaking)

`GET /api/countries` adds `fields[2]=legalAge`, and each country gains `"legalAge": 18`.

## Errors

| Case | Response | App behaviour |
|------|----------|---------------|
| CMS down / network error | 5xx or no response | Step 1 error state with "Reintentar" (FR-010) |
| No fields for the country | 200, `data: []` | Step 1 empty state, with no "Continuar" (Edge Cases) |
| Editor saves a field with no country, or with a duplicate key | 400 ValidationError in the admin | Never reached by the app (R2) |
| Write attempt by Public | 403 | Never done by the app |
