# Imagine — Visual Creation Suite ## Modules Call read_me again with the modules parameter to load detailed guidance: - `diagram` — SVG flowcharts, structural diagrams, illustrative diagrams - `mockup` — UI mockups, forms, cards, dashboards - `interactive` — interactive explainers with controls - `chart` — charts, data analysis, geographic maps (Chart.js, D3 choropleth) - `art` — illustration and generative art Pick the closest fit. The module includes all relevant design guidance. **Complexity budget — hard limits:** - Box subtitles: ≤5 words. Detail goes in click-through (`sendPrompt`) or the prose below — not the box. - Colors: ≤2 ramps per diagram. If colors encode meaning (states, tiers), add a 1-line legend. Otherwise use one neutral ramp. - Horizontal tier: ≤4 boxes at full width (~140px each). 5+ boxes → shrink to ≤110px OR wrap to 2 rows OR split into overview + detail diagrams. If you catch yourself writing "click to learn more" in prose, the diagram itself must ACTUALLY be sparse. Don't promise brevity then front-load everything. **Accessibility:** For HTML widgets, begin with a visually-hidden `

` containing a one-sentence summary of the visualization for screen-reader users. (SVG widgets use `role="img"` with `` and `<desc>` instead — see SVG setup.) You create rich visual content — SVG diagrams/illustrations and HTML interactive widgets — that renders inline in conversation. The best output feels like a natural extension of the chat. ## Core Design System These rules apply to ALL use cases. ### Philosophy - **Seamless**: Users shouldn't notice where claude.ai ends and your widget begins. - **Flat**: No gradients, mesh backgrounds, noise textures, or decorative effects. Clean flat surfaces. - **Compact**: Show the essential inline. Explain the rest in text. - **Text goes in your response, visuals go in the tool** — All explanatory text, descriptions, introductions, and summaries must be written as normal response text OUTSIDE the tool call. The tool output should contain ONLY the visual element (diagram, chart, interactive widget). Never put paragraphs of explanation, section headings, or descriptive prose inside the HTML/SVG. If the user asks "explain X", write the explanation in your response and use the tool only for the visual that accompanies it. ### Streaming Output streams token-by-token. Structure code so useful content appears early. - **HTML**: `<style>` (short) → content HTML → `<script>` last. - **SVG**: `<defs>` (markers) → visual elements immediately. - Prefer inline `style="..."` over `<style>` blocks — inputs/controls must look correct mid-stream. - Keep `<style>` under ~15 lines. Interactive widgets with inputs and sliders need more style rules — that's fine, but don't bloat with decorative CSS. - Gradients, shadows, and blur flash during streaming DOM diffs. Use solid flat fills instead. ### Rules - No `<!-- comments -->` or `/* comments */` (waste tokens, break streaming) - No font-size below 11px - No emoji. Icons = Tabler **outline** webfont (5800+, already loaded): `<i class="ti ti-home"></i>`. Outline only — never use `-filled` suffixes (`ti-heart-filled` etc. are not loaded and will render blank). Inherits color + font-size from parent. Decorative icons get `aria-hidden="true"`; icon-only buttons get `aria-label`. Common: ti-home ti-settings ti-user ti-search ti-x ti-check ti-plus ti-trash ti-edit ti-download ti-upload ti-file ti-folder ti-chart-bar ti-calendar ti-clock ti-arrow-right ti-arrow-left ti-chevron-down ti-external-link ti-copy ti-refresh ti-player-play ti-player-pause ti-heart ti-star ti-bell ti-mail ti-lock ti-eye ti-menu-2. Don't hand-draw icon SVG paths. - No gradients, drop shadows, blur, glow, or neon effects - No dark/colored backgrounds on outer containers (transparent only — host provides the bg) - **Typography**: The default font is the person's Interface font, usually Anthropic Sans. For the rare editorial/blockquote moment, use `font-family: var(--font-voice)`. - **Headings**: h1 = 22px, h2 = 18px, h3 = 16px — all `font-weight: 500`. Heading color is pre-set to `var(--text-primary)` — don't override it. Body text = 16px, weight 400, `line-height: 1.7`. **Two weights only: 400 regular, 500 bold.** Never use 600 or 700 — they look heavy against the host UI. - **Sentence case** always. Never Title Case, never ALL CAPS. This applies everywhere including SVG text labels and diagram headings. - **No mid-sentence bolding**, including in your response text around the tool call. Entity names, class names, function names go in `code style` not **bold**. Bold is for headings and labels only. - The widget container is `display: block; width: 100%`. Your HTML fills it naturally — no wrapper div needed. Just start with your content directly. If you want vertical breathing room, add `padding: 1rem 0` on your first element. - Never use `position: fixed` — the iframe viewport sizes itself to your in-flow content height, so fixed-positioned elements (modals, overlays, tooltips) collapse it to `min-height: 100px`. For modal/overlay mockups: wrap everything in a normal-flow `<div style="min-height: 400px; background: rgba(0,0,0,0.45); display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;">` and put the modal inside — it's a faux viewport that actually contributes layout height. - **Fullscreen / expand buttons**: there is no fullscreen. Never call any element's `requestFullscreen()`, never call `document.exitFullscreen()`, and never key state on `document.fullscreenElement` (the API is dead inside the widget iframe and `fullscreenElement` stays null forever, so a label or branch keyed on it is permanently stuck), never call display-mode host APIs, and never fake fullscreen by restyling your container to viewport size — all of these produce dead or broken controls on at least one platform. If the user asks for a fullscreen or expand button, implement an expanded-layout toggle instead: a synchronous CSS class flip on in-flow content with explicit px sizes (taller chart, roomier controls), updating the button label in the same handler — no async, no awaits, symmetric enter/exit. Mutate the existing elements' classes and text; never rebuild the control's DOM with innerHTML (replacement silently drops event listeners and leaves a dead button). The host resizes to fit your content automatically. - No DOCTYPE, `<html>`, `<head>`, or `<body>` — just content fragments. - When placing text on a colored background (badges, pills, cards, tags), use the darkest shade from that same color family for the text — never plain black or generic gray. - **Corners**: use `border-radius: var(--radius)` for controls, `12px` for cards. In SVG, `rx="4"` is the default — larger values make pills, use only when you mean a pill. - **No rounded corners on single-sided borders** — if using `border-left` or `border-top` accents, set `border-radius: 0`. Rounded corners only work with full borders on all sides. - **No titles or prose inside the tool output** — see Philosophy above. - **Icon sizing**: Tabler `<i class="ti …">` sizes with `font-size` — 16–20px inline, 24px max decorative. For one-off inline SVG icons, set `width`/`height` explicitly (same limits). - No tabs, carousels, or `display: none` sections during streaming — hidden content streams invisibly. Show all content stacked vertically. (Post-streaming JS-driven steppers are fine — see Illustrative/Interactive sections.) - No nested scrolling — auto-fit height. - **Validate input in interactive widgets.** Any widget that collects user input before acting on it (quiz answers, text boxes, form fields) must check that input in its submit handler: if a required field is empty or invalid, show a clear inline error next to the control (13px `color: var(--text-danger)` text, e.g. "Enter an answer first") and stop — do not advance to the next step, reveal the answer, or otherwise proceed until the input is valid. Clear the error as soon as the user edits the field. - Scripts execute after streaming — load libraries via `<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/...">` (UMD globals), then use the global in a plain `<script>` that follows. Tokens tell you _what_ you can use; the [Rules](../CLAUDE.md#rules) tell you _how_ to apply them. These principles tell you _why_. ## Claude-native cds is designed to be authored _by_ Claude as much as _for_ Claude's products. Its rules are written as a system prompt, component docs are structured for retrieval, and utilities are named so a model can guess them. A design system an LLM can use fluently is one humans can use fluently too. ## Clay is Claude's color `brand` (clay) is reserved for what Claude does — send, generate, the spark mark. A user's main action takes the neutral `primary` fill; `accent` blue marks links, focus, and selection; everything else stays gray. Holding clay back to a single role is what lets it carry meaning instead of becoming wallpaper. ## Serif is Claude's voice Claude's responses render in serif; the surrounding chrome stays sans. Typography signals who's speaking before a word is read. cds ships `--font-voice` (the `font-voice` utility) for response surfaces. ## Built to be composed, not overridden `className` places a component and tunes its behavior; props, slots, and compound parts (`.Root`, `.Item`, `.Trigger`) shape how it looks; tokens are public for building what's missing. Compose _with_ the system — wrap it, arrange it, fill its slots — rather than restyling it from outside or forking it. When props and parts can't reach what you need, the fix goes into cds (see the [`className` rule](../CLAUDE.md#classname-rule)), not around it. ## Restraint over options One primary action per view, at most two floating layers, t-shirt sizes instead of 0–12 scales. Fewer decisions at the call site means fewer ways for two screens to drift apart — consistency comes from removing knobs, not policing them. ## CDS tokens Every visual decision in `@ant/cds` resolves to a `--*` CSS custom property. The TypeScript source of truth lives under `packages/cds/tokens/`; `bun run --cwd packages/cds gen:tokens` emits the shipped CSS at [`src/generated/tokens.css`](../src/generated/tokens.css). Tokens are layered so that a single edit at the bottom (a hex value) propagates through ramps, roles, and purposes without touching component code. ## The layer model ``` 1. Each carries `text`, `bg` and `border`; `added`, `removed` and `modified` also carry `fill`, a solid for bars and marks. Values are hues matching the palette claude.ai's diff UI was built on (not CDS ramp stops), so adopting them there is a pure rename; in light, the `added` and `modified` fills are darker than their text colors. ### Background vs. fill Both are backgrounds; the split is saturation, and therefore which foreground token pairs on top. `bg-{role}` is the pale tint (hue-100 light / hue-800 dark) for passive status surfaces — Banner, chip; Badge paints its translucent twin `bg-tint-{hue}`. Light enough that `text-{role}` (hue-600) reads against it: a danger banner is `bg-danger` + `text-danger`. `fill-{role}` is the saturated solid (hue-450) for interactive controls — button, checkbox, toggle. Too dark for `text-{role}`, so it pairs with `on-{role}` (gray-0 / gray-900) instead; the 450 stop is chosen for WCAG contrast against `on-*`. | | Background | Foreground | Example | | ----- | when the hue is ambient context behind body text; `fill-*` when the hue _is_ the control surface. ### Purpose tokens | Token | Value (light) | Use case | | ---------------------------- | sheet | | `--shadow-popover` | `0 8px 24px /12%, 0 2px 6px /8%` | Menu, dropdown popups | | `--surface-popover` | `surface-3` | Named alias | | `--surface-panel` | `surface-2` | Named alias | `--shadow-sm/md/lg` are two-layer composites (contact + diffused drop) driven by `--shadow-color`, which deepens to `black/24%` in dark mode. `--shadow-popover` is a two-layer literal tuned for floating menus, with its own darker value in dark mode. --- ## CDS content How to write the words that go inside cds components. Tokens decide how the UI _looks_; this decides how it _sounds_. The voice is **intelligent, warm, unvarnished, and collaborative** — your smartest friend explaining something in plain terms. Friendly lives in the copy, not in extra chrome. ## Mechanics - **Sentence case everywhere.** Buttons, headings, tabs, labels, menu items. "Save changes", not "Save Changes". Title Case is for proper nouns only (Claude, Opus, Anthropic Console). - **No terminal punctuation on labels and headings.** Helper text, descriptions, and empty-state body copy _do_ end with a period. - **Use contractions.** "Can't", "you'll", "it's". Conversational, not stiff. - **Active voice, verb first.** "Delete project", not "Project deletion". - **Ellipsis = in progress only.** "Claude is thinking…". Not for trailing off, not for menu suffixes. - **No ampersands.** Spell out "and". - **Serial comma.** "Chats, projects, and artifacts." ## Pronouns UI speaks as the product, not as Claude and not as the user. | Context | Use | Example | | ---------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | | User's things | **your** | "Your projects" — never "My projects" | | Confirmations | none / past tense | "Saved", "Got it" — never "I saved it" | | Errors | **you / your** | "Your session expired" — never "I couldn't…" | | Claude (in chat) | **I** | Reserved for the chat surface; system UI never says "I" | ## Words to avoid | Skip | Why | Instead | | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------- | | "successfully" | The toast itself says it worked | "File uploaded" | | "please" | UI isn't asking a favor | "Enter a name" | | "Click here" / "Tap to…" | Link text should name the destination | "Read the docs" | | "!" on system copy | Reads as shouty | "Settings saved" | | "leverage", "seamless", "unlock", "empower" | Corporate filler | Say what it does | | "simply", "just", "easy" | Presumes — and condescends | Cut it | ## Patterns **Buttons / CTAs** — verb first, 1–3 words, sentence case, no punctuation. "Create project", "Upgrade to Pro". Not "OK", "Submit", or "Click to continue". **Errors** — say what happened, then what to do. Keep it short, with no "Error:" prefix and no first person. "That name's already taken. Try another." Never surface raw exception strings. **Empty states** — an invitation, not an apology. Headline names the space ("Start your first project"), one-line body explains it, CTA is a verb ("Create project"). Skip "Nothing here yet." **Placeholders** — a real example of valid input ("name@company.com", "Summarize this document"). No "e.g." prefix, don't repeat the field label. **Links** — describe where they go ("View pricing"). A bare "Learn more" is fine when the sentence before it names the topic. Keep them at the end of the sentence; punctuation sits outside the link. ## Do / Don't | Do | Don't | | --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | | "File uploaded" | "Your file was uploaded successfully!" | | "Enter a workspace name" | "Please enter a workspace name." | | "Couldn't connect to Slack. Try again." | "Error: I was unable to connect." | | "Your projects" | "My projects" | | "Create project" | "Click Here To Get Started" | | "Connect Slack" | "Add the Slack Connector" | End the text before each show_widget call with one short sentence that says that the drawing follows. Do not overthink. Try to keep thinking below 500 tokens. If the visual is complex and requires more reasoning effort, consider creating an artifact instead.

# Implementation Plan: US-01 – Policyholder and vehicle data form

**Branch**: `002-us-01-policyholder-vehicle-form` | **Date**: 2026-11-22 | **Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md) (Approved Gate 1)

**Status**: Draft

**Artifacts**: [research.md](research.md) · [data-model.md](data-model.md) · [contracts/](contracts/) · [quickstart.md](quickstart.md) · [ADR 0004](../../docs/adr/0004-dynamic-form-from-cms.md)

## Summary

**Strapi.** Add a `FormField` collection (draft & publish) with three components: validations, named validators and options.
- A Document Service middleware rejects a field with no country, or with a key already used in its country.
- Country gains `legalAge`.
- The seed adds 10 fictitious fields for Colombia and 9 for Chile, and Public gets `find` on FormField.

**Angular.** Replace the step 1 placeholder with a form built at runtime from those fields.
- The fields come in two sections, each with its configured labels, help texts, options, rules and messages.
- The form is saved to the tab's session as the person types.
- A valid "Continuar" opens a step 2 placeholder with "Volver"; a guard keeps step 2 closed until step 1 is complete.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: TypeScript 6, Angular 22.3 (standalone, zoneless, signals); Strapi 5.63 on Node 22
**Primary Dependencies**: none new. Angular Reactive Forms (`@angular/forms`, already installed); the Strapi Document Service.
**Storage**: SQLite (CMS); `sessionStorage` key `quote-session` (browser)
**Testing**: Vitest (unit); Playwright only for the E2E candidates approved below
**Target Platform**: web, mobile-first (≥320 px) to desktop
**Project Type**: web app, with `frontend/` and `cms/`
**Performance Goals**: step 1 usable in under 2 s on the local stack; completed in under 2 min (SC-003)
**Constraints**: one build for every country; no token in the browser; only `/api` and `/uploads` are proxied; Bootstrap for layout only (ADR 0003)
**Scale/Scope**: about 10 fields per country; 2 screens (step 1 form, step 2 placeholder)

## Constitution Check

| Principle | Status |
|-----------|--------|
| KISS / ask before over-engineering | ✅ Reactive Forms with no form library; one error message per field; no `step` attribute (R1) |
| No new dependency (§3.2) | ✅ None |
| Feature-first, cohesive files | ✅ New `features/quote-form/` (page, components, data, validators) |
| High-value tests only | ✅ Validators, mapper, store, guard, form page interactions (see Test plan) |
| BEM, tokens only | ✅ `.form-card`, `.form-field` recipes from ui-ux-guidelines |
| Breaking API contract (§3.3) | ✅ Additive only: a new endpoint, and Country gains `legalAge` |
| spec/plan ≤ 150 lines | ✅ |

Re-check after design: ✅ no violations, so Complexity Tracking is not needed.

## Project Structure

```text
cms/src/
├── api/form-field/               # schema.json, controller (published only, R3), routes, services
├── api/country/…/schema.json     # + legalAge (R4)
├── components/form/              # validations.json, validator.json, option.json
├── middlewares/form-field-integrity.ts   # Document Service middleware: country required, key unique per country (R2)
├── seed/form-fields.ts           # CO 10 / CL 9 fields (FR-013), plus a legalAge backfill (R4)
└── index.ts                      # register(): middleware; bootstrap(): + Public form-field.find
frontend/src/app/
├── core/country/                 # model, mapper, service: + legalAge
├── core/session/quote-session.store.ts   # + readStep1/saveStep1/step1Completed; hasData = non-empty values (R8)
├── features/quote-form/
│   ├── data/                     # form-field.model.ts, form-field.mapper.ts, form-field.service.ts
│   ├── validation/               # build-validators.ts, named-rules.ts (rut, legalAge, maxYearsAgo, maxYearsAhead)
│   ├── components/form-field/    # one control per type: label, help, error, aria wiring
│   └── step1-form.page.*         # states, sections, Continuar, focus on first invalid control
└── features/quote-wizard/        # routes: '' → Step1FormPage, 'plans' → Step2PlaceholderPage + step1CompleteGuard (R9)
```

**Structure Decision**: same `frontend/` + `cms/` layout as US-00. The step 1 placeholder is deleted.

## ADR changes

- **New:** [ADR 0004 — Dynamic form built from CMS field descriptors](../../docs/adr/0004-dynamic-form-from-cms.md) (Proposed; Accepted with this Gate 2).
- **ADR 0001 amended** to resolve the spec's conflicts:
  1. FormField has `section` (`policyholder` | `vehicle`) and no `step` (R1). It also gains `placeholder`.
  2. Rejecting a FormField without a country moves from *recommended* to *implemented*, together with "key unique per country" (R2).
  3. `legalAge` lives on Country, and the field's `legalAge` rule reads it (clarify Q5).
  4. The FormField `find` returns published entries only, enforced on the server, as for Country (R3).

## Design options — step 1 form (`/:country/quote`)

These sit inside the existing navy header (US-00 option A) and a Bootstrap `.container`. All three use the `.form-field` recipe: label above, 52 px controls, the error below with an icon, and the yellow "Continuar" pill. Interactive mockups were shown at Gate 2.

**Option A — One form card with two sections (recommended).**
- The top shows "Paso 1 de 3 · Tus datos y los de tu carro".
- One centered `.form-card` (`col-12 col-lg-8`) holds the section titles "Tus datos" and "Tu carro".
- Short fields sit in pairs from 768 px (`col-md-6`), and long ones span the full width.
- "Continuar" is at the bottom right (full width on mobile).
- *Pros:* one reading path, quick to scan, scales to more fields.
- *Cons:* a long page on mobile.

**Option B — Two cards side by side.**
- From 992 px, "Tus datos" and "Tu carro" are two cards in `col-lg-6`, and "Continuar" is centered below both.
- On mobile the cards stack.
- *Pros:* shows the two parts of the quote at a glance.
- *Cons:* the policyholder card is much longer than the vehicle card, so the columns look uneven, and keyboard order runs down one card and then up to the next.

**Option C — Form with a side help panel.**
- The form card from A sits in `col-lg-8`, next to a sticky `col-lg-4` panel with the illustration and "¿Por qué te pedimos estos datos?" (short reassurance copy).
- On mobile the panel collapses into a line above the form.
- *Pros:* builds trust and reuses the US-00 illustration style.
- *Cons:* more copy and layout, and the panel is not configurable from the CMS.

**Recommendation:** A. It is the simplest, has the most predictable keyboard order, and works the same on mobile and desktop.

**Step 2 placeholder:** the same card with "Paso 2 de 3 · Elige tu plan", the text "Los planes llegan con US-02." and a secondary "Volver" button. There are no options: it is temporary.

## E2E candidates

| ID | Flow | Justification | Decision |
|----|------|---------------|----------|

# Implementation Plan: US-01 – Policyholder and vehicle data form

**Branch**: `002-us-01-policyholder-vehicle-form` | **Date**: 2026-11-22 | **Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md) (Approved Gate 1)

**Status**: Draft

**Artifacts**: [research.md](research.md) · [data-model.md](data-model.md) · [contracts/](contracts/) · [quickstart.md](quickstart.md) · [ADR 0004](../../docs/adr/0004-dynamic-form-from-cms.md)

## Summary

**Strapi.** Add a `FormField` collection (draft & publish) with three components: validations, named validators and options.
- A Document Service middleware rejects a field with no country, or with a key already used in its country.
- Country gains `legalAge`.
- The seed adds 10 fictitious fields for Colombia and 9 for Chile, and Public gets `find` on FormField.

**Angular.** Replace the step 1 placeholder with a form built at runtime from those fields.
- The fields come in two sections, each with its configured labels, help texts, options, rules and messages.
- The form is saved to the tab's session as the person types.
- A valid "Continuar" opens a step 2 placeholder with "Volver"; a guard keeps step 2 closed until step 1 is complete.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: TypeScript 6, Angular 22.3 (standalone, zoneless, signals); Strapi 5.63 on Node 22
**Primary Dependencies**: none new. Angular Reactive Forms (`@angular/forms`, already installed); the Strapi Document Service.
**Storage**: SQLite (CMS); `sessionStorage` key `quote-session` (browser)
**Testing**: Vitest (unit); Playwright only for the E2E candidates approved below
**Target Platform**: web, mobile-first (≥320 px) to desktop
**Project Type**: web app, with `frontend/` and `cms/`
**Performance Goals**: step 1 usable in under 2 s on the local stack; completed in under 2 min (SC-003)
**Constraints**: one build for every country; no token in the browser; only `/api` and `/uploads` are proxied; Bootstrap for layout only (ADR 0003)
**Scale/Scope**: about 10 fields per country; 2 screens (step 1 form, step 2 placeholder)

## Constitution Check

| Principle | Status |
|-----------|--------|
| KISS / ask before over-engineering | ✅ Reactive Forms with no form library; one error message per field; no `step` attribute (R1) |
| No new dependency (§3.2) | ✅ None |
| Feature-first, cohesive files | ✅ New `features/quote-form/` (page, components, data, validators) |
| High-value tests only | ✅ Validators, mapper, store, guard, form page interactions (see Test plan) |
| BEM, tokens only | ✅ `.form-card`, `.form-field` recipes from ui-ux-guidelines |
| Breaking API contract (§3.3) | ✅ Additive only: a new endpoint, and Country gains `legalAge` |
| spec/plan ≤ 150 lines | ✅ |

Re-check after design: ✅ no violations, so Complexity Tracking is not needed.

## Project Structure

```text
cms/src/
├── api/form-field/               # schema.json, controller (published only, R3), routes, services
├── api/country/…/schema.json     # + legalAge (R4)
├── components/form/              # validations.json, validator.json, option.json
├── middlewares/form-field-integrity.ts   # Document Service middleware: country required, key unique per country (R2)
├── seed/form-fields.ts           # CO 10 / CL 9 fields (FR-013), plus a legalAge backfill (R4)
└── index.ts                      # register(): middleware; bootstrap(): + Public form-field.find
frontend/src/app/
├── core/country/                 # model, mapper, service: + legalAge
├── core/session/quote-session.store.ts   # + readStep1/saveStep1/step1Completed; hasData = non-empty values (R8)
├── features/quote-form/
│   ├── data/                     # form-field.model.ts, form-field.mapper.ts, form-field.service.ts
│   ├── validation/               # build-validators.ts, named-rules.ts (rut, legalAge, maxYearsAgo, maxYearsAhead)
│   ├── components/form-field/    # one control per type: label, help, error, aria wiring
│   └── step1-form.page.*         # states, sections, Continuar, focus on first invalid control
└── features/quote-wizard/        # routes: '' → Step1FormPage, 'plans' → Step2PlaceholderPage + step1CompleteGuard (R9)
```

**Structure Decision**: same `frontend/` + `cms/` layout as US-00. The step 1 placeholder is deleted.

## ADR changes

- **New:** [ADR 0004 — Dynamic form built from CMS field descriptors](../../docs/adr/0004-dynamic-form-from-cms.md) (Proposed; Accepted with this Gate 2).
- **ADR 0001 amended** to resolve the spec's conflicts:
  1. FormField has `section` (`policyholder` | `vehicle`) and no `step` (R1). It also gains `placeholder`.
  2. Rejecting a FormField without a country moves from *recommended* to *implemented*, together with "key unique per country" (R2).
  3. `legalAge` lives on Country, and the field's `legalAge` rule reads it (clarify Q5).
  4. The FormField `find` returns published entries only, enforced on the server, as for Country (R3).

## Design options — step 1 form (`/:country/quote`)

These sit inside the existing navy header (US-00 option A) and a Bootstrap `.container`. All three use the `.form-field` recipe: label above, 52 px controls, the error below with an icon, and the yellow "Continuar" pill. Interactive mockups were shown at Gate 2.

**Option A — One form card with two sections (recommended).**
- The top shows "Paso 1 de 3 · Tus datos y los de tu carro".
- One centered `.form-card` (`col-12 col-lg-8`) holds the section titles "Tus datos" and "Tu carro".
- Short fields sit in pairs from 768 px (`col-md-6`), and long ones span the full width.
- "Continuar" is at the bottom right (full width on mobile).
- *Pros:* one reading path, quick to scan, scales to more fields.
- *Cons:* a long page on mobile.

**Option B — Two cards side by side.**
- From 992 px, "Tus datos" and "Tu carro" are two cards in `col-lg-6`, and "Continuar" is centered below both.
- On mobile the cards stack.
- *Pros:* shows the two parts of the quote at a glance.
- *Cons:* the policyholder card is much longer than the vehicle card, so the columns look uneven, and keyboard order runs down one card and then up to the next.

**Option C — Form with a side help panel.**
- The form card from A sits in `col-lg-8`, next to a sticky `col-lg-4` panel with the illustration and "¿Por qué te pedimos estos datos?" (short reassurance copy).
- On mobile the panel collapses into a line above the form.
- *Pros:* builds trust and reuses the US-00 illustration style.
- *Cons:* more copy and layout, and the panel is not configurable from the CMS.

**Recommendation:** A. It is the simplest, has the most predictable keyboard order, and works the same on mobile and desktop.

**Step 2 placeholder:** the same card with "Paso 2 de 3 · Elige tu plan", the text "Los planes llegan con US-02." and a secondary "Volver" button. There are no options: it is temporary.

## E2E candidates

| ID | Flow | Justification | Decision |
|----|------|---------------|----------|
| E2E-1 | `/co/quote`: the CMS fields render; fill in valid data; "Continuar" → step 2; "Volver" → values kept | The core promise of the story: CMS config, proxy, validation and session together, which only a real stack proves | Pending |
| E2E-2 | `/cl/quote`: invalid RUT and an underage birth date block "Continuar", with the configured messages and focus on the first error | Country-specific rules are the highest-risk logic, and invalid data must never reach plans | Pending |

Not proposed: reloads, the "Cambiar país" dialog, CMS publish/unpublish (unit tests and the quickstart cover them). The full-flow E2E belongs to US-03.

## Test plan (unit, Vitest)

- `named-rules`: `rut` (valid with or without dots, K or k, wrong digit, too short), `legalAge` (day before and on the 18th birthday), `maxYearsAgo`/`maxYearsAhead` (limits) (FR-007, FR-008, FR-014).
- `build-validators`: required, min/max, anchored pattern, an unknown rule skipped with a warning (FR-005, Edge Cases).
- `form-field.mapper`: grouping and sorting, unknown type dropped, null validations and options (FR-002, FR-003).
- `quote-session.store`: save/restore step 1, `hasData` ignores empty values, `step1Completed` cleared on edit (FR-009).
- `step1CompleteGuard`: complete → pass; otherwise → redirect (SC-002).
- Step 1 page:
  - no errors before blur;
  - error after blur, cleared live;
  - "Continuar" shows every error and focuses the first;
  - valid → navigates;
  - loading, empty and error with retry;
  - restored values (FR-005, FR-006, FR-010).
- CMS: middleware rejects a missing country or a duplicate key (a focused unit test of the pure check function).

## Revisions

### 2026-11-22 — Gate 2, round 1 (not approved)
- **Asked:** keep option A (one card), but replace the plain "Paso 1 de 3" + title header; add a smooth load animation for the form; propose a less plain look for the fields.
- **Changed:** a new interactive mockup with three step headers (H1 numbered stepper, H2 progress bar, H3 navy band inside the card), three field styles (F1 floating label, F2 leading icon + valid check, F3 soft filled), and a load animation (skeleton → fields fade up 10 px in a 45 ms stagger, off under `prefers-reduced-motion`). Pending the human's pick.

lines: -# Implementation Plan: US-01 – Policyholder and vehicle data form
-**Strapi.** Add a `FormField` collection (draft & publish) with three components: validations, named validators and options.
-- A Document Service middleware rejects a field with no country, or with a key already used in its country.
-- The seed adds 10 fictitious fields for Colombia and 9 for Chile, and Public gets `find` on FormField.
-**Angular.** Replace the step 1 placeholder with a form built at runtime from those fields.
-- The fields come in two sections, each with its configured labels, help texts, options, rules and messages.
-- The form is saved to the tab's session as the person types.
-- A valid "Continuar" opens a step 2 placeholder with "Volver"; a guard keeps step 2 closed until step 1 is complete.
-**Language/Version**: TypeScript 6, Angular 22.3 (standalone, zoneless, signals); Strapi 5.63 on Node 22
-**Primary Dependencies**: none new. Angular Reactive Forms (`@angular/forms`, already installed); the Strapi Document Service.
-**Testing**: Vitest (unit); Playwright only for the E2E candidates approved below
-**Target Platform**: web, mobile-first (≥320 px) to desktop
-**Performance Goals**: step 1 usable in under 2 s on the local stack; completed in under 2 min (SC-003)
-**Constraints**: one build for every country; no token in the browser; only `/api` and `/uploads` are proxied; Bootstrap for layout only (ADR 0003)
-**Scale/Scope**: about 10 fields per country; 2 screens (step 1 form, step 2 placeholder)
-| KISS / ask before over-engineering | ✅ Reactive Forms with no form library; one error message per field; no `step` attribute (R1) |
-| Feature-first, cohesive files | ✅ New `features/quote-form/` (page, components, data, validators) |
-| High-value tests only | ✅ Validators, mapper, store, guard, form page interactions (see Test plan) |
-| BEM, tokens only | ✅ `.form-card`, `.form-field` recipes from ui-ux-guidelines |
-| Breaking API contract (§3.3) | ✅ Additive only: a new endpoint, and Country gains `legalAge` |
-Re-check after design: ✅ no violations, so Complexity Tracking is not needed.
-├── api/form-field/               # schema.json, controller (published only, R3), routes, services
-├── middlewares/form-field-integrity.ts   # Document Service middleware: country required, key unique per country (R2)
-├── seed/form-fields.ts           # CO 10 / CL 9 fields (FR-013), plus a legalAge backfill (R4)
-└── index.ts                      # register(): middleware; bootstrap(): + Public form-field.find
-│   ├── validation/               # build-validators.ts, named-rules.ts (rut, legalAge, maxYearsAgo, maxYearsAhead)
-│   ├── components/form-field/    # one control per type: label, help, error, aria wiring
-│   └── step1-form.page.*         # states, sections, Continuar, focus on first invalid control
-**Structure Decision**: same `frontend/` + `cms/` layout as US-00. The step 1 placeholder is deleted.
-- **New:** [ADR 0004 — Dynamic form built from CMS field descriptors](../../docs/adr/0004-dynamic-form-from-cms.md) (Proposed; Accepted with this Gate 2).

-  4. The FormField `find` returns published entries only, enforced on the server, as for Country (R3).

-  - Keyboard: ↑/↓, Home/End, Enter/Space to pick, Esc to close, Tab to leave (the WAI-ARIA select-only combobox pattern).
-- **Load animation:** a skeleton first, then the items fade up 14 px one by one (600 ms each, 110 ms apart). It is off under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
-**Step 2 placeholder:** the same card with "Paso 2 de 3 · Elige tu plan", the text "Los planes llegan con US-02." and a secondary "Volver" button. There are no options: it is temporary.

-| E2E-2 | `/cl/quote`: invalid RUT and an underage birth date block "Continuar", with the configured messages and focus on the first error | Country-specific rules are the highest-risk logic, and invalid data must never reach plans | Pending |
-Not proposed: reloads, the "Cambiar país" dialog, CMS publish/unpublish (unit tests and the quickstart cover them). The full-flow E2E belongs to US-03.

-- `named-rules`: `rut` (valid with or without dots, K or k, wrong digit, too short), `legalAge` (day before and on the 18th birthday), `maxYearsAgo`/`maxYearsAhead` (limits) (FR-007, FR-008, FR-014).
-- `build-validators`: required, min/max, anchored pattern, an unknown rule skipped with a warning (FR-005, Edge Cases).
-- `form-field.mapper`: grouping and sorting, unknown type dropped, null validations and options (FR-002, FR-003).
-- `quote-session.store`: save/restore step 1, `hasData` ignores empty values, `step1Completed` cleared on edit (FR-009).

+**Option B — Two cards side by side** (`col-lg-6` each, stacked on mobile). *Pros:* both parts at a glance. *Cons:* uneven columns (7 vs 3 fields); Tab runs down one card, then back up.
+**Option C — Form with a side help panel.**
+- The form card from A sits in `col-lg-8`, next to a sticky `col-lg-4` panel with the illustration and "¿Por qué te pedimos estos datos?" (short reassurance copy).

content.content:
## Summary

**Strapi.** Add a `FormField` collection (draft & publish) with three components: validations, named validators and options.
- A Document Service middleware rejects a field with no country, or with a key already used in its country.
- Country gains `legalAge`.
- The seed adds 10 fictitious fields for Colombia and 9 for Chile, and Public gets `find` on FormField.

**Angular.** Replace the step 1 placeholder with a form built at runtime from those fields.
- The fields come in two sections, each with its configured labels, help texts, options, rules and messages.
- The form is saved to the tab's session as the person types.
- A valid "Continuar" opens a step 2 placeholder with "Volver"; a guard keeps step 2 closed until step 1 is complete.

## Technical Context

**Proposed for Gate 2 (option A, refined with the human):**
- **Step header:** a numbered stepper above the card (Tus datos → Elige tu plan → Resumen).
  - The current and completed circles have a `--color-surface-highlight` fill, a 2 px `--color-action` ring and a `--color-brand` number (a check once completed); upcoming steps are white with a grey ring.
  - The current label is bold `--color-brand`, and the line up to a completed step is `--color-action`. Chosen as S3 at round 3.
  - The current step has `aria-current="step"`. On mobile only the current circle shows, with "Paso 1 de 3 · Tus datos".
- **Card title:** "Cuéntanos de ti y de tu carro" with the subtitle "Te toma menos de 2 minutos." The section titles carry icons.
- **Fields:** a soft fill (`#f3f7ff`, a 12 px top radius, a 2 px bottom line); on focus the line turns action blue and the fill deepens; on error the line turns red.
- **Dropdowns:** custom, never the native list. A button with `role="combobox"` opens a rounded listbox (14 px radius, shadow, a check on the selected option, hover and active tint).
  - Keyboard: ↑/↓, Home/End, Enter/Space to pick, Esc to close, Tab to leave (the WAI-ARIA select-only combobox pattern).
  - No new dependency.
- **Load animation:** a skeleton first, then the items fade up 14 px one by one (600 ms each, 110 ms apart). It is off under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

**Step 2 placeholder:** the same card with "Paso 2 de 3 · Elige tu plan", the text "Los planes llegan con US-02." and a secondary "Volver" button. There are no options: it is temporary.

## E2E candidates

lines: -The same application and the same build must sell car insurance in Colombia and Chile. Each country has its own regulations, identity documents, currency, coverages, terms and copy, and the business team (non-technical) must be able to change form fields and plans from Strapi without a deployment.
-So we need to decide two things:
-1. **Strapi:** how content is differentiated by country.
-2. **Angular:** how the app knows which country to render.
-- Add a new country without touching code or schema.
-- Each piece of content (a field, a plan) can be edited and published on its own.
-- No country data hardcoded in Angular: currency, format, legal age and terms live in Strapi.
-## Part 1 — Strapi: Country as a collection with relations
-Let's take a **Country as collection** approach, and **FormField** and **Plan** as collections too, with a many-to-one relation towards Country. All three use native draft/published.

-- **Country** saves `code`, `name`, `icon` (media), `order`, `active`, `currency`, `numberLocale` (e.g. `es-CO`), `legalAge` and `termsAndConditions`. Each story adds the fields it uses (US-00: `code`, `name`, `icon`, `order`, `active`).

-  - `key` is the stable technical name of the field (e.g. `documentNumber`, `vehicleYear`, `birthDate`). Angular uses it as the form control name, and the summary (masking) and the price rule use it to find values. Labels can't play this role because the business edits them. Unique per country.
-- **Plan** saves `name`, `shortDescription`, `basePrice`, `order`, `recommended`, `active`, and `coverages` and `benefits` as repeatable components.

-  - **No `currency` on Plan, on purpose:** the user story lists currency as a plan attribute, but a plan can never be sold in a currency different from its country's. Keeping it only on Country removes a source of inconsistency (a Chilean plan in COP) and one field editors could get wrong. The plan's currency is always `plan.country.currency`.
-Strapi's REST API returns only published documents by default, so "only published" needs no extra filter. Components aren't returned unless populated, so `populate` is explicit (never `populate=*`).

-A country is **available** when it is published **and** `active`. The `active` filter is enforced by the Country `find` controller, not sent by the browser, so no client can list inactive countries by omitting it.
-Icons are Strapi media served under `/uploads/`, which is proxied like `/api/` (nginx in Docker, the dev-server proxy locally), so the browser still talks only to its own origin.
-The browser only reads, so the Public role gets exactly:
-| Country | `find` | List the selection screen, validate the URL prefix, get currency, locale, legal age and terms. |
-Nothing else: no `findOne` (the filtered list is enough), no `create`/`update`/`delete`, no tokens. Permissions are granted in code at bootstrap, so a fresh database gets the same setup.
-- **Scalable, supports future countries:** create the Country and its fields and plans, without touching code or schema.
-- **Independent publish cycles:** each plan and each field has its own publish cycle.
-- **No hardcoded data:** currency, format and terms and conditions have a place in Strapi.

-- **Country on/off switch:** a country is offered only when it is published and `active`. Editors can switch it off with `active` without unpublishing its content, or unpublish it. Changes to the terms and conditions also go through draft and publish instead of going live on save.
-- **Duplication:** each common field, like email, exists as many times as there are countries. On the other hand, that also gives a clear separation of data per country.
-- **No atomic publication:** everything has to be published one by one, not all at once for a country. Mitigation: Strapi's Releases (only on paid subscriptions).

-- **Risk of forgetting to assign new fields to their country:** Strapi 5 can't mark a relation as required, so it doesn't force fields or plans to be assigned to a Country. An unassigned field just never shows up anywhere, silently. Mitigation (recommended): validate in Strapi on save, using Document Service middleware, rejecting a FormField or Plan without a country.

-- **Extra code for validations:** Angular must parse Strapi data into code validations, because Strapi only sends data, and Angular should apply strict, typed validations in code, especially for forms and input values.

-- **Named validators need code:** rules relative to today (legal age, vehicle year) and algorithms (RUT check digit) can't be expressed with fixed `min`/`max`/`pattern`, so they are named validators with a value, e.g. `{ name: "maxYearsAgo", value: 20 }`. Each name has a function in Angular.
-What we found: Strapi only sends data, so every validation rule ends up as code in Angular.

-- **No deployment needed:** add, remove, reorder or relabel fields; change required flags, help texts, error messages, options, `min`/`max` and `pattern`; use any named validator Angular already implements; add, edit, sort, highlight or deactivate plans.

-- **Needs a developer (and a deployment):** a new kind of rule, e.g. another country's document check digit. That is new behavior, not configuration, so it stays within the requirement "change the form fields and the offered plans from Strapi without requesting a deployment".
-- **Known risk:** an editor can type a validator name that Angular doesn't implement. Angular ignores it and logs a warning, so the form keeps working, but that rule is not applied.
-## Part 2 — Angular: country from the path prefix
-How does Angular know which country to render? Let's take the **path prefix** approach for its simplicity, e.g. `/co/quote` and `/cl/quote`. The path must always have the prefix.
-- The prefix is the country `code` in lower case (`/co` ↔ `CO`).

-- `/` is the **country selection screen** (US-00): it lists the countries returned by `GET /api/countries` in their configured order, with the last country the user was visiting (saved in `sessionStorage`) preselected, if it is still active and available. No country code is hardcoded.
-- Any unknown, inactive or unpublished prefix (e.g. `/pe/quote`) **redirects** to `/` with a message explaining that the country is not available.

-- **Session per tab:** one `sessionStorage` key per tab holds the active country and its wizard data, so a tab works with one country at a time. Changing the country from the wizard, or opening another country's link in the same tab, asks for confirmation before discarding the data. A link opened in a new tab starts its own session and leaves the other tab untouched.
-- **Scalability:** a resolver or guard checks the code against `GET /api/countries`, not against an enum in code.

-- **Separation of domains:** a `CountryContext` with a signal can feed each country separately, loading fields, plans and currency, while the tab's `sessionStorage` session keeps the data of the active country.
-- **Easy e2e per country:** just open each prefix.
-- **Close to a production-ready solution:** in production, subdomains could be better and preferable, and they could be implemented without changing the current approach much.
-- Changing the country in the middle of the wizard restarts it, after the person confirms that their data will be discarded.
-- A mistyped country in the URL sends the user to the selection screen instead of showing an error. Acceptable because the user picks the country again in one click.
-### i18n in Strapi with a locale per country
-- **Good:** built into Strapi, manageable from the admin panel, easy to publish and filter via API by locale.
-- **Not taken because:** i18n is not designed for this business case; it is for translating the same content. For example, the Chilean RUT is not a translation of the Colombian cédula.
-- **Good:** the simplest approach, easy to filter.

-- **Not taken because:** it has a big problem for this business case: we can't save unique values per country (currency, locale, legal age, terms), which would force us to hardcode data in Angular. That doesn't make any sense.
-- **Good:** everything in one request (a strength, but also a weakness) and atomic publishing per country.
-- **Not taken because:** it brings everything at once even if you only need one field, and it doesn't let editors use the draft/publish pattern per plan, only for the whole country document.

+Let's take a **Country as collection** approach, and **FormField** and **Plan** as collections too, with a many-to-one relation towards Country. All three use native draft/published.

+- **Country** saves `code`, `name`, `icon` (media), `order`, `active`, `currency`, `numberLocale` (e.g. `es-CO`), `legalAge` and `termsAndConditions`. Each story adds the fields it uses (US-00: `code`, `name`, `icon`, `order`, `active`).

+- **FormField** saves `key`, `label`, `type`, `required`, `helpText`, `placeholder`, `errorMessage`, `order` and `section` (`policyholder` | `vehicle`; no `step`, because only step 1 is a configurable form), plus two components:

+  - `key` is the stable technical name of the field (e.g. `documentNumber`, `vehicleYear`, `birthDate`). Angular uses it as the form control name, and the summary (masking) and the price rule use it to find values. Labels can't play this role because the business edits them. Unique per country.
+- **Plan** saves `name`, `shortDescription`, `basePrice`, `order`, `recommended`, `active`, and `coverages` and `benefits` as repeatable components.

+  - **No `currency` on Plan, on purpose:** the user story lists currency as a plan attribute, but a plan can never be sold in a currency different from its country's. Keeping it only on Country removes a source of inconsistency (a Chilean plan in COP) and one field editors could get wrong. The plan's currency is always `plan.country.currency`.

+Strapi's REST API returns only published documents by default, but `?status=draft` would override it, so the Country and FormField `find` controllers force `status: 'published'`. Components aren't returned unless populated, so `populate` is explicit (never `populate=*`).
+`legalAge` lives on Country (US-01). The birth-date field enables the named validator `legalAge`, which reads the active country's value, so the age is set once per country.

+A country is **available** when it is published **and** `active`. The `active` filter is enforced by the Country `find` controller, not sent by the browser, so no client can list inactive countries by omitting it.
+Icons are Strapi media served under `/uploads/`, which is proxied like `/api/` (nginx in Docker, the dev-server proxy locally), so the browser still talks only to its own origin.
+The browser only reads, so the Public role gets exactly:
+| Country | `find` | List the selection screen, validate the URL prefix, get currency, locale, legal age and terms. |
+Nothing else: no `findOne` (the filtered list is enough), no `create`/`update`/`delete`, no tokens. Permissions are granted in code at bootstrap, so a fresh database gets the same setup.
+- **Scalable, supports future countries:** create the Country and its fields and plans, without touching code or schema.
+- **Independent publish cycles:** each plan and each field has its own publish cycle.
+- **No hardcoded data:** currency, format and terms and conditions have a place in Strapi.

+- **Country on/off switch:** a country is offered only when it is published and `active`. Editors can switch it off with `active` without unpublishing its content, or unpublish it. Changes to the terms and conditions also go through draft and publish instead of going live on save.
+- **Duplication:** each common field, like email, exists as many times as there are countries. On the other hand, that also gives a clear separation of data per country.
+- **No atomic publication:** everything has to be published one by one, not all at once for a country. Mitigation: Strapi's Releases (only on paid subscriptions).

+- **Risk of forgetting to assign new fields to their country:** Strapi 5 can't mark a relation as required, so it doesn't force fields or plans to be assigned to a Country. An unassigned field just never shows up anywhere, silently. Mitigation (implemented for FormField in US-01): a Document Service middleware rejects, on create, update and publish, a FormField without a country or with a `key` already used in its country. Plan gets the same check in US-02.

+- **Extra code for validations:** Angular must parse Strapi data into code validations, because Strapi only sends data, and Angular should apply strict, typed validations in code, especially for forms and input values.

+- **Named validators need code:** rules relative to today (legal age, vehicle year) and algorithms (RUT check digit) can't be expressed with fixed `min`/`max`/`pattern`, so they are named validators with a value, e.g. `{ name: "maxYearsAgo", value: 20 }`. Each name has a function in Angular.
+What we found: Strapi only sends data, so every validation rule ends up as code in Angular.

+- **No deployment needed:** add, remove, reorder or relabel fields; change required flags, help texts, error messages, options, `min`/`max` and `pattern`; use any named validator Angular already implements; add, edit, sort, highlight or deactivate plans.

+- **Needs a developer (and a deployment):** a new kind of rule, e.g. another country's document check digit. That is new behavior, not configuration, so it stays within the requirement "change the form fields and the offered plans from Strapi without requesting a deployment".
+- **Known risk:** an editor can type a validator name that Angular doesn't implement. Angular ignores it and logs a warning, so the form keeps working, but that rule is not applied.
+## Part 2 — Angular: country from the path prefix
+How does Angular know which country to render? Let's take the **path prefix** approach for its simplicity, e.g. `/co/quote` and `/cl/quote`. The path must always have the prefix.
+- The prefix is the country `code` in lower case (`/co` ↔ `CO`).

+- `/` is the **country selection screen** (US-00): it lists the countries returned by `GET /api/countries` in their configured order, with the last country the user was visiting (saved in `sessionStorage`) preselected, if it is still active and available. No country code is hardcoded.
+- Any unknown, inactive or unpublished prefix (e.g. `/pe/quote`) **redirects** to `/` with a message explaining that the country is not available.

+- **Session per tab:** one `sessionStorage` key per tab holds the active country and its wizard data, so a tab works with one country at a time. Changing the country from the wizard, or opening another country's link in the same tab, asks for confirmation before discarding the data. A link opened in a new tab starts its own session and leaves the other tab untouched.
+- **Scalability:** a resolver or guard checks the code against `GET /api/countries`, not against an enum in code.

+- **Separation of domains:** a `CountryContext` with a signal can feed each country separately, loading fields, plans and currency, while the tab's `sessionStorage` session keeps the data of the active country.
+- **Easy e2e per country:** just open each prefix.
+- **Close to a production-ready solution:** in production, subdomains could be better and preferable, and they could be implemented without changing the current approach much.
+- Changing the country in the middle of the wizard restarts it, after the person confirms that their data will be discarded.
+- A mistyped country in the URL sends the user to the selection screen instead of showing an error. Acceptable because the user picks the country again in one click.
+### i18n in Strapi with a locale per country
+- **Good:** built into Strapi, manageable from the admin panel, easy to publish and filter via API by locale.
+- **Not taken because:** i18n is not designed for this business case; it is for translating the same content. For example, the Chilean RUT is not a translation of the Colombian cédula.
+- **Good:** the simplest approach, easy to filter.

+- **Not taken because:** it has a big problem for this business case: we can't save unique values per country (currency, locale, legal age, terms), which would force us to hardcode data in Angular. That doesn't make any sense.
+- **Good:** everything in one request (a strength, but also a weakness) and atomic publishing per country.
+- **Not taken because:** it brings everything at once even if you only need one field, and it doesn't let editors use the draft/publish pattern per plan, only for the whole country document.

Hey, question, doen't this contradict requirements, right?

'the step 1 form is built from the CMS fields using Angular's reactive forms, and the RUT, legal age and vehicle year rules are implemented in code.'

and requierement, which is truly important: 'The business team wants to add, remove or reorder fields

message.content:
Hey, question, doen't this contradict requirements, right?

'the step 1 form is built from the CMS fields using Angular's reactive forms, and the RUT, legal age and vehicle year rules are implemented in code.'

and requierement, which is truly important: 'The business team wants to add, remove or reorder fields
from Strapi without asking development for changes.'

content.text:
No, it doesn't contradict the requirement. My earlier sentence made it sound like the rules are hardcoded, and they aren't. Only how three kinds of rule are calculated lives in code; whether a field uses them, and their values, live in Strapi.

**What the business changes in Strapi, with no deployment:**
- Add, remove, reorder or relabel fields, and publish or unpublish them.
- Change a field's type, required flag, help text, placeholder and error message, and a select's options.
- Change the `pattern`, `min` and `max` of any field, which covers cédula, placa, patente, phone and email.
- Turn a named rule on or off for any field, and set its value:
  - the vehicle year limits (20 years back, 1 year ahead);
  - the legal age, which is set per country on the Country entry.

So a new Chilean field, another vehicle year limit or a legal age of 21 needs no developer.

**What lives in Angular code** is the calculation behind three named rules:
- **`rut`:** the modulo-11 check digit is a calculation that a regular expression can't express.
- **`legalAge`:** turns a birth date into an age relative to today.
- **`maxYearsAgo` / `maxYearsAhead`:** compare the year with the current year. A fixed `min`/`max` in Strapi would go stale every January.

**The one thing that needs a developer** is a new kind of rule, such as another country's document check digit. That is new behaviour, not a change to the fields, so it's outside "add, remove or reorder fields". [ADR 0001](docs/adr/0001-multi-country-content-strategy.md) ("Limits of configurability") and the spec's Assumptions already state this limit. Even then, an editor who types a rule name the app doesn't know never breaks the form: that rule is skipped, a warning is logged, and the person can still continue.

Quickstart scenario 10 (add and publish a field for Chile, then unpublish it, with no deployment) will check this requirement by hand.

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\Quijote\Documents\insurance-multiregion-app\.claude\skills\autopilot

Read `.specify/memory/constitution.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and the current feature folder in `specs/` (`spec.md` and `plan.md`).

1. Verify that `plan.md` has already been approved by the user (`**Status**: Approved (Gate 2)`). If it does not exist or critical clarifications are missing, stop and ask for them.
2. Generate `tasks.md` following `.specify/templates/tasks-template.md`:
   - Explicitly mark tasks that do not share files and can run in parallel with `[P]`.
   - Tag each task with its owner `[CMS]` or `[FE]` and the requirements it covers (`US-XX`, `FR-XXX`).
   - **Analyze (automatic check):** run the `speckit-analyze` skill on `spec.md`, `plan.md` and `tasks.md`. Save its report to `specs/<feature>/analysis.md` (append a new `## Run N` section per run; the skill itself is read-only). Then:
     - **CRITICAL/HIGH in `tasks.md`** (an FR without tasks, a task without an FR, wrong ordering): fix `tasks.md` yourself and rerun analyze. Max 3 runs, then stop and ask (constitution §3.4).
     - **CRITICAL/HIGH that needs a change in `spec.md` or `plan.md`:** stop and ask the human. Those artifacts are approved at Gates 1 and 2 and must not change without them.
     - **MEDIUM/LOW:** keep them in the report and continue.
     Do not start implementation until the last run has no CRITICAL/HIGH findings.
3. Execute the tasks in `tasks.md` in waves:
   - Spawn subagents in parallel for `[P]` task groups: `cms-developer` for `[CMS]`, `frontend-developer` for `[FE]`.
   - Execute tasks with dependencies sequentially.
   - When `cms-developer` reports a contract change, make sure the matching Angular models are updated in the same wave.

## Project Structure

```text
cms/src/
├── api/form-field/               # schema.json, controller (published only, R3), routes, services
├── api/country/…/schema.json     # + legalAge (R4)
├── components/form/              # validations.json, validator.json, option.json
├── middlewares/form-field-integrity.ts   # Document Service middleware: country required, key unique per country (R2)
├── seed/form-fields.ts           # CO 10 / CL 9 fields (FR-013), plus a legalAge backfill (R4)
└── index.ts                      # register(): middleware; bootstrap(): + Public form-field.find
frontend/src/app/
├── core/country/                 # model, mapper, service: + legalAge
├── core/session/quote-session.store.ts   # + readStep1/saveStep1/step1Completed; hasData = non-empty values (R8)
├── features/quote-form/
│   ├── data/                     # form-field.model.ts, form-field.mapper.ts, form-field.service.ts
│   ├── validation/               # build-validators.ts, named-rules.ts (rut, legalAge, maxYearsAgo, maxYearsAhead)
│   ├── components/form-field/    # one control per type: label, help, error, aria wiring
│   └── step1-form.page.*         # states, sections, Continuar, focus on first invalid control
└── features/quote-wizard/        # routes: '' → Step1FormPage, 'plans' → Step2PlaceholderPage + step1CompleteGuard (R9)
```

**Structure Decision**: same `frontend/` + `cms/` layout as US-00. The step 1 placeholder is deleted.

## ADR changes

- **New:** [ADR 0004 — Dynamic form built from CMS field descriptors](../../docs/adr/0004-dynamic-form-from-cms.md) (Proposed; Accepted with this Gate 2).
- **ADR 0001 amended** to resolve the spec's conflicts:
  1. FormField has `section` (`policyholder` | `vehicle`) and no `step` (R1). It also gains `placeholder`.
  2. Rejecting a FormField without a country moves from *recommended* to *implemented*, together with "key unique per country" (R2).
  3. `legalAge` lives on Country, and the field's `legalAge` rule reads it (clarify Q5). 4. The FormField `find` returns published entries only, enforced on the server (R3).

## Design options — step 1 form (`/:country/quote`)

These sit inside the existing navy header (US-00 option A) and a Bootstrap `.container`. All three use the `.form-field` recipe: label above, 52 px controls, the error below with an icon, and the yellow "Continuar" pill. Interactive mockups were shown at Gate 2.

import type { Core } from '@strapi/strapi';

// Actions the Public role needs, each with the reason it is granted.
const PUBLIC_ACTIONS = [
  // The wizard reads the list of available countries (US-00).
  'api::country.country.find',
];

export async function grantPublicPermissions(strapi: Core.Strapi): Promise<void> {
  const role = await strapi.db.query('plugin::users-permissions.role').findOne({ where: { type: 'public' } });
  if (!role) return;

  for (const action of PUBLIC_ACTIONS) {
    const existing = await strapi.db
      .query('plugin::users-permissions.permission')
      .findOne({ where: { action, role: role.id } });
    if (!existing) {
      await strapi.db.query('plugin::users-permissions.permission').create({ data: { action, role: role.id } });
    }
  }
}

Create `validation.model.ts` with exactly:
```ts
export type FieldType = 'text' | 'number' | 'select' | 'date' | 'checkbox';
export interface NamedRule { name: string; value: number | null; }
export interface FieldRules { type: FieldType; required: boolean; min: number | null; max: number | null; pattern: string | null; validators: NamedRule[]; }
export type FieldValue = string | boolean;
export interface ValidationContext { legalAge: number; today: Date; }
export const INVALID_ERROR = 'invalid';
```
`named-rules.ts`: pure functions + a registry `NAMED_RULES: Record<string, (value: number | null, ctx: ValidationContext) => (raw: string) => boolean>` (true = valid), for:
- `rut`: strip dots, spaces and hyphen, upper-case; body 7–8 digits + check char (0-9/K); modulo 11 with weights 2..7 cycling from the right; 11→'0', 10→'K'. Accept with or without dots, with hyphen or none, k/K.
- `legalAge`: value ignored, uses ctx.legalAge; raw is `yyyy-mm-dd`; compute age against ctx.today in local time (no UTC parsing pitfalls: build dates from components); valid if age >= legalAge; future or invalid date invalid.
- `maxYearsAgo` (value N): integer year >= today.year - N. `maxYearsAhead` (value N): integer year <= today.year + N. Non-integer/text invalid.
`build-validators.ts`: `buildValidators(rules: FieldRules, ctx: ValidationContext, fieldKey: string): ValidatorFn[]` (Angular `ValidatorFn`). Every failing check returns `{ [INVALID_ERROR]: true }`. Empty value: only `required` fails (other rules pass on empty so optional fields stay valid). Required: empty string/whitespace, or `false` for checkbox. min/max for number type (parse number; non-numeric invalid). pattern: anchored whole-value (`^(?:pattern)$`), an invalid regex is skipped with `console.warn` naming the field. Named rules looked up in NAMED_RULES; unknown name skipped with `console.warn(\`[form] Unknown rule "${name}" on field "${fieldKey}" – skipped\`)`. Keep `today` from ctx (do not call new Date() inside rules) so tests are deterministic.

- rut valid: '12.345.678-5', '12345678-5', '7.654.321-6', '765432-16'? NO — only compute valid ones yourself and double-check: include one valid RUT whose check digit is K (find one by computing, e.g. iterate bodies in the test helper is NOT allowed — hardcode a computed one and verify by hand), lower-case k accepted. Invalid: wrong check digit ('12.345.678-9'), letters in body, fewer than 7 body digits, empty → passes rut (required handles empty).
- legalAge (legalAge 18, today fixed e.g. 2026-11-22): turns 18 today valid; turns 18 tomorrow invalid; future date invalid; country at 21 → age 20 invalid, 21 valid.
- maxYearsAgo 20 / maxYearsAhead 1 with today 2026: 2006 valid, 2005 invalid, 2027 valid, 2028 invalid, '20.5' and 'abc' invalid.
- build-validators: required; min/max; anchored pattern rejects partial match (pattern '[0-9]{3}' rejects '1234'); invalid regex skipped with warning (spy console.warn); unknown rule skipped with warning; checkbox required.
Run `npm --prefix frontend run verify` (other agents' in-progress work may cause unrelated failures — report them separately). Report files and test results.

Create `validation.model.ts` with exactly:
```ts
export type FieldType = 'text' | 'number' | 'select' | 'date' | 'checkbox';
export interface NamedRule { name: string; value: number | null; }
export interface FieldRules { type: FieldType; required: boolean; min: number | null; max: number | null; pattern: string | null; validators: NamedRule[]; }
export type FieldValue = string | boolean;
export interface ValidationContext { legalAge: number; today: Date; }
export const INVALID_ERROR = 'invalid';
```
`named-rules.ts`: pure functions + a registry `NAMED_RULES: Record<string, (value: number | null, ctx: ValidationContext) => (raw: string) => boolean>` (true = valid), for:
- `rut`: strip dots, spaces and hyphen, upper-case; body 7–8 digits + check char (0-9/K); modulo 11 with weights 2..7 cycling from the right; 11→'0', 10→'K'. Accept with or without dots, with hyphen or none, k/K.
- `legalAge`: value ignored, uses ctx.legalAge; raw is `yyyy-mm-dd`; compute age against ctx.today in local time (no UTC parsing pitfalls: build dates from components); valid if age >= legalAge; future or invalid date invalid.
- `maxYearsAgo` (value N): integer year >= today.year - N. `maxYearsAhead` (value N): integer year <= today.year + N. Non-integer/text invalid.
`build-validators.ts`: `buildValidators(rules: FieldRules, ctx: ValidationContext, fieldKey: string): ValidatorFn[]` (Angular `ValidatorFn`). Every failing check returns `{ [INVALID_ERROR]: true }`. Empty value: only `required` fails (other rules pass on empty so optional fields stay valid). Required: empty string/whitespace, or `false` for checkbox. min/max for number type (parse number; non-numeric invalid). pattern: anchored whole-value (`^(?:pattern)$`), an invalid regex is skipped with `console.warn` naming the field. Named rules looked up in NAMED_RULES; unknown name skipped with `console.warn(\`[form] Unknown rule "${name}" on field "${fieldKey}" – skipped\`)`. Keep `today` from ctx (do not call new Date() inside rules) so tests are deterministic.

Tests (Vitest, `*.spec.ts` next to code), named `describe('US-01 · FR-014 RUT check digit', ...)` etc., with these tables:
- rut valid: '12.345.678-5', '12345678-5', '7.654.321-6', '765432-16'? NO — only compute valid ones yourself and double-check: include one valid RUT whose check digit is K (find one by computing, e.g. iterate bodies in the test helper is NOT allowed — hardcode a computed one and verify by hand), lower-case k accepted. Invalid: wrong check digit ('12.345.678-9'), letters in body, fewer than 7 body digits, empty → passes rut (required handles empty).
- legalAge (legalAge 18, today fixed e.g. 2026-11-22): turns 18 today valid; turns 18 tomorrow invalid; future date invalid; country at 21 → age 20 invalid, 21 valid.
- maxYearsAgo 20 / maxYearsAhead 1 with today 2026: 2006 valid, 2005 invalid, 2027 valid, 2028 invalid, '20.5' and 'abc' invalid.
- build-validators: required; min/max; anchored pattern rejects partial match (pattern '[0-9]{3}' rejects '1234'); invalid regex skipped with warning (spy console.warn); unknown rule skipped with warning; checkbox required.

```ts
export type FieldType = 'text' | 'number' | 'select' | 'date' | 'checkbox';
export interface NamedRule { name: string; value: number | null; }
export interface FieldRules { type: FieldType; required: boolean; min: number | null; max: number | null; pattern: string | null; validators: NamedRule[]; }
export type FieldValue = string | boolean;
export interface ValidationContext { legalAge: number; today: Date; }
export const INVALID_ERROR = 'invalid';
```
`named-rules.ts`: pure functions + a registry `NAMED_RULES: Record<string, (value: number | null, ctx: ValidationContext) => (raw: string) => boolean>` (true = valid), for:
- `rut`: strip dots, spaces and hyphen, upper-case; body 7–8 digits + check char (0-9/K); modulo 11 with weights 2..7 cycling from the right; 11→'0', 10→'K'. Accept with or without dots, with hyphen or none, k/K.
- `legalAge`: value ignored, uses ctx.legalAge; raw is `yyyy-mm-dd`; compute age against ctx.today in local time (no UTC parsing pitfalls: build dates from components); valid if age >= legalAge; future or invalid date invalid.
- `maxYearsAgo` (value N): integer year >= today.year - N. `maxYearsAhead` (value N): integer year <= today.year + N. Non-integer/text invalid.
`build-validators.ts`: `buildValidators(rules: FieldRules, ctx: ValidationContext, fieldKey: string): ValidatorFn[]` (Angular `ValidatorFn`). Every failing check returns `{ [INVALID_ERROR]: true }`. Empty value: only `required` fails (other rules pass on empty so optional fields stay valid). Required: empty string/whitespace, or `false` for checkbox. min/max for number type (parse number; non-numeric invalid). pattern: anchored whole-value (`^(?:pattern)$`), an invalid regex is skipped with `console.warn` naming the field. Named rules looked up in NAMED_RULES; unknown name skipped with `console.warn(\`[form] Unknown rule "${name}" on field "${fieldKey}" – skipped\`)`. Keep `today` from ctx (do not call new Date() inside rules) so tests are deterministic.

Tests (Vitest, `*.spec.ts` next to code), named `describe('US-01 · FR-014 RUT check digit', ...)` etc., with these tables:
- rut valid: '12.345.678-5', '12345678-5', '7.654.321-6', '765432-16'? NO — only compute valid ones yourself and double-check: include one valid RUT whose check digit is K (find one by computing, e.g. iterate bodies in the test helper is NOT allowed — hardcode a computed one and verify by hand), lower-case k accepted. Invalid: wrong check digit ('12.345.678-9'), letters in body, fewer than 7 body digits, empty → passes rut (required handles empty).
- legalAge (legalAge 18, today fixed e.g. 2026-11-22): turns 18 today valid; turns 18 tomorrow invalid; future date invalid; country at 21 → age 20 invalid, 21 valid.
- maxYearsAgo 20 / maxYearsAhead 1 with today 2026: 2006 valid, 2005 invalid, 2027 valid, 2028 invalid, '20.5' and 'abc' invalid.
- build-validators: required; min/max; anchored pattern rejects partial match (pattern '[0-9]{3}' rejects '1234'); invalid regex skipped with warning (spy console.warn); unknown rule skipped with warning; checkbox required.

+- **E2E candidates:** list only critical flows that deserve an e2e test, each with a one-line justification. The human marks each one **Approved** or **Rejected** at Gate 2. The `e2e-tester` agent runs only for approved candidates.
+- **Design options:** for every client-facing view, 2–3 design options based on the `ui-ux-guidelines` skill, with a recommendation. The human picks one at Gate 2.
+- **ADRs:** every architectural decision gets an ADR in `docs/adr/` (context, alternatives, consequences), linked from `plan.md`.

+- **Revisions:** when the human rejects or corrects the plan at Gate 2, append an entry to a `## Revisions` section at the end of `plan.md`: date, what the human asked to change, and what changed. Never delete entries.

+- Every question to the human (Gate 1 clarify questions, Gate 2 choices, stop conditions) MUST be asked with the interactive question tool (`AskUserQuestion`): one question per call, 2–4 options, the recommended one first with "(Recommended)" in its label, and a self-contained question text (the human may see only the dialog).
+- Never put a question and its options only in prose: in the desktop app, text written before the end-of-turn summary can be collapsed and the human never sees it.
+- After the answer, repeat the question and the chosen answer in plain text so they stay in the session log.
+- The user story ID `US-XX` appears in: spec folder name, spec header, each task line, ADR "Related" field, test names (`describe('US-XX · FR-XXX …')`), and commit footer `Refs: US-XX`.

+- **NEVER** read, print, or commit `cms/.env` or any `.env` file (only read `.env.example` when checking required environment variables).

+- The Strapi schema (`cms/src/api/`) is the source of truth for API contracts; Angular models in `frontend/src/app/features/*/data/` must match it. A schema change updates the models in the same commit.
