ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

Call it silently and proceed directly to the visualization in your response.

modules.description: Which module(s) to load. Pick all that fit.

platform.description: The client platform the widget will render on. Pass 'mobile' when your system prompt indicates a mobile client (narrow ~380px viewport) so SVG viewBox and layout guidance are sized accordingly; otherwise pass 'desktop'. Defaults to 'unknown' (desktop sizing).

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder

tools.name: mcp__visualize__show_widget
tools.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.

IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

# Project Context & Rules

Always read and follow `.specify/memory/constitution.md` before planning, writing code, or running commands.
The full agentic flow (steps, gates, agents) is described in `FLOW.md`.

## Repository Structure
- `cms/`: Headless CMS built with Strapi 5 (TypeScript, SQLite). Content types, APIs, seed, permissions.
- `frontend/`: Angular 22 app (TypeScript, ESLint), Vitest unit tests next to the code, Playwright e2e in `frontend/e2e/`.
- `docs/user-stories/`: Functional user stories pasted verbatim by the human (`US-XX.md`). Never edited by AI.
- `docs/adr/`: Architecture Decision Records (MADR), `NNNN-<slug>.md`.
- `specs/NNN-us-XX-<slug>/`: `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, `analysis.md`, `review.md` per user story (Spec Kit).
- `.claude/agents/`: subagent definitions. `.claude/skills/`: skills.
- `ai-logs/`: exported agent sessions. Never edit.

## Verification Commands
- **Frontend (lint + typecheck + unit tests):** `npm --prefix frontend run verify`
- **Frontend build:** `npm --prefix frontend run build`
- **Frontend e2e (Playwright):** `npm --prefix frontend run e2e`
- **CMS build / typecheck:** `npm --prefix cms run build`
- **CMS unit tests:** `npm --prefix cms test`
- **CMS dev server:** `npm --prefix cms run develop`
- **Full stack:** `docker compose up --build`

## Stack Rules (all agents)
- **Angular:** standalone components only, no NgModules; signals for state; built-in control flow (`@if`, `@for`, `@switch`); typed forms; no `any`. Details: `angular-conventions` skill.
- **Strapi:** schemas defined in code; Public role gets only `find`/`findOne` on what the wizard reads. Details: `strapi-conventions` skill.
- **Security:** no Strapi token of any kind in the frontend; the browser calls only relative `/api/...` URLs (proxied by nginx / `proxy.conf.json`).
- **Layout:** Bootstrap 5.3 grid and utilities only (containers, grid, flex, spacing), never its colour, typography or component classes. Details: `ui-ux-guidelines` skill §5, ADR 0003.
- **Accessibility:** every field has a visible label; the wizard is fully keyboard-operable; works on mobile and desktop.
- **Data:** fictitious data only. No real personal data, documents, plates or credentials anywhere in the repo.

## Plan Phase Additions (Gate 2)
`plan.md` must also contain, when applicable:
- **E2E candidates:** list only critical flows that deserve an e2e test, each with a one-line justification. The human marks each one **Approved** or **Rejected** at Gate 2. The `e2e-tester` agent runs only for approved candidates.
- **Design options:** for every client-facing view, 2–3 design options based on the `ui-ux-guidelines` skill, with a recommendation. The human picks one at Gate 2.
- **ADRs:** every architectural decision gets an ADR in `docs/adr/` (context, alternatives, consequences), linked from `plan.md`.
- **Revisions:** when the human rejects or corrects the plan at Gate 2, append an entry to a `## Revisions` section at the end of `plan.md`: date, what the human asked to change, and what changed. Never delete entries.

## Asking the Human
- Every question to the human (Gate 1 clarify questions, Gate 2 choices, stop conditions) MUST be asked with the interactive question tool (`AskUserQuestion`): one question per call, 2–4 options, the recommended one first with "(Recommended)" in its label, and a self-contained question text (the human may see only the dialog).
- Never put a question and its options only in prose: in the desktop app, text written before the end-of-turn summary can be collapsed and the human never sees it.
- After the answer, repeat the question and the chosen answer in plain text so they stay in the session log.

## Traceability
- The user story ID `US-XX` appears in: spec folder name, spec header, each task line, ADR "Related" field, test names (`describe('US-XX · FR-XXX …')`), and commit footer `Refs: US-XX`.
- Requirements in `spec.md` are numbered `FR-XXX`; tasks and tests reference them.
- Gate approvals are recorded in the artifact header: `**Status**: Approved (Gate 1|2) — <date>`. Gate 3 is recorded as the last line of `review.md`: `Gate 3: Approved — <date>`.
- Human corrections: Gate 1 in `spec.md` › Clarifications, Gate 2 in `plan.md` › Revisions, Gate 3 as new tasks in `tasks.md`.

## Security & Workflow Hygiene
- **NEVER** read, print, or commit `cms/.env` or any `.env` file (only read `.env.example` when checking required environment variables).
- The Strapi schema (`cms/src/api/`) is the source of truth for API contracts; Angular models in `frontend/src/app/features/*/data/` must match it. A schema change updates the models in the same commit.
- Never edit `.specify/templates/`, `.specify/scripts/`, `.claude/skills/speckit-*` or the constitution unless the human explicitly asks.

1. **Primary Request and Intent**

   - **tasks.md:**

<system-reminder>
Result of calling the Read tool:
1	# Feature Specification: US-01 – Policyholder and vehicle data form
2	
3	**Feature Branch**: `002-us-01-policyholder-vehicle-form`
4	
5	**Created**: 2026-11-22
6	
7	**Status**: Approved (Gate 1) — 2026-11-22
8	
9	**Input**: User story [US-01](../../docs/user-stories/US-01.md) (verbatim business story, the source of truth). Builds on [US-00](../001-us-00-country-selection/spec.md), which provides the country selection and the wizard shell with a step 1 placeholder. Architecture: [ADR 0001](../../docs/adr/0001-multi-country-content-strategy.md) (content per country, validations, limits of configurability) and [ADR 0003](../../docs/adr/0003-bootstrap-grid-for-layouts.md) (layout).
10	
11	## Clarifications
12	
13	### Session 2026-11-22
14	
15	- Q: Should the Chilean RUT be checked with its modulo-11 check digit or only by format? → A: Format and check digit. The check is a named rule (`rut`) that the application implements and that is turned on per field; seeded RUT examples are valid.
16	- Q: When does a field show its error message? → A: When the person leaves the field, or when they press "Continuar". Once shown, the error updates as they type and disappears as soon as the value is valid. Untouched fields show no errors.
17	- Q: Which fictitious fields does the seed create? → A: The proposed set: 10 fields for Colombia and 9 for Chile, listed in FR-013.
18	- Q: When are step 1 values saved to the tab's session? → A: As the person types, including incomplete or invalid values, so a reload or "Volver" never loses input. Restored invalid values follow the FR-005 timing.
19	- Q (Gate 3, review R-04): Must the RUT include the hyphen and dots only as thousand separators? → A: No. Any spelling with digits, optional dots and an optional hyphen is accepted; the check digit decides validity.
20	- Q: Where is the legal age configured? → A: On the Country (18 for Colombia and Chile), as ADR 0001 says. The birth-date field turns on the named rule `legalAge`, which reads the active country's value.
21	
22	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
23	
24	### User Story 1 - Fill in my data and my vehicle's data for my country (Priority: P1)
25	
26	A person who chose a country sees step 1 of the wizard with the fields the business configured for that country, in the configured order: their own data first, then their vehicle's. They fill it in and continue to step 2.
27	
28	**Why this priority**: Without the form there is nothing to price; it is the first step of every quote.
29	
30	**Independent Test**: With fields configured for Colombia and Chile, open `/co/quote` and `/cl/quote` and check that each shows only its own fields in order. Fill in valid data and continue to step 2.
31	
32	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
33	
34	1. **Given** fields are configured for Colombia and for Chile, **When** I open the wizard for a country, **Then** I see only that country's published fields, in the configured order, each with its label and help text.
35	2. **Given** a field is a select (for example vehicle make or city), **When** I open it, **Then** I see the options configured for it in the content manager.
36	3. **Given** all required fields are valid, **When** I press "Continuar", **Then** I move to step 2.
37	4. **Given** I use only the keyboard, **When** I fill in the form, **Then** I can reach, fill in and leave every field and press "Continuar".
38	
39	---
40	
41	### User Story 2 - Be told what is wrong before continuing (Priority: P1)
42	
43	When a value does not meet its configured rule, the person sees the configured error message next to the field and cannot continue until it is fixed.
44	
45	**Why this priority**: The quote depends on correct data; invalid data must never reach the plans step.
46	
47	**Independent Test**: Leave a required field empty, enter an underage birth date and a vehicle year older than 20 years; check each message and that "Continuar" does not advance.
48	
49	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
50	
51	1. **Given** I am filling out the form, **When** a field does not meet its configured validation, **Then** I see that field's configured error message next to it, and I cannot move to the next step.
52	2. **Given** I press "Continuar" with invalid or empty required fields, **When** the form is checked, **Then** every invalid field shows its message and focus moves to the first invalid field.
53	3. **Given** the birth date makes me younger than the country's legal age, **When** the field is checked, **Then** I see the configured error message.
54	4. **Given** a vehicle year later than next year or more than 20 years before the current year, **When** the field is checked, **Then** I see the configured error message.
55	
56	---
57	
58	### User Story 3 - Keep my data when I go back (Priority: P2)
59	
60	A person who moved on to step 2 goes back to step 1 and finds everything they typed still there.
61	
62	**Why this priority**: Re-typing data is a common reason to abandon a quote.
63	
64	**Independent Test**: Fill in the form, continue to step 2, go back; all values are still there. Reload the page: they are still there (same tab).
65	
66	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
67	
68	1. **Given** I moved on to step 2, **When** I go back to step 1, **Then** my data is still filled in.
69	2. **Given** I entered data and reload the page in the same tab, **When** step 1 opens, **Then** my data is still filled in.
70	3. **Given** I entered data, **When** I use "Cambiar país" or open another country's link in the same tab, **Then** I am asked to confirm before my data is discarded (US-00 FR-007, FR-012).
71	
72	---
73	
74	### User Story 4 - Change the form without a deployment (Priority: P1)
75	
76	The business team adds, removes, reorders or relabels fields, and changes their options, rules and messages, from the content manager.
77	
78	**Why this priority**: It is the core business promise of the product: the form adapts per country without development work.
79	
80	**Independent Test**: Publish a new field for Chile, reload `/cl/quote`: it appears in its order. Unpublish it: it disappears. No code change, no deployment.
81	
82	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
83	
84	1. **Given** the business team adds a new published field in the content manager, **When** I reload the application, **Then** the new field appears without code changes.
85	2. **Given** a field is unpublished or deleted, **When** I reload, **Then** it no longer appears and is not required.
86	
87	---
88	
89	### Edge Cases
90	
91	- **No fields configured** for the country, or the content service fails: step 1 shows a clear message and a retry action instead of an empty form; "Continuar" is not offered.
92	- **Unknown rule name**: a field references a rule the application does not implement. The field still works, that rule is skipped, and the problem is reported for developers. The person is not blocked.
93	- **Field saved without a country**: the content manager rejects it, so a field can never be silently lost (ADR 0001 mitigation).
94	- **Select without options**: shown as unavailable with its help text; if required, the person cannot continue and sees its error message.
95	- **Saved data for a field that no longer exists** (after a configuration change): it is ignored. Saved data that no longer meets a changed rule is restored as is, and shows its error per FR-005.
96	- **Two fields with the same technical key in one country**: the content manager rejects the second one.
97	- **Dates**: legal age and vehicle year are computed against the current date in the person's time zone.
98	
99	## Requirements *(mandatory)*
100	
101	### Functional Requirements
102	
103	- **FR-001**: The business team MUST be able to configure each form field per country with: label, technical key, type (text, number, select, date, checkbox), required flag, validations, help text, error message, order, section (policyholder or vehicle) and country, and publish or unpublish it, without code changes.
104	- **FR-002**: Step 1 MUST show only the published fields of the active country, grouped by section (policyholder first, then vehicle) and sorted by their configured order.
105	- **FR-003**: Select fields MUST list the options configured for them, in their configured order.
106	- **FR-004**: Each field MUST show its label (always visible), its help text when configured, and a required marker when it is required.
107	- **FR-005**: A field that does not meet its validation (required, minimum and maximum, pattern, or a named rule) MUST show its configured error message next to it, first when the person leaves the field or presses "Continuar". After that, the message updates as they type and disappears once the value is valid. A field the person has not touched shows no error.
108	- **FR-006**: "Continuar" MUST NOT move to step 2 while any field is invalid. Pressing it MUST show every error and move focus to the first invalid field.
109	- **FR-007**: The policyholder MUST be of legal age for the active country. The age is configured once on the country (seed: 18 for both), and the birth-date field enables the named rule `legalAge`, which reads it.
110	- **FR-008**: The vehicle year MUST be no later than next year and no earlier than 20 years before the current year, with the limits set in the field's configuration.
111	- **FR-009**: Every step 1 value MUST be saved in the tab's session as the person types, valid or not, so going back from step 2 or reloading shows it again. Restored values show errors only per FR-005. The US-00 confirmations before discarding data apply.
112	- **FR-010**: Step 1 MUST show loading, empty and error states with a retry action (see Edge Cases).
113	- **FR-011**: The form MUST be fully keyboard-operable, and errors MUST be announced to assistive technology and linked to their field.
114	- **FR-012**: Step 2 MUST exist as a placeholder with a "Volver" action back to step 1, until US-02 replaces it with the plans.
115	- **FR-013**: The seed MUST provide these fictitious fields, all required:
116	  - **Colombia (10):** policyholder: document type (select: Cédula de ciudadanía, Cédula de extranjería), document number, full name, birth date, email, mobile phone, city (select). Vehicle: placa (format ABC123), make (select), year.
117	  - **Chile (9):** policyholder: RUT (rule `rut`), full name, birth date, email, mobile phone, region (select). Vehicle: patente (format BBBB12 or AB1234), make (select), year.
118	
119	- **FR-014**: A field with the named rule `rut` MUST accept a Chilean RUT only when its format is valid (digits with or without dots, with or without a hyphen) and its check digit (0–9 or K, either case) matches the modulo-11 calculation; otherwise its configured error message is shown.
120	
121	### Key Entities

### Section Requirements

- **Mandatory sections**: Must be completed for every feature
- **Optional sections**: Include only when relevant to the feature

### For AI Generation

When creating this spec from a user prompt:

1. **Make informed guesses**: Use context, industry standards, and common patterns to fill gaps
2. **Document assumptions**: Record reasonable defaults in the Assumptions section
3. **Limit clarifications**: Maximum 3 [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers - use only for critical decisions that:
   - Significantly impact feature scope or user experience
   - Have multiple reasonable interpretations with different implications
   - Lack any reasonable default
4. **Prioritize clarifications**: scope > security/privacy > user experience > technical details
5. **Think like a tester**: Every vague requirement should fail the "testable and unambiguous" checklist item
6. **Common areas needing clarification** (only if no reasonable default exists):
   - Feature scope and boundaries (include/exclude specific use cases)
   - User types and permissions (if multiple conflicting interpretations possible)
   - Security/compliance requirements (when legally/financially significant)

**Examples of reasonable defaults** (don't ask about these):

- Data retention: Industry-standard practices for the domain
- Performance targets: Standard web/mobile app expectations unless specified
- Error handling: User-friendly messages with appropriate fallbacks
- Authentication method: Standard session-based or OAuth2 for web apps
- Integration patterns: Use project-appropriate patterns (REST/GraphQL for web services, function calls for libraries, CLI args for tools, etc.)

### Success Criteria Guidelines

Success criteria must be:

1. **Measurable**: Include specific metrics (time, percentage, count, rate)
2. **Technology-agnostic**: No mention of frameworks, languages, databases, or tools
3. **User-focused**: Describe outcomes from user/business perspective, not system internals
4. **Verifiable**: Can be tested/validated without knowing implementation details

**Good examples**:

- "Users can complete checkout in under 3 minutes"
- "System supports 10,000 concurrent users"
- "95% of searches return results in under 1 second"
- "Task completion rate improves by 40%"

**Bad examples** (implementation-focused):

- "API response time is under 200ms" (too technical, use "Users see results instantly")
- "Database can handle 1000 TPS" (implementation detail, use user-facing metric)
- "React components render efficiently" (framework-specific)
- "Redis cache hit rate above 80%" (technology-specific)

- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. The user follows your progress on a task list the app shows under your latest message, not by reading your messages, so keeping it is part of doing the task here. `mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan` is that list, and the only one the app shows under your message: use it in place of Claude Code's own task-list tools (TaskCreate, TaskUpdate, TaskList, TaskGet), and do not search for them. For every request that involves editing files or running more than one command, the very first tool call of the turn — even one that only reads a file — MUST go out in the same message as `mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan` carrying the whole plan; as each step finishes, `{"advance": true}` rides along with the call that starts the next step. That same first message also says, unasked, what the request is to this session — `update_plan`'s `scope`: "first_task" until you have wrapped up a task here; after that every request is either "new_task" or "continuation". "new_task" is unrelated work: a fresh session would do it just as well from the user's words alone, because it builds on nothing done, found or decided in this conversation. Everything else is a "continuation": not only a correction, a follow-up or a question, but also the requests that look separable, such as the next iteration of the work here, or going ahead with what you just investigated or suggested (the user says "ok, do it"). Those depend on what this session already knows, so they stay here even when the work will get its own commit or PR. So does anything a few tool calls settle, whatever it is about. An offer stops the user's work and makes them choose before anything happens, while a wrong "continuation" only makes this session a little longer, so when you are unsure it is a "continuation". You can tell; the app cannot. A "new_task" turn — and any turn where the user names a task and asks you to suggest, split off or make a task or session for it — does not start with the plan: its first message is `mcp__ccd_session__start_session` with `initiation` "offer" and a `title` — nothing else, no prompt or background yet, so the card is up at once. Do not restate the plan as a list in your text. Every turn in which you kept a task list, changed files or ran commands closes with `mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up`, called when this turn's work is done, before any closing message: it fills the next-step box, and without the call the app has nothing to draw. The box holds a two-or-three-sentence recap of what is now true and where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. When this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, it also holds one short question, the decision alone with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give, plus buttons of one to three words that answer it; a turn with nothing pending sends the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Your closing message follows the call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the box's recap never replaces. Never write it before the call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The call's result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR the app watches it and wakes you on CI failures, merge conflicts and review comments, so the box never offers to keep watching, poll or fix CI, in a question or a button. It asks only what the user must do or decide (an approval, a review request, a choice), as one question. Part of wrapping up is deciding, unasked, whether what the user asked for left a real follow-up, and where it runs; most turns leave none. One piece of work that acts on what this session just found stays here while this session has nothing else in flight ("Starting other sessions" says why): make it the box's question, with a button that has you do it here. A piece you left or could not verify is still this task, not a follow-up: finish or check it now, here or in a subagent, or name it in the recap. Any other that is a task of its own, as that section defines one (work that lands apart from this change, something the user set aside earlier, or a self-contained next task better started fresh than from a long history — never work unrelated to the request), you propose with `mcp__ccd_session__start_session` (initiation "own_initiative"; skip if you already did this turn); it shows as a New task card in the transcript, where the user starts it.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

**Do not spawn agents unless the user asks.** Each spawn starts cold and re-derives context you already have — it's the expensive path on this plan. A task with "multiple angles," "thorough," or several parts is not a request to spawn; handle it inline with your own tools. Only use this tool when the user explicitly says to use a subagent, or names one of the available agent types. This does not cover the `web-fetch` agent type where it is listed and you have no WebFetch tool of your own: it stands in for that tool, so calling it to read a page is ordinary tool use.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
