tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SearchPlugins

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. Set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). Use ListPlugins for plugins they already have.

After the card, continue the task. Example: "ship this to staging" and a deploy plugin that is not enabled → contextLabel "For your deploys".

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a plugin would help, when SearchPlugins returned nothing relevant (then continue the task without mentioning the search), or if you already rendered a plugin or skill suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a proposal you made with start_session (initiation "own_initiative" or "offer") that the user has not started.

Call this when it went stale: the work was done here after all (by you or the user), it turned out unnecessary, or you proposed a better-scoped replacement (propose the new one first, then dismiss the old task_id). A card the user answered has already left, "Do it here" included, so it needs no call.

Read the result before you start the task anew or do it here: after "Not withdrawn", do neither.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

At most 100 characters.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

## US-02 – Plan list

Step 2 of the quote wizard: the customer sees the plans configured in Strapi for their country, with a price adjusted to their step 1 data, picks one and continues to the summary.

Story: `docs/user-stories/US-02.md` · Spec: `specs/003-us-02-plan-list/`

### CMS (Strapi 5)
- New `Plan` collection (draft & publish): name, short description, base price, coverages and benefits (repeatable `plan.item`), order, recommended, active, country.

- The save check middleware (`country-integrity`) now also requires a country on plans.
- Seed: 3 plans for CO and CL (one recommended each, one inactive in CO). A safe backfill adds pricing to existing countries without overwriting edits or publishing pending drafts.
- Public role: `find` on plans only. The public API returns published plans only.

### Frontend (Angular 22)
- Plan list page: loading, empty and error states; native radio group with keyboard support; the choice is kept in the quote session.
- Simulated price: `round(basePrice × driverFactor × vehicleFactor)`, shown in local currency per month. The rule is not shown to customers; it is documented in ADR 0005, in the code and in the Strapi field descriptions.
- Plan cards: rows aligned across cards, a prominent "Recomendado" badge, selection with no layout shift; "Continuar" stays disabled until a plan is chosen.
- Layout: 3-column grid on desktop; Swiper slider below 992px, or on any width when there are more than 3 plans (arrows, dots, no loop or autoplay).
- Guards: step 2 re-checks the saved step 1 values; the summary requires a chosen plan. The summary itself is a placeholder until US-03.

### Decisions
- ADR 0005: simulated price rule with age bands per country.
- ADR 0001 amended for US-02.

- Unit: UT-01…UT-10 (approved at Gate 2), plus named regression tests from review and Gate 3. Frontend 188 passing; CMS suite passing.
- E2E (Playwright): E2E-3 (CO choose-plan flow), E2E-4 (CL price adjustment).
- Code review: 7 rounds recorded in `review.md`, all findings resolved or accepted.

### Gates
- Gate 1 (spec), Gate 2 (plan) and Gate 3 (manual test) approved on 2026-11-22.

﻿## US-03 – Summary and payment

### Story

As a person who chose a plan, I want to review a summary of my quote and pay, so that I
become insured.

### Context

Before paying, the person must confirm their data and accept the terms and conditions,
whose text varies by country and is managed by the business team from Strapi. Payment
is simulated for this test.

### Business rules

- The summary shows the policyholder's data, the vehicle's data and the chosen plan

   - Set `SPEC_FILE` to `SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY/spec.md`
   - Persist the resolved path to `.specify/feature.json`:
     ```json
     {
       "feature_directory": "<resolved feature dir>"
     }
     ```
     Write the actual resolved directory path value (for example, `specs/003-user-auth`), not the literal string `SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY`.
     This allows downstream commands (`/speckit-plan`, `/speckit-tasks`, etc.) to locate the feature directory without relying on git branch name conventions.

   **IMPORTANT**:
   - You must only create one feature per `/speckit-specify` invocation
   - The spec directory name and the git branch name are independent — they may be the same but that is the user's choice
   - The spec directory and file are always created by this command, never by the hook

4. Use `TEMPLATE_CONTENT` to understand required sections.

5. **IF EXISTS**: Load `.specify/memory/constitution.md` for project principles and governance constraints.

6. Follow this execution flow:
    1. Parse user description from arguments
       If empty: ERROR "No feature description provided"
    2. Extract key concepts from description
       Identify: actors, actions, data, constraints
    3. For unclear aspects:
       - Make informed guesses based on context and industry standards
       - Only mark with [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: specific question] if:
         - The choice significantly impacts feature scope or user experience
         - Multiple reasonable interpretations exist with different implications

      - [ ] Scope is clearly bounded

      - For each item, determine if it passes or fails
      - Document specific issues found (quote relevant spec sections)

   c. **Handle Validation Results**:

      - **If all items pass**: Mark checklist complete and proceed to the Mandatory Post-Execution Hooks section

      - **If items fail (excluding [NEEDS CLARIFICATION])**:
        1. List the failing items and specific issues
        2. Update the spec to address each issue
        3. Re-run validation until all items pass (max 3 iterations)

        5. Number questions sequentially (Q1, Q2, Q3 - max 3 total)
        6. Present all questions together before waiting for responses
        7. Wait for user to respond with their choices for all questions (e.g., "Q1: A, Q2: Custom - [details], Q3: B")
        8. Update the spec by replacing each [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] marker with the user's selected or provided answer

## Mandatory Post-Execution Hooks

**You MUST complete this section before reporting completion to the user.**

Check if `.specify/extensions.yml` exists in the project root.
- If it does not exist, or no hooks are registered under `hooks.after_specify`, skip to the Completion Report.

- For each executable hook, output the following based on its `optional` flag:
  - **Mandatory hook** (`optional: false`) — **You MUST emit `EXECUTE_COMMAND:` for each mandatory hook**:
    ```
    ## Extension Hooks

    **Automatic Hook**: {extension}
    Executing: `/{command}`
    EXECUTE_COMMAND: {command}
    ```
    After emitting the block above you MUST actually invoke the hook and wait for it to finish before continuing. Run it the same way you would run the command yourself in this agent/session (the invocation may differ from the literal `{command}` id shown above, e.g. a skills-mode agent runs it as `/skill:speckit-...` or `$speckit-...`). Emitting the block alone does not run the hook.
  - **Optional hook** (`optional: true`):
    ```

    **Optional Hook**: {extension}
    Command: `/{command}`
    Description: {description}

    Prompt: {prompt}
    To execute: `/{command}`
    ```

## Completion Report

Report completion to the user with:
- `SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY` — the feature directory path
- `SPEC_FILE` — the spec file path
- Checklist results summary
- Readiness for the next phase (`/speckit-clarify` or `/speckit-plan`)

**NOTE:** Branch creation is handled by the `before_specify` hook (git extension). Spec directory and file creation are always handled by this core command.

## Quick Guidelines

- Focus on **WHAT** users need and **WHY**.
- Avoid HOW to implement (no tech stack, APIs, code structure).
- Written for business stakeholders, not developers.
- DO NOT create any checklists that are embedded in the spec. That will be a separate command.

### Section Requirements

- **Mandatory sections**: Must be completed for every feature
- **Optional sections**: Include only when relevant to the feature
- When a section doesn't apply, remove it entirely (don't leave as "N/A")

### For AI Generation

When creating this spec from a user prompt:

1. **Make informed guesses**: Use context, industry standards, and common patterns to fill gaps
2. **Document assumptions**: Record reasonable defaults in the Assumptions section
3. **Limit clarifications**: Maximum 3 [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers - use only for critical decisions that:
   - Significantly impact feature scope or user experience
   - Have multiple reasonable interpretations with different implications
   - Lack any reasonable default
4. **Prioritize clarifications**: scope > security/privacy > user experience > technical details
5. **Think like a tester**: Every vague requirement should fail the "testable and unambiguous" checklist item
6. **Common areas needing clarification** (only if no reasonable default exists):
   - Feature scope and boundaries (include/exclude specific use cases)
   - User types and permissions (if multiple conflicting interpretations possible)
   - Security/compliance requirements (when legally/financially significant)

**Examples of reasonable defaults** (don't ask about these):

- Data retention: Industry-standard practices for the domain
- Performance targets: Standard web/mobile app expectations unless specified
- Error handling: User-friendly messages with appropriate fallbacks
- Authentication method: Standard session-based or OAuth2 for web apps
- Integration patterns: Use project-appropriate patterns (REST/GraphQL for web services, function calls for libraries, CLI args for tools, etc.)

### Success Criteria Guidelines

Success criteria must be:

1. **Measurable**: Include specific metrics (time, percentage, count, rate)
2. **Technology-agnostic**: No mention of frameworks, languages, databases, or tools
3. **User-focused**: Describe outcomes from user/business perspective, not system internals
4. **Verifiable**: Can be tested/validated without knowing implementation details

**Good examples**:

- "Users can complete checkout in under 3 minutes"
- "System supports 10,000 concurrent users"
- "95% of searches return results in under 1 second"
- "Task completion rate improves by 40%"

**Bad examples** (implementation-focused):

- "API response time is under 200ms" (too technical, use "Users see results instantly")
- "Database can handle 1000 TPS" (implementation detail, use user-facing metric)
- "React components render efficiently" (framework-specific)
- "Redis cache hit rate above 80%" (technology-specific)

## Done When

- [ ] Specification written to `SPEC_FILE` and validated against quality checklist
- [ ] Extension hooks dispatched or skipped according to the rules in Mandatory Post-Execution Hooks above
- [ ] Completion reported to user with feature directory, spec file path, and checklist results

# Feature Specification: US-02 – Plan list

**Feature Branch**: `003-us-02-plan-list`

**Created**: 2026-11-22

**Status**: Approved (Gate 1) — 2026-11-22

**Input**: User story [US-02](../../docs/user-stories/US-02.md) (verbatim business story, the source of truth). Builds on [US-01](../002-us-01-policyholder-vehicle-form/spec.md), which provides the step 1 form, the tab's quote session (step 1 values and completion) and a step 2 placeholder at `/:country/quote/plans`. Architecture: [ADR 0001](../../docs/adr/0001-multi-country-content-strategy.md) (Plan collection, currency on Country, limits of configurability), [ADR 0003](../../docs/adr/0003-bootstrap-grid-for-layouts.md) (layout), [ADR 0004](../../docs/adr/0004-dynamic-form-from-cms.md) (step 1 values by field key).

## Clarifications

### Session 2026-11-22

- Q: Which step 1 data drives the simulated price rule? → A: The policyholder's age and the vehicle's age: final price = base price × driver-age factor × vehicle-age factor (FR-005).
- Q: Can the business change the rule's factors from the content manager? → A: Yes, per country. The age bands and their factors are configured on the Country; the shape of the rule (age × vehicle) is fixed and documented (ADR 0001, limits of configurability).
- Q: Where is the currency configured? → A: On the Country only, with its number format, as ADR 0001 says; every plan uses its country's currency (FR-004).
- Q: What period does a price cover and what does a plan show? → A: Prices are monthly. Each plan shows only its final monthly price ("/ mes") (FR-004).
- Q (Gate 2, human design review): Should the page explain how the price is calculated? → A: No. The rule still applies, but the person doesn't need to know how the company estimates prices: no help text about it. The rule is documented as an explicit decision in the docs (ADR 0005), in the code and in the content manager (FR-004, FR-005).
- Q (Gate 2, human design review): What does "Continuar" do before a plan is chosen? → A: It is disabled until a plan is chosen, with no extra hint text (FR-008).

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - See the plans for my country (Priority: P1)

A person who completed step 1 sees the plans offered in their country, in the order the business chose, each with its name, short description, price, coverages and benefits.

**Why this priority**: Without plans there is nothing to choose; it is the core of the quote.

**Independent Test**: With plans configured for Colombia and Chile, complete step 1 in each country and check that step 2 shows only that country's active, published plans, in order, with prices in the country's currency.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** I completed step 1, **When** I reach the plans step, **Then** I see only the active and published plans for my country, in the configured order.
2. **Given** a plan, **When** I view it, **Then** I see its name, short description, final price in my country's currency and format, its coverages and its benefits.
3. **Given** a plan is inactive, unpublished or belongs to another country, **When** I view the list, **Then** it is not shown.

---

### User Story 2 - Spot the recommended plan (Priority: P2)

The business marks one plan as recommended, and the person sees it highlighted.

**Why this priority**: It guides the choice, but the list works without it.

**Independent Test**: Mark one Chilean plan as recommended, reload step 2 for Chile: that plan is visually distinguished and announced as recommended.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a plan is marked as recommended, **When** I view the plan list, **Then** that plan is visually distinguished from the others, and the distinction is not conveyed by colour alone.
2. **Given** no plan is marked as recommended, **When** I view the list, **Then** no plan is highlighted.

---

### User Story 3 - Choose one plan and continue (Priority: P1)

The person selects exactly one plan and moves on to the summary.

**Why this priority**: The quote cannot finish without a chosen plan.

content.content:
**Independent Test**: Select a plan, then another: only the last one is marked. Press "Continuar": the summary step opens. Go back: the chosen plan is still marked.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** I am on the plan list, **When** I select a plan, **Then** it is marked as chosen and any previously chosen plan is not.
2. **Given** a plan is chosen, **When** I press "Continuar", **Then** I move on to the summary step.
3. **Given** no plan is chosen, **When** I view the list, **Then** "Continuar" is disabled.
4. **Given** I chose a plan, **When** I come back to step 2 from the summary or reload the tab, **Then** the same plan is still chosen, if it is still offered.
5. **Given** I use only the keyboard or a screen reader, **When** I choose a plan, **Then** I can reach, choose and confirm it, and I hear which plan is chosen.

---

### User Story 4 - Be told when there are no plans (Priority: P2)

When the business has no active plans for a country, the person is told so instead of seeing an empty page.

**Why this priority**: An empty page would look broken and lose the person.

**Independent Test**: Deactivate every plan of a country and reach step 2: a clear message explains that no plans are available, with a way back.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** there are no active plans for my country, **When** I reach the plans step, **Then** I see a message explaining that no plans are available, and "Continuar" is not offered.

---

### Edge Cases

- **Content service fails**: step 2 shows an error with a retry action, like step 1 (US-01 FR-010).
- **Step 1 data no longer valid** (the business changed a field or rule after the person continued, review R-19): step 2 re-checks the saved step 1 values against the current fields and sends the person back to step 1 when they are not valid.
- **Chosen plan no longer offered** (deactivated, unpublished or removed): the choice is dropped, and the person must choose again.
- **Step 1 edited after choosing a plan**: the plan stays chosen and its price is recalculated with the new data.
- **More than one plan marked as recommended**: only the first one in the configured order is highlighted.
- **Plan saved without a country**: the content manager rejects it, as for form fields (ADR 0001 mitigation).
- **Plan with no coverages or no benefits**: shown without that list; never an empty heading.
- **Price adjustment needs a step 1 value that the country does not ask for**, or no band covers the age: that factor does not apply (factor 1).
- **Overlapping bands** configured by mistake: the first band in its configured order wins.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: The business team MUST be able to configure each plan per country with: name, short description, base price, coverages, benefits, order, recommended flag, active status and country, and publish or unpublish it, without code changes.
- **FR-002**: Step 2 MUST show only the plans of the active country that are published and active, sorted by their configured order.
- **FR-003**: Each plan MUST show its name, short description, final price, coverages and benefits.
- **FR-004**: Prices are monthly. Each plan MUST show only its final monthly price, followed by "/ mes", in the active country's currency and number format (Colombian pesos for Colombia, Chilean pesos for Chile), with no decimals. The currency and format are configured once on the country, never on a plan. The page does not explain how the price is calculated.
- **FR-005**: The final price MUST be the base price × the driver-age factor × the vehicle-age factor, rounded to a whole peso. Each factor comes from the age bands configured on the active country (an age range and its factor); the policyholder's age and the vehicle's age come from step 1. The rule is simulated, and it is documented as an explicit decision in the docs, in the code and in the content manager's field descriptions, but not shown to the person. The same inputs MUST always give the same price.
- **FR-006**: A plan marked as recommended MUST be visually distinguished and announced as recommended to assistive technology. At most one plan is highlighted (see Edge Cases).
- **FR-007**: The person MUST be able to choose exactly one plan; choosing another replaces the choice. The choice MUST be visible and announced.
- **FR-008**: "Continuar" MUST be disabled until a plan is chosen; once a plan is chosen, it moves to the summary step.
- **FR-009**: The chosen plan MUST be saved in the tab's session and restored when the person returns to step 2 or reloads, while the plan is still offered.
- **FR-010**: Step 2 MUST show loading, empty ("no plans available") and error (with retry) states. The empty state offers a way back to step 1.
- **FR-011**: Step 2 MUST be reachable only with a complete and still valid step 1 (US-01 guard, plus the re-check in Edge Cases).
- **FR-012**: The summary step MUST exist as a placeholder with a "Volver" action to step 2, until US-03 replaces it.
- **FR-013**: The plan list MUST be fully keyboard-operable and work on mobile (320 px) and desktop.
- **FR-014**: The seed MUST provide fictitious plans: 3 for Colombia and 3 for Chile, each with coverages and benefits, one recommended per country, plus one inactive plan to show filtering, and the price factors of each country (see Assumptions).

### Key Entities

- **Plan**: one offer in one country. Attributes: name, short description, base price, coverages (list), benefits (list), order, recommended, active, country, publication status.
- **Country** (from US-00/US-01): gains its **currency**, **number format**, **driver-age bands** and **vehicle-age bands** (each band: from age, to age, factor) in this story.
- **Quote session** (from US-01): now also holds the chosen plan.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: A plan published, reordered, highlighted or deactivated by the business team is reflected on step 2 after a reload, with no deployment, in 100% of cases.
- **SC-002**: 100% of shown prices use the country's currency and format, and match the documented rule for the given step 1 data.
- **SC-003**: A person can compare the plans and choose one in under 1 minute.
- **SC-004**: The chosen plan is still chosen in 100% of returns to step 2 and reloads, while it is offered.
- **SC-005**: The whole step can be completed using only the keyboard, on mobile (320 px) and desktop.

## Assumptions

- Copy is in Spanish. Plan texts come from the content manager; state messages and button texts are fixed application texts.
- **Seeded price factors (same for both countries, editable per country):** driver age under 25: 1.20; 25–65: 1.00; over 65: 1.15. Vehicle age 0–5 years: 1.00; 6–10: 1.10; 11–20: 1.20. Ages are whole years on the current date. It is a simulation, not a real tariff.
- The summary step (US-03) does not exist yet, so it is a placeholder (FR-012). Data stays in the tab's session and is never sent to a server.
- Data is fictitious: plan names, prices, coverages and benefits are invented.

## Conflicts with ADR 0001 *(resolved at clarify)*

- **Currency:** the story lists currency as a plan attribute; ADR 0001 keeps it only on Country. Resolved: Country only (FR-004).
- **Price rule:** resolved as a fixed, documented rule shape with its factors configured per country (FR-005), consistent with ADR 0001's limits of configurability.

**Independent Test**: Select a plan, then another: only the last one is marked. Press "Continuar": the summary step opens. Go back: the chosen plan is still marked.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** I am on the plan list, **When** I select a plan, **Then** it is marked as chosen and any previously chosen plan is not.
2. **Given** a plan is chosen, **When** I press "Continuar", **Then** I move on to the summary step.
3. **Given** no plan is chosen, **When** I view the list, **Then** "Continuar" is disabled.
4. **Given** I chose a plan, **When** I come back to step 2 from the summary or reload the tab, **Then** the same plan is still chosen, if it is still offered.
5. **Given** I use only the keyboard or a screen reader, **When** I choose a plan, **Then** I can reach, choose and confirm it, and I hear which plan is chosen.

---

### User Story 4 - Be told when there are no plans (Priority: P2)

When the business has no active plans for a country, the person is told so instead of seeing an empty page.

**Why this priority**: An empty page would look broken and lose the person.

**Independent Test**: Deactivate every plan of a country and reach step 2: a clear message explains that no plans are available, with a way back.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** there are no active plans for my country, **When** I reach the plans step, **Then** I see a message explaining that no plans are available, and "Continuar" is not offered.

---

### Edge Cases

- **Content service fails**: step 2 shows an error with a retry action, like step 1 (US-01 FR-010).
- **Step 1 data no longer valid** (the business changed a field or rule after the person continued, review R-19): step 2 re-checks the saved step 1 values against the current fields and sends the person back to step 1 when they are not valid.
- **Chosen plan no longer offered** (deactivated, unpublished or removed): the choice is dropped, and the person must choose again.
- **Step 1 edited after choosing a plan**: the plan stays chosen and its price is recalculated with the new data.
- **More than one plan marked as recommended**: only the first one in the configured order is highlighted.
- **Plan saved without a country**: the content manager rejects it, as for form fields (ADR 0001 mitigation).
- **Plan with no coverages or no benefits**: shown without that list; never an empty heading.
- **Price adjustment needs a step 1 value that the country does not ask for**, or no band covers the age: that factor does not apply (factor 1).
- **Overlapping bands** configured by mistake: the first band in its configured order wins.

- **FR-003**: Each plan MUST show its name, short description, final price, coverages and benefits.
- **FR-004**: Prices are monthly. # Feature Specification: US-03 – Summary and payment

**Feature Branch**: `004-us-03-summary-payment`

**Created**: 2026-11-22

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User story [US-03](../../docs/user-stories/US-03.md) (verbatim business story, the source of truth). Builds on [US-02](../003-us-02-plan-list/spec.md), which provides the chosen plan in the tab's quote session, the simulated price ([ADR 0005](../../docs/adr/0005-simulated-price-rule-age-bands.md)) and a summary placeholder at `/:country/quote/summary`. Architecture: [ADR 0001](../../docs/adr/0001-multi-country-content-strategy.md) (terms and conditions on Country, limits of configurability), [ADR 0003](../../docs/adr/0003-bootstrap-grid-for-layouts.md) (layout), [ADR 0004](../../docs/adr/0004-dynamic-form-from-cms.md) (step 1 values by field key). This is the last story of the wizard.

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Review my quote (Priority: P1)

A person who chose a plan sees one summary with their data, their vehicle's data and the chosen plan with its final monthly price, before paying.

**Why this priority**: The person must confirm what they are buying; it is the core of the story.

**Independent Test**: Complete steps 1 and 2 in Colombia and in Chile, reach the summary: every step 1 answer appears under its current label, grouped as policyholder or vehicle, the identity document is partly masked, and the plan shows the same price as on step 2.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** I chose a plan, **When** I reach the summary, **Then** I see my data, my vehicle's data and the chosen plan (name and final monthly price in my country's currency).
2. **Given** my country asks for different fields, **When** I view the summary, **Then** it lists the fields my country's form asked, with their current labels, in the form's order, and the label of the chosen option for list fields.
3. **Given** I entered my identity document, **When** I view the summary, **Then** only its last 4 characters are visible; the rest is replaced by a mask character.
4. **Given** an optional field I left empty, **When** I view the summary, **Then** it is not listed.

---

### User Story 2 - Fix my data or change the plan (Priority: P1)

From the summary, the person can go back to edit step 1 or choose another plan, and return to an updated summary.

**Why this priority**: The business rule requires it, and a wrong quote cannot be paid.

**Independent Test**: From the summary, edit the birth date in step 1 and continue through step 2: the summary shows the new date and the recalculated price. Then change the plan: the summary shows the new plan.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** I am on the summary, **When** I choose "Editar mis datos", **Then** step 1 opens with my answers filled in.
2. **Given** I am on the summary, **When** I choose "Cambiar plan", **Then** step 2 opens with my plan still chosen.
3. **Given** I changed my data or my plan, **When** I come back to the summary, **Then** it shows the new values and the recalculated price.

---

### User Story 3 - Accept the terms of my country (Priority: P1)

The person reads the terms and conditions configured by the business for their country and accepts them before paying.

**Why this priority**: Paying without accepting the terms is not allowed.

**Independent Test**: Change Chile's terms in the content manager and publish: the Chilean summary shows the new text, Colombia's does not change. "Pagar" stays disabled until the acceptance box is ticked.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** I am on the summary, **When** I view the terms and conditions, **Then** the text is the one published for my country.
2. **Given** I have not accepted the terms, **When** I view the summary, **Then** "Pagar" is disabled.
3. **Given** I accept the terms, **When** I view the summary, **Then** "Pagar" is enabled; if I untick them, it is disabled again.

---

### User Story 4 - Pay and get my quote number (Priority: P1)

The person pays (simulated) and gets a confirmation with a quote number; a failed payment can be retried without losing anything.

**Why this priority**: It closes the quote; without it the person never becomes insured.

**Independent Test**: Accept the terms and press "Pagar": the button is locked and shows progress, then a confirmation shows a quote number. Force a failed payment: a clear error appears, the data and the acceptance are kept, and "Pagar" works again.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** I accepted the terms, **When** I press "Pagar", **Then** the button is locked and announced as processing until the payment ends, and further presses do nothing.
2. **Given** the payment succeeds, **When** it ends, **Then** I see a confirmation with a simulated quote number, the plan and the amount paid.
3. **Given** the payment fails, **When** it ends, **Then** I see a clear error message, my data, plan and acceptance are kept, and I can press "Pagar" again.
4. **Given** I see the confirmation, **When** I reload, go back or open the summary again, **Then** the same quote is never paid twice.

---

### Edge Cases

- **Terms not configured or not published for a country**: the summary shows an error instead of the terms and "Pagar" stays disabled; a person can never pay without terms to accept.
- **Content service fails** (country, form fields or plans): the summary shows an error with a retry action, like steps 1 and 2.
- **Chosen plan no longer offered** when reaching the summary: the person is sent back to step 2 to choose again (US-02 behaviour).
- **Step 1 data no longer valid**: the person is sent back to step 1 (US-02 re-check).
- **Reaching the summary without a plan or the confirmation without a payment** (typed URL): the person is redirected to the step they still need.
- **Very long terms text**: shown in a scrollable area of limited height that is keyboard-reachable; the acceptance box stays visible.
- **Identity document of 4 characters or fewer**: shown fully masked.
- **Price changed by the business between step 2 and payment**: the summary always shows the price calculated with the current plan and country data, and that is the amount paid.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: The summary MUST show the step 1 answers in two groups, policyholder data and vehicle data, using each field's current label and order from the content manager, and the option label for list fields. Empty optional fields are not shown.
- **FR-002**: The summary MUST show the chosen plan: name, short description and final monthly price, calculated with the same rule and format as step 2 (US-02 FR-004, FR-005).
- **FR-003**: The identity document number MUST be shown partially masked: only the last 4 characters visible, the rest replaced by "•". Which fields are masked is decided per field in the content manager (see Clarifications).
- **FR-004**: The summary MUST offer "Editar mis datos" (to step 1, answers kept) and "Cambiar plan" (to step 2, plan kept). Coming back shows the updated data and price.
- **FR-005**: The business team MUST be able to configure the terms and conditions text per country, with basic formatting, publish it through draft and publish, without code changes.
- **FR-006**: The summary MUST show the active country's published terms and an unticked acceptance checkbox with a visible label. "Pagar" MUST be disabled until it is ticked.
- **FR-007**: Pressing "Pagar" MUST lock the button and show a processing state until the payment ends. While processing, and after success, the payment cannot be submitted again.
- **FR-008**: The payment is simulated: no card or bank data is asked or stored, nothing is charged, and the outcome (approved or rejected) is decided by a documented rule that testers can trigger on purpose.
- **FR-009**: On success, a confirmation view MUST show a simulated quote number, the plan, the amount paid and the country. The quote number is unique enough not to repeat in practice, and its format is documented.
- **FR-010**: On rejection, the summary MUST show a clear error message announced to assistive technology, keep the data, plan and acceptance, and let the person retry.
- **FR-011**: After a successful payment, the quote session MUST be closed so the quote cannot be paid again or edited; the confirmation stays visible on reload in the same tab, and the person can start a new quote from it.
- **FR-012**: The summary MUST be reachable only with a valid step 1 and a chosen plan still offered; the confirmation only after a successful payment.
- **FR-013**: The summary, payment and confirmation MUST show loading and error states, be fully keyboard-operable, and work on mobile (320 px) and desktop. The stepper shows step 3 "Resumen" as current.
- **FR-014**: The seed MUST provide fictitious terms and conditions for Colombia and Chile, different from each other.

### Key Entities

- **Country** (from US-00–US-02): gains its **terms and conditions** text in this story.
- **Form field** (from US-01): may gain a per-field **masked in summary** setting (see Clarifications).
- **Quote session** (from US-01/US-02): also holds the terms acceptance, the payment state and, after success, the confirmed quote (number, plan, amount, date).
- **Confirmed quote**: simulated quote number, country, plan, amount, date. It exists only in the tab; nothing is sent to a server.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: In 100% of summaries, every step 1 answer and the plan's price match what the person entered and saw on step 2.
- **SC-002**: A terms text published by the business team for a country appears on that country's summary after a reload, with no deployment, in 100% of cases.
- **SC-003**: No quote can be paid twice: repeated presses, reloads and back navigation produce at most one confirmation per quote.
- **SC-004**: After a rejected payment, the person can retry without re-entering anything, in 100% of cases.
- **SC-005**: A person can review, accept and pay in under 1 minute, using only the keyboard, on mobile (320 px) and desktop.

## Assumptions

- Copy is in Spanish. Terms text comes from the content manager; labels, buttons and messages are fixed application texts.
- The simulated payment takes about 1–2 seconds so the processing state is visible.
- Policyholder and vehicle groups follow the field groups already defined for step 1 (US-01).
- Data is fictitious: terms texts and quote numbers are invented; no real payment is made.
- The quote session lives in the tab only (US-01); closing the tab discards it, including the confirmation.

## Conflicts with ADRs *(to resolve at clarify)*

# Feature Specification: US-03 – Summary and payment

**Feature Branch**: `004-us-03-summary-payment`

**Created**: 2026-11-22

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User story [US-03](../../docs/user-stories/US-03.md) (verbatim business story, the source of truth). Builds on [US-02](../003-us-02-plan-list/spec.md), which provides the chosen plan in the tab's quote session, the simulated price ([ADR 0005](../../docs/adr/0005-simulated-price-rule-age-bands.md)) and a summary placeholder at `/:country/quote/summary`. Architecture: [ADR 0001](../../docs/adr/0001-multi-country-content-strategy.md) (terms and conditions on Country, limits of configurability), [ADR 0003](../../docs/adr/0003-bootstrap-grid-for-layouts.md) (layout), [ADR 0004](../../docs/adr/0004-dynamic-form-from-cms.md) (step 1 values by field key). This is the last story of the wizard.

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Review my quote (Priority: P1)

A person who chose a plan sees one summary with their data, their vehicle's data and the chosen plan with its final monthly price, before paying.

**Why this priority**: The person must confirm what they are buying; it is the core of the story.

**Independent Test**: Complete steps 1 and 2 in Colombia and in Chile, reach the summary: every step 1 answer appears under its current label, grouped as policyholder or vehicle, the identity document is partly masked, and the plan shows the same price as on step 2.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** I chose a plan, **When** I reach the summary, **Then** I see my data, my vehicle's data and the chosen plan (name and final monthly price in my country's currency).
2. **Given** my country asks for different fields, **When** I view the summary, **Then** it lists the fields my country's form asked, with their current labels, in the form's order, and the label of the chosen option for list fields.
3. **Given** I entered my identity document, **When** I view the summary, **Then** only its last 4 characters are visible; the rest is replaced by a mask character.
4. **Given** an optional field I left empty, **When** I view the summary, **Then** it is not listed.

---

### User Story 2 - Fix my data or change the plan (Priority: P1)

From the summary, the person can go back to edit step 1 or choose another plan, and return to an updated summary.

**Why this priority**: The business rule requires it, and a wrong quote cannot be paid.

**Independent Test**: From the summary, edit the birth date in step 1 and continue through step 2: the summary shows the new date and the recalculated price. Then change the plan: the summary shows the new plan.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** I am on the summary, **When** I choose "Editar mis datos", **Then** step 1 opens with my answers filled in.
2. **Given** I am on the summary, **When** I choose "Cambiar plan", **Then** step 2 opens with my plan still chosen.
3. **Given** I changed my data or my plan, **When** I come back to the summary, **Then** it shows the new values and the recalculated price.

---

### User Story 3 - Accept the terms of my country (Priority: P1)

The person reads the terms and conditions configured by the business for their country and accepts them before paying.

**Why this priority**: Paying without accepting the terms is not allowed.

**Independent Test**: Change Chile's terms in the content manager and publish: the Chilean summary shows the new text, Colombia's does not change. "Pagar" stays disabled until the acceptance box is ticked.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** I am on the summary, **When** I view the terms and conditions, **Then** the text is the one published for my country.
2. **Given** I have not accepted the terms, **When** I view the summary, **Then** "Pagar" is disabled.
3. **Given** I accept the terms, **When** I view the summary, **Then** "Pagar" is enabled; if I untick them, it is disabled again.

---

### User Story 4 - Pay and get my quote number (Priority: P1)

The person pays (simulated) and gets a confirmation with a quote number; a failed payment can be retried without losing anything.

**Why this priority**: It closes the quote; without it the person never becomes insured.

**Independent Test**: Accept the terms and press "Pagar": the button is locked and shows progress, then a confirmation shows a quote number. Force a failed payment: a clear error appears, the data and the acceptance are kept, and "Pagar" works again.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** I accepted the terms, **When** I press "Pagar", **Then** the button is locked and announced as processing until the payment ends, and further presses do nothing.
2. **Given** the payment succeeds, **When** it ends, **Then** I see a confirmation with a simulated quote number, the plan and the amount paid.
3. **Given** the payment fails, **When** it ends, **Then** I see a clear error message, my data, plan and acceptance are kept, and I can press "Pagar" again.
4. **Given** I see the confirmation, **When** I reload, go back or open the summary again, **Then** the same quote is never paid twice.

---

### Edge Cases

- **Terms not configured or not published for a country**: the summary shows an error instead of the terms and "Pagar" stays disabled; a person can never pay without terms to accept.
- **Content service fails** (country, form fields or plans): the summary shows an error with a retry action, like steps 1 and 2.
- **Chosen plan no longer offered** when reaching the summary: the person is sent back to step 2 to choose again (US-02 behaviour).
- **Step 1 data no longer valid**: the person is sent back to step 1 (US-02 re-check).
- **Reaching the summary without a plan or the confirmation without a payment** (typed URL): the person is redirected to the step they still need.
- **Very long terms text**: shown in a scrollable area of limited height that is keyboard-reachable; the acceptance box stays visible.
- **Identity document of 4 characters or fewer**: shown fully masked.
- **Price changed by the business between step 2 and payment**: the summary always shows the price calculated with the current plan and country data, and that is the amount paid.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: The summary MUST show the step 1 answers in two groups, policyholder data and vehicle data, using each field's current label and order from the content manager, and the option label for list fields. Empty optional fields are not shown.
- **FR-002**: The summary MUST show the chosen plan: name, short description and final monthly price, calculated with the same rule and format as step 2 (US-02 FR-004, FR-005).
- **FR-003**: The identity document number MUST be shown partially masked: only the last 4 characters visible, the rest replaced by "•". Which fields are masked is decided per field in the content manager (see Clarifications).
- **FR-004**: The summary MUST offer "Editar mis datos" (to step 1, answers kept) and "Cambiar plan" (to step 2, plan kept). Coming back shows the updated data and price.
- **FR-005**: The business team MUST be able to configure the terms and conditions text per country, with basic formatting, publish it through draft and publish, without code changes.
- **FR-006**: The summary MUST show the active country's published terms and an unticked acceptance checkbox with a visible label. "Pagar" MUST be disabled until it is ticked.
- **FR-007**: Pressing "Pagar" MUST lock the button and show a processing state until the payment ends. While processing, and after success, the payment cannot be submitted again.
- **FR-008**: The payment is simulated: no card or bank data is asked or stored, nothing is charged, and the outcome (approved or rejected) is decided by a documented rule that testers can trigger on purpose.
- **FR-009**: On success, a confirmation view MUST show a simulated quote number, the plan, the amount paid and the country. The quote number is unique enough not to repeat in practice, and its format is documented.
- **FR-010**: On rejection, the summary MUST show a clear error message announced to assistive technology, keep the data, plan and acceptance, and let the person retry.
- **FR-011**: After a successful payment, the quote session MUST be closed so the quote cannot be paid again or edited; the confirmation stays visible on reload in the same tab, and the person can start a new quote from it.
- **FR-012**: The summary MUST be reachable only with a valid step 1 and a chosen plan still offered; the confirmation only after a successful payment.
- **FR-013**: The summary, payment and confirmation MUST show loading and error states, be fully keyboard-operable, and work on mobile (320 px) and desktop. The stepper shows step 3 "Resumen" as current.
- **FR-014**: The seed MUST provide fictitious terms and conditions for Colombia and Chile, different from each other.

### Key Entities

- **Country** (from US-00–US-02): gains its **terms and conditions** text in this story.
- **Form field** (from US-01): may gain a per-field **masked in summary** setting (see Clarifications).
- **Quote session** (from US-01/US-02): also holds the terms acceptance, the payment state and, after success, the confirmed quote (number, plan, amount, date).
- **Confirmed quote**: simulated quote number, country, plan, amount, date. It exists only in the tab; nothing is sent to a server.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: In 100% of summaries, every step 1 answer and the plan's price match what the person entered and saw on step 2.
- **SC-002**: A terms text published by the business team for a country appears on that country's summary after a reload, with no deployment, in 100% of cases.
- **SC-003**: No quote can be paid twice: repeated presses, reloads and back navigation produce at most one confirmation per quote.
- **SC-004**: After a rejected payment, the person can retry without re-entering anything, in 100% of cases.
- **SC-005**: A person can review, accept and pay in under 1 minute, using only the keyboard, on mobile (320 px) and desktop.

## Assumptions

- Copy is in Spanish. Terms text comes from the content manager; labels, buttons and messages are fixed application texts.
- The simulated payment takes about 1–2 seconds so the processing state is visible.
- Policyholder and vehicle groups follow the field groups already defined for step 1 (US-01).
- Data is fictitious: terms texts and quote numbers are invented; no real payment is made.
- The quote session lives in the tab only (US-01); closing the tab discards it, including the confirmation.

## Conflicts with ADRs *(to resolve at clarify)*

- **Masking by key vs. configuration (ADR 0001/0004):** ADR 0001 says the summary finds the document by key `documentNumber`, but Chile's document field key is `rut`. Masking needs either a list of keys in code or a per-field setting in the content manager.
- **Payment outcome:** the story needs a reproducible failure, but no rule is defined; it must be agreed and documented.

### User Story 1 - Review my quote (Priority: P1)
1. **Given** I chose a plan, **When** I reach the summary, **Then** I see my data, my vehicle's data and the chosen plan (name and final monthly price in my country's currency).

2. **Given** my country asks for different fields, **When** I view the summary, **Then** it lists the fields my country's form asked, with their current labels, in the form's order, and the label of the chosen option for list fields.
-3. **Given** I entered my identity document, **When** I view the summary, **Then** only its last 4 characters are visible; the rest is replaced by a mask character.
+3. **Given** a field the business marked as masked (the identity document), **When** I view the summary, **Then** only its last 4 characters are visible; the rest is replaced by a mask character.
4. **Given** an optional field I left empty, **When** I view the summary, **Then** it is not listed.
**Why this priority**: It closes the quote; without it the person never becomes insured.

- **FR-002**: The summary MUST show the chosen plan: name, short description and final monthly price, calculated with the same rule and format as step 2 (US-02 FR-004, FR-005).

- **FR-004**: The summary MUST offer "Editar mis datos" (to step 1, answers kept) and "Cambiar plan" (to step 2, plan kept). Coming back shows the updated data and price.

## ADR changes

## Design options — plan list (`/:country/quote/plans`)

All options use the navy header and stepper, a `.container`, the `.plan-card` recipe as a native radio group, and "Volver" / "Continuar". Interactive mockups were shown at Gate 2.

- **Option A — Card grid (recommended):** `col-12 col-md-6 col-lg-4`; each card has the badge, name, description, the price with " / mes", Coberturas and Beneficios; the buttons sit below. *Pros:* easy side-by-side comparison; it matches the recipe. *Cons:* long cards on mobile.
- **Option B — Compact list:** one row per plan, with the price and radio on the right and the lists behind "Ver coberturas y beneficios". *Pros:* short on mobile. *Cons:* comparing needs extra clicks.
- **Option C — Grid with a sticky bar** showing the chosen plan, its price and "Continuar". *Pros:* the CTA is always in reach. *Cons:* the bar covers content at 320 px.

**Recommendation:** A. It is the simplest, follows the recipe, and has one keyboard path.

**Chosen (Gate 2, rounds 1–3): option A, refined with the human:**
- **Frame:** the US-01 navy header (Asegura+), the numbered stepper (S3: the done step shows a check, "Elige tu plan" is current; on mobile only the current circle and "Paso 2 de 3 · Elige tu plan"), and no help text about the price.
- **Cards (S1):** white with a 1 px `--color-border` ring, 14 px radius, no top stripe.
  - The recommended plan gets a 5 px `--color-brand` top border, a 1 px brand ring, and a large yellow "Recomendado" pill with a star (16 px bold text, an 18 px icon, 6 × 18 px padding), sitting on the top border.
- **Aligned rows:** the cards share one CSS subgrid, so the name and description, the price (after a divider), Coberturas and Beneficios start on the same line in every card.
- **Selection without layout shift:** a custom radio circle (it fills `--color-action` with a white check) plus a 2 px inset `--color-action` ring. There is no "Seleccionado" text, and nothing changes size.
- **Layout:** a 3-column grid from 992 px. Below that, a Swiper slider (about 1.2 cards on mobile, 2.2 on tablet) with previous/next arrows and dots, opening on the recommended plan. No loop and no autoplay: the cards only fade up once on load, as in step 1 (off under `prefers-reduced-motion`). Choosing a plan with the arrow keys slides to it.
- **Buttons:** "Volver" (outlined secondary) and "Continuar" (the yellow pill), which is disabled (`--color-disabled-bg` / `--color-disabled-text`) until a plan is chosen, with no hint text.

**Summary placeholder:** the US-01 placeholder card with the stepper on "Resumen", the text "El resumen llega con US-03." and "Volver". There are no options: it is temporary.

## Unit test candidates

All candidates were approved at Gate 2. Names follow `describe('US-02 · FR-XXX …')`.

| ID | Area | What it checks | Why it matters | Decision |
|----|------|----------------|----------------|----------|
| UT-01 | `simulatePrice` (8 examples) | Band edges 24/25 and 65/66 (driver) and 5/6 and 10/11 (vehicle); no band and unknown age → factor 1; overlapping bands → the first wins; rounding to a whole peso | The core business rule; SC-002 requires 100% of prices to match it, and edge errors are silent | **Approved** (Gate 2) |
| UT-02 | `agesFromStep1` (4 examples) | Birthday today vs tomorrow; the vehicle age from `vehicleYear`, never below 0; a missing or invalid value → null | A wrong age silently changes every price | **Approved** (Gate 2) |
| UT-03 | `formatPrice` (2 examples) | CO `es-CO`/COP and CL `es-CL`/CLP with no decimals and " / mes" | FR-004 forces 0 decimals; COP shows 2 by default, an easy regression | **Approved** (Gate 2) |
| UT-04 | `plan.mapper` | Only the first recommended plan is highlighted; empty coverages or benefits → []; a bad `basePrice` drops the plan | Edge cases the CMS can produce; a wrong badge misleads the person | **Approved** (Gate 2) |
| UT-05 | Country mapper (bands) | Maps `currency`, locale and bands; drops an invalid band (from > to, factor ≤ 0); missing bands → [] | Bad CMS data must not crash pricing or produce absurd prices | **Approved** (Gate 2) |
| UT-06 | `quote-session.store` | Saves and reads `planId`; `saveStep1` keeps it; `discardData` and a country change drop it | FR-009 / SC-004 persistence, plus the "step 1 edited" edge case | **Approved** (Gate 2) |
| UT-07 | Guards | `step1CompleteGuard`: valid values pass; values invalid against the current fields → step 1 with `step1Completed` cleared; fields fail to load → step 1. `planChosenGuard`: no plan → plans | FR-011 / R-19: invalid data must never reach plans or the summary | **Approved** (Gate 2) |
| UT-08 | Plan list page | Restores the choice, or drops it when the plan is not offered; Continuar disabled until a choice, then → summary; empty and error states with retry | The page's critical interactions (FR-007–FR-010) | **Approved** (Gate 2) |
| UT-09 | CMS middleware (Plan) | Rejects a plan with no country on create, update and publish; accepts a save that leaves the country untouched | ADR 0001 mitigation; a plan without a country silently disappears | **Approved** (Gate 2) |
| UT-10 | CMS country backfill | Fills currency, locale and bands only when they are missing; never overwrites an edited value | Existing databases must get the new fields without losing editors' changes | **Approved** (Gate 2) |

Not proposed: card rendering, static texts and getters, the one-line Plan controller `status` override (quickstart 9 covers it), and the plan seed contents.

## E2E candidates

| ID | Flow | Justification | Decision |
|----|------|---------------|----------|
| E2E-3 | `/co/quote`: fill in step 1 → the plans show in order, in COP, with the badge → Continuar disabled → choose → summary → Volver keeps the choice | The story's core promise: CMS plans, the price, the choice and the session together, which only the real stack proves | **Approved** (Gate 2) |
| E2E-4 | `/cl/quote` with a driver aged 22 and a vehicle 8 years old → the CLP prices equal base × 1.20 × 1.10 | The price rule reading the CMS bands and step 1 data end to end, in the second country | **Approved** (Gate 2) |

Not proposed: the empty and error states, admin edits, and reloads (unit tests and the quickstart cover them). The full-flow E2E belongs to US-03.
