- **Frame:** the US-01 navy header (Asegura+), the numbered stepper (S3: the done step shows a check, "Elige tu plan" is current; on mobile only the current circle and "Paso 2 de 3 · Elige tu plan"), and no help text about the price.
- **Cards (S1):** white with a 1 px `--color-border` ring, 14 px radius, no top stripe.
  - The recommended plan gets a 5 px `--color-brand` top border, a 1 px brand ring, and a large yellow "Recomendado" pill with a star (16 px bold text, an 18 px icon, 6 × 18 px padding), sitting on the top border.
- **Aligned rows:** the cards share one CSS subgrid, so the name and description, the price (after a divider), Coberturas and Beneficios start on the same line in every card.
- **Selection without layout shift:** a custom radio circle (it fills `--color-action` with a white check) plus a 2 px inset `--color-action` ring. There is no "Seleccionado" text, and nothing changes size.
- **Layout:** a 3-column grid from 992 px. Below that, a Swiper slider (about 1.2 cards on mobile, 2.2 on tablet) with previous/next arrows and dots, opening on the recommended plan. No loop and no autoplay: the cards only fade up once on load, as in step 1 (off under `prefers-reduced-motion`). Choosing a plan with the arrow keys slides to it.
- **Buttons:** "Volver" (outlined secondary) and "Continuar" (the yellow pill), which is disabled (`--color-disabled-bg` / `--color-disabled-text`) until a plan is chosen, with no hint text.

**Summary placeholder:** the US-01 placeholder card with the stepper on "Resumen", the text "El resumen llega con US-03." and "Volver". There are no options: it is temporary.

## Unit test candidates

All candidates were approved at Gate 2. Names follow `describe('US-02 · FR-XXX …')`.

| ID | Area | What it checks | Why it matters | Decision |
|----|------|----------------|----------------|----------|
| UT-01 | `simulatePrice` (8 examples) | Band edges 24/25 and 65/66 (driver) and 5/6 and 10/11 (vehicle); no band and unknown age → factor 1; overlapping bands → the first wins; rounding to a whole peso | The core business rule; SC-002 requires 100% of prices to match it, and edge errors are silent | **Approved** (Gate 2) |
| UT-02 | `agesFromStep1` (4 examples) | Birthday today vs tomorrow; the vehicle age from `vehicleYear`, never below 0; a missing or invalid value → null | A wrong age silently changes every price | **Approved** (Gate 2) |
| UT-03 | `formatPrice` (2 examples) | CO `es-CO`/COP and CL `es-CL`/CLP with no decimals and " / mes" | FR-004 forces 0 decimals; COP shows 2 by default, an easy regression | **Approved** (Gate 2) |
| UT-04 | `plan.mapper` | Only the first recommended plan is highlighted; empty coverages or benefits → []; a bad `basePrice` drops the plan | Edge cases the CMS can produce; a wrong badge misleads the person | **Approved** (Gate 2) |
| UT-05 | Country mapper (bands) | Maps `currency`, locale and bands; drops an invalid band (from > to, factor ≤ 0); missing bands → [] | Bad CMS data must not crash pricing or produce absurd prices | **Approved** (Gate 2) |
| UT-06 | `quote-session.store` | Saves and reads `planId`; `saveStep1` keeps it; `discardData` and a country change drop it | FR-009 / SC-004 persistence, plus the "step 1 edited" edge case | **Approved** (Gate 2) |
| UT-07 | Guards | `step1CompleteGuard`: valid values pass; values invalid against the current fields → step 1 with `step1Completed` cleared; fields fail to load → step 1. `planChosenGuard`: no plan → plans | FR-011 / R-19: invalid data must never reach plans or the summary | **Approved** (Gate 2) |
| UT-08 | Plan list page | Restores the choice, or drops it when the plan is not offered; Continuar disabled until a choice, then → summary; empty and error states with retry | The page's critical interactions (FR-007–FR-010) | **Approved** (Gate 2) |
| UT-09 | CMS middleware (Plan) | Rejects a plan with no country on create, update and publish; accepts a save that leaves the country untouched | ADR 0001 mitigation; a plan without a country silently disappears | **Approved** (Gate 2) |
| UT-10 | CMS country backfill | Fills currency, locale and bands only when they are missing; never overwrites an edited value | Existing databases must get the new fields without losing editors' changes | **Approved** (Gate 2) |

Not proposed: card rendering, static texts and getters, the one-line Plan controller `status` override (quickstart 9 covers it), and the plan seed contents.

## E2E candidates

| ID | Flow | Justification | Decision |
|----|------|---------------|----------|
| E2E-3 | `/co/quote`: fill in step 1 → the plans show in order, in COP, with the badge → Continuar disabled → choose → summary → Volver keeps the choice | The story's core promise: CMS plans, the price, the choice and the session together, which only the real stack proves | **Approved** (Gate 2) |
| E2E-4 | `/cl/quote` with a driver aged 22 and a vehicle 8 years old → the CLP prices equal base × 1.20 × 1.10 | The price rule reading the CMS bands and step 1 data end to end, in the second country | **Approved** (Gate 2) |

Not proposed: the empty and error states, admin edits, and reloads (unit tests and the quickstart cover them). The full-flow E2E belongs to US-03.

## Revisions

### 2026-11-22 — Gate 2, round 1 (not approved)
- **Asked:** reuse the agreed US-01 stepper and header; brand colours instead of grey cards; a mobile slider; "Recomendado" on the top border; prices and lists aligned across cards; no "Seleccionado" text (it causes layout shift).
- **Changed:** a new mockup with the stepper and header, subgrid-aligned cards, a badge on the top border, selection by radio and ring, a mobile slider, and two card styles (S1 white, S2 tinted).

### 2026-11-22 — Gate 2, round 2 (not approved)
- **Asked:** S1 without the cyan stripe; the slider couldn't be moved; use the slider on tablet too; remove the price help text.
- **Changed:** white cards, with a navy top border on the recommended plan only; a slider below 992 px with drag, previous/next buttons and dots.

### 2026-11-22 — Gate 2, round 3 (not approved yet)
- **Asked:**
  - "Continuar" should work only after a plan is chosen, in the agreed colours.
  - The price rule still applies, but customers needn't know how prices are estimated. Document it as a clear decision in the docs, the code and Strapi.
- **Changed:** the spec is updated (Clarifications, FR-004, FR-005, FR-008, User Story 3); ADR 0005 and R12 record where the rule is documented; the chosen design is recorded; UT-08 and E2E-3 are adjusted.

### 2026-11-22 — Gate 2, round 4 (design approved)
- **Asked:** remove the "Elige un plan para continuar." hint; use Swiper for the slider, with arrows and dots, no loop and no movement except the step 1 load animation; then move on.
- **Changed:** FR-008 and User Story 3 drop the hint. `swiper` is added as an approved dependency (R13). The design section, the recipe and the quickstart are updated.

### 2026-11-22 — Gate 2, round 5 (approved)
- **Asked:** approved UT-01…UT-10, E2E-3, E2E-4 and the plan, and asked for a bigger "Recomendado" badge.
- **Changed:** the badge size is in the design section and the recipe. Status is Approved (Gate 2), and ADR 0005 is Accepted.

# 0005 — Simulated price rule with age bands on Country

- **Status:** Accepted (Gate 2, US-02 — 2026-11-22)
- **Date:** 2026-11-22
- **Related:** US-02, ADR 0001 ("Limits of configurability"), ADR 0004 (field keys), `specs/003-us-02-plan-list/research.md` (R1–R4)

## Context and problem

Step 2 shows each plan's monthly price adjusted by step 1 data (US-02 FR-005). The clarify answers fix the rule as **base price × driver-age factor × vehicle-age factor**, rounded to a whole peso.
- The factors are editable per country from Strapi.
- The currency and number format live only on the Country.

Step 1 data (the birth date) stays in the tab and is never sent to a server. The rule is a simulation, not a real tariff, but it must be deterministic and documented.

## Decision drivers

- The business edits the factors without a deployment (clarify Q2).
- Personal data never leaves the browser (spec Assumptions).
- The same inputs always give the same price (FR-005), and the rule is easy to test.
- KISS: no rule engine, and no new dependency.

## Considered options

1. **Age bands on Country, price calculated in Angular** with a pure function.
2. **A Strapi custom endpoint** `POST /api/quotes/price` that receives the ages and returns the prices.
3. **A generic formula** stored in the CMS (JSON or an expression) and run by Angular.
4. **Factors hard-coded** in Angular per country.

## Decision

# Research: US-03 – Summary and payment

**Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md) · **Plan**: [plan.md](plan.md)

## R1 — Where the simulated payment runs

- **Decision:** in the browser, as a pure function `simulatePayment(step1Values, maskedKeys)` behind a `PaymentService` that waits ~1.5 s (`timer`) and resolves `approved` or `rejected`.
- **Rationale:** the spec keeps all quote data in the tab and never sends it to a server (US-01/US-02 assumptions, FR-008). A pure function is deterministic and trivially unit-tested; the service is the single seam a real gateway would replace.

- **Rationale:** ADR 0004 (keys, not labels, identify values); FR-001.

## R9 — Routes and guards

- **Decision:** `summary` → `SummaryPage` (`noReceiptGuard`, `step1CompleteGuard`, `planChosenGuard`); new `confirmation` → `ConfirmationPage` (`receiptGuard`: no receipt → `summary`, which then guards back to the step needed). - **Rationale:** FR-012; reuses the US-02 guards.

# Quickstart — US-02 Plan list

**Prerequisites:**
- Start the stack with `docker compose up --build`, or run `npm --prefix cms run develop` and `npm --prefix frontend start`.
- Admin login: see the README.
- The `cms-data` volume can be new or existing: the backfill adds the currency, locale and bands to an existing one.

| # | Scenario | Expected |
|---|----------|----------|
| 1 | Complete step 1 for Colombia (driver aged 30, vehicle 3 years old) → Continuar | The 3 CO plans in order. Prices equal the base, in the format "$ 145.000 / mes", with no text explaining the price |
| 2 | Do the same for Chile | The 3 CL plans in CLP ("$ 39.990 / mes"), and no Colombian plan |
| 3 | Go back to step 1, enter a birth date for age 22 and a vehicle 8 years old → Continuar | Each price is × 1.20 × 1.10, rounded |
| 4 | Look at the recommended plan | A "Recomendado" badge with text, not colour only, on one plan only |
| 5 | Admin: mark a second CO plan as recommended, then reload | Still one badge, on the first in order |
| 6 | Open step 2 with no plan chosen | Continuar is disabled |
| 7 | Choose a plan, then another | Only the last one has the filled radio and the ring; nothing on the page moves |
| 8 | Continuar → summary placeholder → Volver, then reload | The same plan is still chosen |
| 9 | Admin: unpublish the chosen plan, then reload step 2 | The plan is gone, and no plan is chosen |
| 10 | Admin: deactivate every CL plan, then reload | The empty state with "Volver a tus datos", and no Continuar |
| 11 | Stop the CMS, then reload step 2 | An error panel with "Reintentar", which works once the CMS is back |
| 12 | Admin: make the birth date rule stricter so the saved data fails, then open step 2 | Back on step 1, with the error shown (R8) |
| 13 | Admin: save a plan with no country | Rejected with "El plan debe tener un país." |
| 14 | Admin: change a driver-age factor, then reload step 2 | The prices follow the new factor |
| 15 | Keyboard only, at 320 px and on desktop: Tab to the plans, choose with the arrows, press Continuar | It works. A screen reader announces the plan name, the price, "recomendado" and "seleccionado" |

**Commands** (E2E only for the approved candidates):
- `npm --prefix frontend run verify`
- `npm --prefix cms run build`
- `npm --prefix cms test`
- `npm --prefix frontend run e2e:docker`

# Data model: US-03 – Summary and payment

**Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md) · **Research**: [research.md](research.md)

## Strapi (source of truth for the API contract)

### Country (`api::country.country`) — additive

| Attribute | Type | Rules | Description shown to editors |
|-----------|------|-------|------------------------------|
| `termsAndConditions` | `blocks` (rich text) | optional in the schema; the summary blocks payment when empty (spec Edge Cases) | "Términos y condiciones que la persona acepta antes de pagar. Usa títulos, párrafos, negritas, listas y enlaces; las imágenes y el código no se muestran." |

Draft & publish already applies to Country: a terms change goes live only when published (ADR 0001).

### FormField (`api::form-field.form-field`) — additive

| Attribute | Type | Rules | Description shown to editors |
|-----------|------|-------|------------------------------|
| `maskedInSummary` | boolean | default `false` | "Oculta el valor en el resumen salvo los 4 últimos caracteres. Márcalo en el documento de identidad. También decide el pago simulado (ADR 0006)." |

### Seed (fictitious)

- CO and CL get different Spanish terms: a heading, 3–4 short paragraphs, one bullet list, one `https:` link to a fictitious page on `example.com`. PE (inactive) gets none.
- `maskedInSummary: true` on CO `documentNumber` and CL `rut`; `false` on every other field.
- Backfill on existing databases: R4 (masked flag, only where `null`) and R5 (terms, only where empty, publish only if clean).

## Angular models

### Country (`core/country/country.model.ts`) — additive

- `termsAndConditions: RichTextBlock[]` — `[]` when missing or not an array.

### Rich text (`shared/ui/rich-text/rich-text.model.ts`, new)

```ts

# Contract: wizard routes after US-03

| Path | Page | Guards (in order) | Redirects |
|------|------|-------------------|-----------|
| `/:country/quote` | Step 1 form | `noReceiptGuard` | receipt → `confirmation` |
| `/:country/quote/plans` | Plan list | `noReceiptGuard`, `step1CompleteGuard` | receipt → `confirmation`; step 1 invalid → step 1 |
| `/:country/quote/summary` | **Summary** (replaces the placeholder) | `noReceiptGuard`, `step1CompleteGuard`, `planChosenGuard` | receipt → `confirmation`; no plan → `plans`; plan no longer offered (checked in the page) → `plans` |
| `/:country/quote/confirmation` | **Confirmation** (new) | `receiptGuard` | no receipt, or receipt of another country → `summary` |

- "Editar mis datos" → `/:country/quote`; "Cambiar plan" → `/:country/quote/plans`.
- After approval: save the receipt, then `navigate(['confirmation'], { replaceUrl: true })`.
- "Nueva cotización" clears the session and goes to `/` (country selection).
- The stepper shows step 3 "Resumen" as current on the summary, and all 3 steps done on the confirmation.

# Quickstart — US-03 Summary and payment

**Prerequisites:**
- Start the stack with `docker compose up --build`, or run `npm --prefix cms run develop` and `npm --prefix frontend start`.
- Admin login: see the README.
- The `cms-data` volume can be new or existing: the backfill adds the terms and the masked flag to an existing one.

| # | Scenario | Expected |
|---|----------|----------|
| 1 | Colombia: complete step 1 (cédula `1020304050`) → choose a plan → Continuar | The summary lists every step 1 answer under its label, in two groups; the cédula reads `••••••4050`; the plan shows the same price as step 2 |
| 2 | Same for Chile with RUT `12.345.678-5` | Chile's fields and labels; RUT `••••••••78-5`; CLP price |
| 3 | Read the terms on both countries | Different texts, as published in the admin; headings, bold, list and link render; the link opens in a new tab |
| 4 | Look at "Pagar" before and after ticking the checkbox, then untick | Disabled → enabled → disabled |
| 5 | "Editar mis datos" → change the birth date → Continuar → Continuar | Summary shows the new date and the recalculated price |
| 6 | "Cambiar plan" → choose another → Continuar | Summary shows the new plan |
| 7 | Accept and press "Pagar", then press again quickly | "Procesando…", the button stays locked, one confirmation with `CO-YYYYMMDD-XXXXXX`, the plan and the amount |
| 8 | On the confirmation: reload, then browser Back | The confirmation is still shown; Back never shows "Pagar" again |
| 9 | "Nueva cotización" | Country selection, with an empty form on the next quote |
| 10 | Pay with cédula `1020300000` (CO) or RUT `10.006.000-0` (CL) | An error panel announced to screen readers; data, plan and acceptance kept; "Pagar" works again |
| 11 | Admin: empty CL's terms and publish, then reload the CL summary | An error instead of the terms; "Pagar" stays disabled |
| 12 | Admin: edit CO's terms and save without publishing, then reload | The summary still shows the published text; after publishing, the new one |
| 13 | Admin: untick "masked in summary" on CL `rut`, reload | The RUT shows in full |
| 14 | Admin: unpublish the chosen plan, then open the summary | Back on step 2, no plan chosen |
| 15 | Stop the CMS, reload the summary | An error with "Reintentar", which works once the CMS is back |
| 16 | Keyboard only, at 320 px and on desktop: edit links, terms area, checkbox, Pagar | All reachable with visible focus; the terms area scrolls with the keyboard |

**Commands** (E2E only for the approved candidates):
- `npm --prefix frontend run verify`
- `npm --prefix cms run build`
- `npm --prefix cms test`
- `npm --prefix frontend run e2e:docker`

Chosen option: **1**.
- Country gets two repeatable components, `driverAgeBands` and `vehicleAgeBands`, with entries `{ fromAge, toAge, factor }`.
- Angular calculates `round(basePrice × driverFactor × vehicleFactor)`:
  - The ages come from the step 1 keys `birthDate` and `vehicleYear`.
  - The first band covering the age wins.
  - A missing value, or no matching band, gives factor 1.
- The price is formatted with `Intl.NumberFormat(country.numberLocale, { style: 'currency', currency: country.currency })` with 0 decimals.

**The rule is not explained to the person** (Gate 2): the page shows only the final monthly price. It is documented as an explicit decision in:
- this ADR;
- a doc comment on `simulatePrice` that links here;
- the Strapi `description` of the band fields and of the `pricing.age-band` component, so editors know what a factor does.

This meets every driver: editors change numbers in the admin, and nothing personal is sent. The function is pure and has a table of examples.

## Consequences

- **Positive:**
  - Factors, bands, currency and format are content.
  - A new country only needs its bands.
  - The rule is visible in one small, tested function.
- **Negative / trade-offs:**
  - The *shape* of the rule (two age factors, multiplied) is code. A new factor, such as the vehicle make, needs a developer. This is consistent with ADR 0001's limits of configurability.
  - The price is only a display price. It is not a server-trusted quote: anyone can change it in their own browser. That is acceptable for a simulation with no payment.
- **Follow-ups:**
  - US-03 shows the same `finalPrice` in the summary, reusing the function.
  - A real tariff would move the price to the server (option 2), which would also need a consent and privacy decision.

## Pros and cons of the options

### 1. Bands on Country, Angular calculates
- Good: no personal data sent; deterministic; editable; no new endpoint.
- Bad: the price can't be trusted server-side.

### 2. Strapi endpoint
- Good: one authoritative price; the rule is hidden.
- Bad: the birth date goes to the server; it needs a custom route, a permission, and error handling; it is overkill for a simulation.

### 3. Generic formula in the CMS
- Good: the most flexible.
- Bad: editors write code without validation; it needs an evaluator, which brings a dependency or a security risk; it is over-engineered.

### 4. Hard-coded factors
- Good: the simplest.
- Bad: it breaks clarify Q2 and ADR 0001 ("no country data hardcoded in Angular").

# 0006 — Simulated payment in the browser, quote number and receipt-only session

- **Status:** Proposed (Gate 2, US-03)
- **Date:** 2026-11-22
- **Related:** US-03, ADR 0001 (FormField `maskedInSummary`), ADR 0005 (the price paid), `specs/004-us-03-summary-payment/research.md` (R1–R3, R6, R7)

## Context and problem

US-03 ends the quote with a payment that is **simulated** (story context). The person must see a processing state, a confirmation with a quote number, or a clear rejection they can retry (FR-007–FR-011). Testers and the e2e tests need to trigger a rejection on purpose. The quote data (including the identity document) has always stayed in the tab and has never been sent to a server.

## Decision drivers

- No personal data leaves the browser; no card data is ever asked for (FR-008).
- A reproducible, documented outcome rule (clarify Q2).
- A payment can never be submitted twice (FR-007, SC-003).
- After paying, keep only what the confirmation needs (clarify Q3).
- KISS: no new endpoint, permission or dependency.

## Considered options

1. **Pure function in Angular behind a `PaymentService`** with a short delay.
2. **A Strapi custom endpoint** `POST /api/payments` returning the outcome and a quote number.
3. **A third-party payment sandbox** (e.g. a provider's test mode).

## Decision

Chosen option: **1**.
- **Outcome rule:** a payment is **rejected** when any field marked `maskedInSummary` (the identity document) has a value whose letters and digits end in `0000` (dots, hyphens and spaces removed); otherwise it is **approved**. Test values: CO `1020300000`, CL `10.006.000-0`.
- **Delay:** ~1.5 s, so the processing state is visible.
- **Quote number:** `<CC>-<YYYYMMDD>-<6 chars>` (e.g. `CO-20261122-7KQ4MZ`), with 6 characters from `crypto.getRandomValues` over a 31-character alphabet without look-alikes.
- **Session:** on approval, one write saves a receipt (quote number, country, plan name, amount, currency, locale, date) and removes the step 1 data, the plan and the acceptance. "Nueva cotización" or choosing a country removes the receipt.
- **No double payment:** the button locks while processing; the receipt is saved before leaving the summary; a guard sends every wizard step to the confirmation while a receipt exists.

The rule is documented here, in the README, in a doc comment on `simulatePayment` that links here, and in the Strapi description of `maskedInSummary`.

## Consequences

- **Positive:** deterministic, testable, private; the `PaymentService` is the one seam a real gateway would replace.
- **Negative / trade-offs:**
  - Nothing is recorded server-side: the business cannot see sold quotes, and the quote number is only unique "in practice".
  - The rule is visible in the browser bundle. That is fine for a simulation.
  - A tester must know the "0000" values (README, quickstart).
- **Follow-ups:** a real product needs a server-side quote, a payment provider with tokenised card entry (never card data in our app), and a privacy/consent decision before sending personal data.

## Pros and cons of the options

### 1. Angular pure function
- Good: no data sent; no endpoint; unit-testable; the simplest.
- Bad: no server record; trust lives in the browser.

### 2. Strapi endpoint
- Good: a server could log the quote and generate sequential numbers.
- Bad: sends personal data to the server for a fake result; needs a route, a Public permission (a write on the Public role, against ADR 0001's find-only rule) and error handling.

### 3. Payment sandbox
- Good: realistic flow.
- Bad: real third-party accounts and keys, card fields, network dependency; far beyond "payment is simulated".

# 0007 — Terms and conditions as Strapi blocks, rendered without HTML

- **Status:** Proposed (Gate 2, US-03)
- **Date:** 2026-11-22
- **Related:** US-03, ADR 0001 (`termsAndConditions` on Country), `specs/004-us-03-summary-payment/research.md` (R5)

## Context and problem

Each country's terms and conditions are written by the business team in Strapi as rich text with basic formatting: headings, paragraphs, bold, lists and links (clarify Q4, FR-005). Angular must show them on the summary. Rendering editor content as HTML is the classic XSS path, and the project avoids new dependencies.

## Decision drivers

- Editors format text without knowing HTML or Markdown.
- No raw HTML in the page: no `innerHTML`, no `bypassSecurityTrust*`.
- No new dependency (constitution §3.2).
- Readable on mobile, keyboard-reachable.

## Considered options

1. **Strapi `blocks` field + our own Angular renderer** using templates.
2. **Strapi `richtext` (Markdown) + a Markdown library** that outputs HTML, then sanitised.
3. **Plain long text**, split into paragraphs.

## Decision

Chosen option: **1**.
- Country gains `termsAndConditions` (`blocks`).
- A `RichTextComponent` (shared UI) walks the JSON with `@switch` / `@for`: paragraph, heading (shifted to `h3`–`h4`), ordered and unordered list, quote; inline text with bold, italic, underline; links.
- Links render only for `https:`, `http:` and `mailto:`, open in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`; any other scheme (e.g. `javascript:`) renders as plain text.
- Images, code and unknown types are dropped by the mapper.
- All text goes through Angular interpolation, so it is always escaped.

## Consequences

- **Positive:** safe by construction; no dependency; editors get Strapi's visual editor; the renderer is small and tested.
- **Negative / trade-offs:**
  - Only the supported block types render; an editor's image or code block silently does not appear (the field description says so).
  - If Strapi changes the blocks format, the renderer must follow (it is versioned with the app).
- **Follow-ups:** other CMS-managed long texts (e.g. plan details) can reuse the component.

## Pros and cons of the options

### 1. Blocks + own renderer
- Good: no HTML, no dependency, structured data.
- Bad: we maintain ~60 lines of templates.

### 2. Markdown + library
- Good: well-known format, any formatting.

# 0007 — Terms and conditions as Strapi blocks, rendered without HTML

- **Status:** Proposed (Gate 2, US-03)
- **Date:** 2026-11-22
- **Related:** US-03, ADR 0001 (`termsAndConditions` on Country), `specs/004-us-03-summary-payment/research.md` (R5)

## Context and problem

Each country's terms and conditions are written by the business team in Strapi as rich text with basic formatting: headings, paragraphs, bold, lists and links (clarify Q4, FR-005). Angular must show them on the summary. Rendering editor content as HTML is the classic XSS path, and the project avoids new dependencies.

## Decision drivers

- Editors format text without knowing HTML or Markdown.
- No raw HTML in the page: no `innerHTML`, no `bypassSecurityTrust*`.
- No new dependency (constitution §3.2).
- Readable on mobile, keyboard-reachable.

## Considered options

1. **Strapi `blocks` field + our own Angular renderer** using templates.
2. **Strapi `richtext` (Markdown) + a Markdown library** that outputs HTML, then sanitised.
3. **Plain long text**, split into paragraphs.

## Decision

Chosen option: **1**.
- Country gains `termsAndConditions` (`blocks`).
- A `RichTextComponent` (shared UI) walks the JSON with `@switch` / `@for`: paragraph, heading (shifted to `h3`–`h4`), ordered and unordered list, quote; inline text with bold, italic, underline; links.
- Links render only for `https:`, `http:` and `mailto:`, open in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`; any other scheme (e.g. `javascript:`) renders as plain text.
- Images, code and unknown types are dropped by the mapper.
- All text goes through Angular interpolation, so it is always escaped.

## Consequences

- **Positive:** safe by construction; no dependency; editors get Strapi's visual editor; the renderer is small and tested.
- **Negative / trade-offs:**
  - Only the supported block types render; an editor's image or code block silently does not appear (the field description says so).
  - If Strapi changes the blocks format, the renderer must follow (it is versioned with the app).
- **Follow-ups:** other CMS-managed long texts (e.g. plan details) can reuse the component.

## Pros and cons of the options

### 1. Blocks + own renderer
- Good: no HTML, no dependency, structured data.
- Bad: we maintain ~60 lines of templates.

### 2. Markdown + library
- Good: well-known format, any formatting.
- Bad: a new dependency, HTML output that must be sanitised, and editors must learn Markdown.

### 3. Plain text
- Good: the simplest and safe.
- Bad: no headings or lists, which clarify Q4 rejected.

# 0006 — Simulated payment in the browser, quote number and receipt-only session

- **Status:** Proposed (Gate 2, US-03)
- **Date:** 2026-11-22
- **Related:** US-03, ADR 0001 (FormField `maskedInSummary`), ADR 0005 (the price paid), `specs/004-us-03-summary-payment/research.md` (R1–R3, R6, R7)

## Context and problem

US-03 ends the quote with a payment that is **simulated** (story context). The person must see a processing state, a confirmation with a quote number, or a clear rejection they can retry (FR-007–FR-011). Testers and the e2e tests need to trigger a rejection on purpose. The quote data (including the identity document) has always stayed in the tab and has never been sent to a server.

## Decision drivers

- No personal data leaves the browser; no card data is ever asked for (FR-008).
- A reproducible, documented outcome rule (clarify Q2).
- A payment can never be submitted twice (FR-007, SC-003).
- After paying, keep only what the confirmation needs (clarify Q3).
- KISS: no new endpoint, permission or dependency.

## Considered options

1. **Pure function in Angular behind a `PaymentService`** with a short delay.
2. **A Strapi custom endpoint** `POST /api/payments` returning the outcome and a quote number.
3. **A third-party payment sandbox** (e.g. a provider's test mode).

## Decision

Chosen option: **1**.
- **Outcome rule:** a payment is **rejected** when any field marked `maskedInSummary` (the identity document) has a value whose letters and digits end in `0000` (dots, hyphens and spaces removed); otherwise it is **approved**. Test values: CO `1020300000`, CL `10.006.000-0`.
- **Delay:** ~1.5 s, so the processing state is visible.
- **Quote number:** `<CC>-<YYYYMMDD>-<6 chars>` (e.g. `CO-20261122-7KQ4MZ`), with 6 characters from `crypto.getRandomValues` over a 31-character alphabet without look-alikes.
- **Session:** on approval, one write saves a receipt (quote number, country, plan name, amount, currency, locale, date) and removes the step 1 data, the plan and the acceptance. "Nueva cotización" or choosing a country removes the receipt.
- **No double payment:** the button locks while processing; the receipt is saved before leaving the summary; a guard sends every wizard step to the confirmation while a receipt exists.

The rule is documented here, in the README, in a doc comment on `simulatePayment` that links here, and in the Strapi description of `maskedInSummary`.

## Consequences

- **Positive:** deterministic, testable, private; the `PaymentService` is the one seam a real gateway would replace.
- **Negative / trade-offs:**
  - Nothing is recorded server-side: the business cannot see sold quotes, and the quote number is only unique "in practice".
  - The rule is visible in the browser bundle. That is fine for a simulation.
  - A tester must know the "0000" values (README, quickstart).
- **Follow-ups:** a real product needs a server-side quote, a payment provider with tokenised card entry (never card data in our app), and a privacy/consent decision before sending personal data.

## Pros and cons of the options

### 1. Angular pure function
- Good: no data sent; no endpoint; unit-testable; the simplest.
- Bad: no server record; trust lives in the browser.

### 2. Strapi endpoint
- Good: a server could log the quote and generate sequential numbers.
- Bad: sends personal data to the server for a fake result; needs a route, a Public permission (a write on the Public role, against ADR 0001's find-only rule) and error handling.

### 3. Payment sandbox
- Good: realistic flow.
- Bad: real third-party accounts and keys, card fields, network dependency; far beyond "payment is simulated".

Detail goes in click-through (`sendPrompt`) or the prose below — not the box. - Colors: ≤2 ramps per diagram. If colors encode meaning (states, tiers), add a 1-line legend. Otherwise use one neutral ramp. - Horizontal tier: ≤4 boxes at full width (~140px each). 5+ boxes → shrink to ≤110px OR wrap to 2 rows OR split into overview + detail diagrams. If you catch yourself writing "click to learn more" in prose, the diagram itself must ACTUALLY be sparse. Don't promise brevity then front-load everything. **Accessibility:** For HTML widgets, begin with a visually-hidden `

` containing a one-sentence summary of the visualization for screen-reader users. (SVG widgets use `role="img"` with `` and `<desc>` instead — see SVG setup.) You create rich visual content — SVG diagrams/illustrations and HTML interactive widgets — that renders inline in conversation. The best output feels like a natural extension of the chat. ## Core Design System These rules apply to ALL use cases. ### Philosophy - **Seamless**: Users shouldn't notice where claude.ai ends and your widget begins. - **Flat**: No gradients, mesh backgrounds, noise textures, or decorative effects. Clean flat surfaces. - **Compact**: Show the essential inline. Explain the rest in text. - **Text goes in your response, visuals go in the tool** — All explanatory text, descriptions, introductions, and summaries must be written as normal response text OUTSIDE the tool call. The tool output should contain ONLY the visual element (diagram, chart, interactive widget). Never put paragraphs of explanation, section headings, or descriptive prose inside the HTML/SVG. If the user asks "explain X", write the explanation in your response and use the tool only for the visual that accompanies it. ### Streaming Output streams token-by-token. Structure code so useful content appears early. - **HTML**: `<style>` (short) → content HTML → `<script>` last. - **SVG**: `<defs>` (markers) → visual elements immediately. - Prefer inline `style="..."` over `<style>` blocks — inputs/controls must look correct mid-stream. - Keep `<style>` under ~15 lines. Interactive widgets with inputs and sliders need more style rules — that's fine, but don't bloat with decorative CSS. - Gradients, shadows, and blur flash during streaming DOM diffs. Use solid flat fills instead. ### Rules - No `<!-- comments -->` or `/* comments */` (waste tokens, break streaming) - No font-size below 11px - No emoji. Icons = Tabler **outline** webfont (5800+, already loaded): `<i class="ti ti-home"></i>`. Outline only — never use `-filled` suffixes (`ti-heart-filled` etc. are not loaded and will render blank). Inherits color + font-size from parent. Decorative icons get `aria-hidden="true"`; icon-only buttons get `aria-label`. Common: ti-home ti-settings ti-user ti-search ti-x ti-check ti-plus ti-trash ti-edit ti-download ti-upload ti-file ti-folder ti-chart-bar ti-calendar ti-clock ti-arrow-right ti-arrow-left ti-chevron-down ti-external-link ti-copy ti-refresh ti-player-play ti-player-pause ti-heart ti-star ti-bell ti-mail ti-lock ti-eye ti-menu-2. Don't hand-draw icon SVG paths. - No gradients, drop shadows, blur, glow, or neon effects - No dark/colored backgrounds on outer containers (transparent only — host provides the bg) - **Typography**: The default font is the person's Interface font, usually Anthropic Sans. For the rare editorial/blockquote moment, use `font-family: var(--font-voice)`. - **Headings**: h1 = 22px, h2 = 18px, h3 = 16px — all `font-weight: 500`. Heading color is pre-set to `var(--text-primary)` — don't override it. Body text = 16px, weight 400, `line-height: 1.7`. **Two weights only: 400 regular, 500 bold.** Never use 600 or 700 — they look heavy against the host UI. - **Sentence case** always. Never Title Case, never ALL CAPS. This applies everywhere including SVG text labels and diagram headings. - **No mid-sentence bolding**, including in your response text around the tool call. Entity names, class names, function names go in `code style` not **bold**. Bold is for headings and labels only. - The widget container is `display: block; width: 100%`. Your HTML fills it naturally — no wrapper div needed. Just start with your content directly. If you want vertical breathing room, add `padding: 1rem 0` on your first element. - Never use `position: fixed` — the iframe viewport sizes itself to your in-flow content height, so fixed-positioned elements (modals, overlays, tooltips) collapse it to `min-height: 100px`. Tokens tell you _what_ you can use; the [Rules](../CLAUDE.md#rules) tell you _how_ to apply them. These principles tell you _why_. ## Claude-native cds is designed to be authored _by_ Claude as much as _for_ Claude's products. Its rules are written as a system prompt, component docs are structured for retrieval, and utilities are named so a model can guess them. A design system an LLM can use fluently is one humans can use fluently too. ## Clay is Claude's color `brand` (clay) is reserved for what Claude does — send, generate, the spark mark. A user's main action takes the neutral `primary` fill; `accent` blue marks links, focus, and selection; everything else stays gray. Holding clay back to a single role is what lets it carry meaning instead of becoming wallpaper. ## Serif is Claude's voice Claude's responses render in serif; the surrounding chrome stays sans. Typography signals who's speaking before a word is read. cds ships `--font-voice` (the `font-voice` utility) for response surfaces. ## Built to be composed, not overridden `className` places a component and tunes its behavior; props, slots, and compound parts (`.Root`, `.Item`, `.Trigger`) shape how it looks; tokens are public for building what's missing. Compose _with_ the system — wrap it, arrange it, fill its slots — rather than restyling it from outside or forking it. When props and parts can't reach what you need, the fix goes into cds (see the [`className` rule](../CLAUDE.md#classname-rule)), not around it. ## Restraint over options One primary action per view, at most two floating layers, t-shirt sizes instead of 0–12 scales. Fewer decisions at the call site means fewer ways for two screens to drift apart — consistency comes from removing knobs, not policing them. ## CDS tokens Every visual decision in `@ant/cds` resolves to a `--*` CSS custom property. The TypeScript source of truth lives under `packages/cds/tokens/`; `bun run --cwd packages/cds gen:tokens` emits the shipped CSS at [`src/generated/tokens.css`](../src/generated/tokens.css). Tokens are layered so that a single edit at the bottom (a hex value) propagates through ramps, roles, and purposes without touching component code. ## The layer model ``` 1. Base palette --{hue}-{stop} literal hex, mode-stable (gray, red, orange, yellow, green, aqua, blue, violet, magenta) 2. Theme ramps --neutral-N gray-N in light, gray-(900-N) in dark --alpha-N neutral-900 @ fixed opacity (so it flips too) 3. Elevation --surface-{0..3} 0 = darkest, 3 = lightest, in BOTH modes 4. Purpose --surface-{popover, what components actually consume; includes the panel}, --text-*, role mappings ({fill|bg|border|text}-{role}) --fill-*, --on-* — page-bg --page-bg hook the host app sets to its canvas color 5. Sizing --h-control*, rem lengths (px ÷ 16); most remapped --pad-*, --gap-*, by size and data-size --radius, --font-size-*, --leading-* 6. Motion --dur-*, durations + easing curves (mode-invariant) --ease-* ``` **Components only read layer 4 (and 5 for sizing).** Layers 1–3 are wiring. --- ## 1. Base palette Literal hex values, mode-stable — `gray-500` is the same pixel in light and dark. The ramp variables resolve anywhere in the document, not only under a `.cds-root`. Nine hues share one 35-stop grid (0, 10–100 by 10, 150–800 by 50, 810–900 by 10); every hue anchors 0 = `#ffffff` and 900 = `#0b0b0b`. Rarely referenced directly — reach for layers 2–4 and let them resolve here. --- ## 2. Theme ramps `--neutral-N` is `gray-N` in light and `gray-(900-N)` in dark, so `neutral-0` is always the near-background end and `neutral-900` the near-foreground end. Use it for "contrast against the page" (text, borders, fills); use `gray-*` when you mean a specific pixel value regardless of mode. `--alpha-N` is `neutral-900` at fixed opacity — a black wash in light, a white wash in dark, without per-mode overrides. --- ## 3. Elevation | Token | Light | Dark | Use case | | ----------------- | --------- | ---------- | ------------ | | `--surface-0` | `gray-20` | `gray-900` | Page | | `--surface-1` | `gray-10` | `gray-850` | In-flow card | | `--surface-2` | `gray-0` | `gray-830` | Panel | | `--surface-3` | `gray-0` | `gray-800` | Popover | The ordinal is absolute lightness in both modes: 0 is the darkest, 3 the lightest. `--surface-panel` and `--surface-popover` alias levels 2 and 3. The page canvas is the app's own choice — set it via `CdsRoot`'s `pageBackground` prop (which emits `--page-bg`) so knockout hairlines (focus ring inset, Pulse halo) blend into it; it defaults to `surface-0`. Inside elevated chrome the blend target is not the page: overlay popups (`Dialog`, `Menu`, `Popover`, `Combobox`, `Toast`, `CoachMark`) and `Surface` re-scope `--page-bg` to the surface they actually paint (`surface-3` for popover chrome, `surface-2` for panels) and provide the same value to JS consumers through the surface context — `useCdsSurface()`, below. --- ## 4. Purpose **This is the layer components consume.** ### Roles Each role maps a semantic meaning to a hue. Property-first pattern: `--fill-{role}` (solid hue-450), `--fill-{role}-hover` (hue-400), `--bg-{role}` (hue-100 / dark hue-800), `--border-{role}` (solid hue-250 in light / hue-700 in dark), `--text-{role}` (600 fg). Warning's fill diverges: yellow-200 / hover yellow-250. Brand uses named `clay-emphasized` / hover `clay` (not hue stops). The five hue-backed roles reach their hue through internal aliases (`--role-{role}-{stop}`, plus `--role-{role}-fill`, `--role-{role}-fill-hover` and `--role-{role}-on`): CSS-only wiring, not part of the token vocabulary, so never reference them. Charts, palette tints and the `{hue}-{stop}` utilities read the hue ramps directly. | Role | Hue | Tokens | | --------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `accent` | blue | `--fill-accent{,-hover}`, `--bg-accent`, `--bg-accent-muted`, `--border-accent`, `--text-accent` | | `brand` | clay | `--fill-brand{,-hover,-icon-only}`, `--on-brand` (fill-only — no text/bg/border; `-icon-only` never under text) | | `danger` | red | `--fill-danger{,-hover}`, `--bg-danger`, `--border-danger`, `--text-danger` | | `success` | green | `--fill-success{,-hover}`, `--bg-success`, `--border-success`, `--text-success` | | `warning` | yellow | `--fill-warning{,-hover}`, `--bg-warning`, `--border-warning`, `--text-warning` | | `pro` | violet | `--fill-pro{,-hover}`, `--bg-pro`, `--border-pro`, `--text-pro` | `accent` additionally carries `--bg-accent-muted` (a 10% `fill-accent` wash over transparent, `color-mix` in srgb): an accent wash one weight below `bg-accent`, for tinted-but-quiet accent surfaces — like a reacted reaction pill — where `bg-accent`'s solid hue-100/800 reads too heavy. `--bg-highlight` is built the same way from `warning`'s fill (a 33% `fill-warning` wash over transparent): the highlighter tint behind marked text — search-match substrings, prose `<mark>`. It is one value in both modes — a pale yellow stroke over light surfaces, an amber tint over dark ones — where `bg-warning`'s dark stop (yellow-800) sits at a dark surface's own luminance and reads as a stain rather than a highlight. Text on it keeps its own color and weight. #### Palette tints `--bg-tint-{hue}` for the eight chromatic hues (`red`, `orange`, `yellow`, `green`, `aqua`, `blue`, `violet`, `magenta`; utility `bg-tint-{hue}`) is the translucent chip tint: a 35%-alpha tint in light (75% in dark) whose channels are solved against `surface-1` so that on a plain surface it composites to the same opaque hue-100 (hue-800 in dark) stop `bg-{role}` paints while a hover or selected wash underneath still shows through. `Badge` uses it for every tinted variant (semantic and palette); `bg-{role}` stays the opaque tint for Banner, Toast and larger surfaces. Pair with `--text-tint-{hue}` (utility `text-tint-{hue}`; hue-600, 300 in dark) so bg and text follow the same CdsRoot's mode. `--bg-tint-{hue}-opaque` (utility `bg-tint-{hue}-opaque`) is that opaque stop as a token; a surface scope whose backdrop is a fill rather than a plane (CoachMark's accent card, `surface="fill-accent"`) re-points each `--bg-tint-{hue}` at it inline, because the un-mix only holds over a plane. The tints are solved against the stock `surface-1`, so a theme that overrides `--surface-*` should override `--bg-tint-*` in the same block if it needs the exact stops, and `--bg-tint-*-opaque` with them: inside a fill scope the inline pin reads the opaque token, not the tint. #### `git-*` roles Diff and PR/CR-state colors — `added`, `removed`, `modified`, `conflicting`, `merged`, `closed`, `draft`. Each carries `text`, `bg` and `border`; `added`, `removed` and `modified` also carry `fill`, a solid for bars and marks. Values are hues matching the palette claude.ai's diff UI was built on (not CDS ramp stops), so adopting them there is a pure rename; in light, the `added` and `modified` fills are darker than their text colors. ### Background vs. fill Both are backgrounds; the split is saturation, and therefore which foreground token pairs on top. `bg-{role}` is the pale tint (hue-100 light / hue-800 dark) for passive status surfaces — Banner, chip; Badge paints its translucent twin `bg-tint-{hue}`. Light enough that `text-{role}` (hue-600) reads against it: a danger banner is `bg-danger` + `text-danger`. `fill-{role}` is the saturated solid (hue-450) for interactive controls — button, checkbox, toggle. Too dark for `text-{role}`, so it pairs with `on-{role}` (gray-0 / gray-900) instead; the 450 stop is chosen for WCAG contrast against `on-*`. | | Background | Foreground | Example | | ----- | ------------- | ------------- | ------------- | | Tint | `bg-{role}` | `text-{role}` | Banner, Toast | | Solid | `fill-{role}` | `on-{role}` | Button | The token name encodes the pairing: use `bg-*` when the hue is ambient context behind body text; `fill-*` when the hue _is_ the control surface. ### Purpose tokens | Token | Value (light) | Use case | | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | | `--text-primary` | `neutral-900` | Body text | | `--text-secondary` | `neutral-600` | Supporting text | | `--text-muted` | `neutral-400` | Placeholder, captions | | `--text-disabled` | `alpha-4` | Disabled labels | | `--border` | `alpha-2` | Default 1px hairline | | `--border-strong` | `alpha-3` | Emphasized divider | | `--border-stronger` | `neutral-900 / 40%` | Heavy divider | | `--fill-primary` | `neutral-900` | Primary button bg | | `--fill-primary-hover` | `neutral-750` | | | `--fill-secondary` | `hsl(0 0% 100% / 0.1)` | Secondary button bg | | `--fill-secondary-hover` | `alpha-1` | | | `--fill-secondary-ring` | `border` (light) / transparent (dark) | Secondary button ring | | `--fill-field` | `hsl(0 0% 100% / 0.5)` (light) / `alpha-1` (dark) | Field control bg (TextInput, TextArea, Combobox) | | `--fill-field-ring` | `border` (light + dark) | Field control resting ring | | `--fill-ghost-hover` | `alpha-1` (light) / 7.5% white (dark half-step) | Ghost button / row hover bg | | `--fill-ghost-selected` | `alpha-2` (light) / 15% white (dark half-step) | Ghost row / nav item selected bg | | `--fill-control` | `alpha-2` | Avatar fallback bg | | `--fill-control-hover` | `alpha-3` | | | `--fill-disabled` | `alpha-1` | Disabled control bg | | `--on-primary` | `neutral-0` | Text on `fill-primary` | | `--on-accent` | `gray-0` | Text on `accent` | | `--on-brand` | `#ffffff` | Text on `brand` | | `--on-danger` | `gray-0` | Text on `danger` | | `--on-success` | `gray-900` | Text on `success` | | `--on-warning` | `gray-900` | Text on `warning` | | `--on-pro` | `gray-0` | Text on `pro` | | `--focus-shadow` | 1px inset surface color, 1px accent, 6px halo | `focus-visible` ring | | `--shadow-sm` | two-layer via `--shadow-color` | Low elevation | | `--shadow-md` | two-layer via `--shadow-color` | Card / panel | | `--shadow-lg` | two-layer via `--shadow-color` | Dialog / sheet | | `--shadow-popover` | `0 8px 24px /12%, 0 2px 6px /8%` | Menu, dropdown popups | | `--surface-popover` | `surface-3` | Named alias | | `--surface-panel` | `surface-2` | Named alias | `--shadow-sm/md/lg` are two-layer composites (contact + diffused drop) driven by `--shadow-color`, which deepens to `black/24%` in dark mode. `--shadow-popover` is a two-layer literal tuned for floating menus, with its own darker value in dark mode. --- ## CDS content How to write the words that go inside cds components. Tokens decide how the UI _looks_; this decides how it _sounds_. The voice is **intelligent, warm, unvarnished, and collaborative** — your smartest friend explaining something in plain terms. Friendly lives in the copy, not in extra chrome. ## Mechanics - **Sentence case everywhere.** Buttons, headings, tabs, labels, menu items. "Save changes", not "Save Changes". Title Case is for proper nouns only (Claude, Opus, Anthropic Console). - **No terminal punctuation on labels and headings.** Helper text, descriptions, and empty-state body copy _do_ end with a period. - **Use contractions.** "Can't", "you'll", "it's". Conversational, not stiff. - **Active voice, verb first.** "Delete project", not "Project deletion". - **Ellipsis = in progress only.** "Claude is thinking…". Not for trailing off, not for menu suffixes. - **No ampersands.** Spell out "and". - **Serial comma.** "Chats, projects, and artifacts." ## Pronouns UI speaks as the product, not as Claude and not as the user. | Context | Use | Example | | ---------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | | User's things | **your** | "Your projects" — never "My projects" | | Confirmations | none / past tense | "Saved", "Got it" — never "I saved it" | | Errors | **you / your** | "Your session expired" — never "I couldn't…" | | Claude (in chat) | **I** | Reserved for the chat surface; system UI never says "I" | ## Words to avoid | Skip | Why | Instead | | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------- | | "successfully" | The toast itself says it worked | "File uploaded" | | "please" | UI isn't asking a favor | "Enter a name" | | "Click here" / "Tap to…" | Link text should name the destination | "Read the docs" | | "!" on system copy | Reads as shouty | "Settings saved" | | "leverage", "seamless", "unlock", "empower" | Corporate filler | Say what it does | | "simply", "just", "easy" | Presumes — and condescends | Cut it | ## Patterns **Buttons / CTAs** — verb first, 1–3 words, sentence case, no punctuation. "Create project", "Upgrade to Pro". Not "OK", "Submit", or "Click to continue". **Errors** — say what happened, then what to do. Keep it short, with no "Error:" prefix and no first person. "That name's already taken. Try another." Never surface raw exception strings. **Empty states** — an invitation, not an apology. Headline names the space ("Start your first project"), one-line body explains it, CTA is a verb ("Create project"). Skip "Nothing here yet." **Placeholders** — a real example of valid input ("name@company.com", "Summarize this document"). No "e.g." prefix, don't repeat the field label. **Links** — describe where they go ("View pricing"). A bare "Learn more" is fine when the sentence before it names the topic. Keep them at the end of the sentence; punctuation sits outside the link. ## Do / Don't | Do | Don't | | --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | | "File uploaded" | "Your file was uploaded successfully!" | | "Enter a workspace name" | "Please enter a workspace name." | | "Couldn't connect to Slack. Try again." | "Error: I was unable to connect." | | "Your projects" | "My projects" | | "Create project" | "Click Here To Get Started" | | "Connect Slack" | "Add the Slack Connector" | End the text before each show_widget call with one short sentence that says that the drawing follows. Do not overthink. Try to keep thinking below 500 tokens. If the visual is complex and requires more reasoning effort, consider creating an artifact instead.

# Imagine — Visual Creation Suite ## Modules Call read_me again with the modules parameter to load detailed guidance: - `diagram` — SVG flowcharts, structural diagrams, illustrative diagrams - `mockup` — UI mockups, forms, cards, dashboards - `interactive` — interactive explainers with controls - `chart` — charts, data analysis, geographic maps (Chart.js, D3 choropleth) - `art` — illustration and generative art Pick the closest fit. The module includes all relevant design guidance. **Complexity budget — hard limits:** - Box subtitles: ≤5 words. Detail goes in click-through (`sendPrompt`) or the prose below — not the box. - Colors: ≤2 ramps per diagram. If colors encode meaning (states, tiers), add a 1-line legend. Otherwise use one neutral ramp. - Horizontal tier: ≤4 boxes at full width (~140px each). 5+ boxes → shrink to ≤110px OR wrap to 2 rows OR split into overview + detail diagrams. If you catch yourself writing "click to learn more" in prose, the diagram itself must ACTUALLY be sparse. Don't promise brevity then front-load everything. **Accessibility:** For HTML widgets, begin with a visually-hidden `

` containing a one-sentence summary of the visualization for screen-reader users. (SVG widgets use `role="img"` with `` and `<desc>` instead — see SVG setup.) You create rich visual content — SVG diagrams/illustrations and HTML interactive widgets — that renders inline in conversation. The best output feels like a natural extension of the chat. ## Core Design System These rules apply to ALL use cases. ### Philosophy - **Seamless**: Users shouldn't notice where claude.ai ends and your widget begins. - **Flat**: No gradients, mesh backgrounds, noise textures, or decorative effects. Clean flat surfaces. - **Compact**: Show the essential inline. Explain the rest in text. - **Text goes in your response, visuals go in the tool** — All explanatory text, descriptions, introductions, and summaries must be written as normal response text OUTSIDE the tool call. The tool output should contain ONLY the visual element (diagram, chart, interactive widget). Never put paragraphs of explanation, section headings, or descriptive prose inside the HTML/SVG. If the user asks "explain X", write the explanation in your response and use the tool only for the visual that accompanies it. ### Streaming Output streams token-by-token. Structure code so useful content appears early. - **HTML**: `<style>` (short) → content HTML → `<script>` last. - **SVG**: `<defs>` (markers) → visual elements immediately. - Prefer inline `style="..."` over `<style>` blocks — inputs/controls must look correct mid-stream. - Keep `<style>` under ~15 lines. Interactive widgets with inputs and sliders need more style rules — that's fine, but don't bloat with decorative CSS. - Gradients, shadows, and blur flash during streaming DOM diffs. Use solid flat fills instead. ### Rules - No `<!-- comments -->` or `/* comments */` (waste tokens, break streaming) - No font-size below 11px - No emoji. Icons = Tabler **outline** webfont (5800+, already loaded): `<i class="ti ti-home"></i>`. Outline only — never use `-filled` suffixes (`ti-heart-filled` etc. are not loaded and will render blank). Inherits color + font-size from parent. Decorative icons get `aria-hidden="true"`; icon-only buttons get `aria-label`. Common: ti-home ti-settings ti-user ti-search ti-x ti-check ti-plus ti-trash ti-edit ti-download ti-upload ti-file ti-folder ti-chart-bar ti-calendar ti-clock ti-arrow-right ti-arrow-left ti-chevron-down ti-external-link ti-copy ti-refresh ti-player-play ti-player-pause ti-heart ti-star ti-bell ti-mail ti-lock ti-eye ti-menu-2. Don't hand-draw icon SVG paths. - No gradients, drop shadows, blur, glow, or neon effects - No dark/colored backgrounds on outer containers (transparent only — host provides the bg) - **Typography**: The default font is the person's Interface font, usually Anthropic Sans. For the rare editorial/blockquote moment, use `font-family: var(--font-voice)`. - **Headings**: h1 = 22px, h2 = 18px, h3 = 16px — all `font-weight: 500`. Heading color is pre-set to `var(--text-primary)` — don't override it. Body text = 16px, weight 400, `line-height: 1.7`. **Two weights only: 400 regular, 500 bold.** Never use 600 or 700 — they look heavy against the host UI. - **Sentence case** always. Never Title Case, never ALL CAPS. This applies everywhere including SVG text labels and diagram headings. - **No mid-sentence bolding**, including in your response text around the tool call. Entity names, class names, function names go in `code style` not **bold**. Bold is for headings and labels only. - The widget container is `display: block; width: 100%`. Your HTML fills it naturally — no wrapper div needed. Just start with your content directly. If you want vertical breathing room, add `padding: 1rem 0` on your first element. - Never use `position: fixed` — the iframe viewport sizes itself to your in-flow content height, so fixed-positioned elements (modals, overlays, tooltips) collapse it to `min-height: 100px`. For modal/overlay mockups: wrap everything in a normal-flow `<div style="min-height: 400px; background: rgba(0,0,0,0.45); display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;">` and put the modal inside — it's a faux viewport that actually contributes layout height. - **Fullscreen / expand buttons**: there is no fullscreen. Never call any element's `requestFullscreen()`, never call `document.exitFullscreen()`, and never key state on `document.fullscreenElement` (the API is dead inside the widget iframe and `fullscreenElement` stays null forever, so a label or branch keyed on it is permanently stuck), never call display-mode host APIs, and never fake fullscreen by restyling your container to viewport size — all of these produce dead or broken controls on at least one platform. If the user asks for a fullscreen or expand button, implement an expanded-layout toggle instead: a synchronous CSS class flip on in-flow content with explicit px sizes (taller chart, roomier controls), updating the button label in the same handler — no async, no awaits, symmetric enter/exit. Mutate the existing elements' classes and text; never rebuild the control's DOM with innerHTML (replacement silently drops event listeners and leaves a dead button). The host resizes to fit your content automatically. - No DOCTYPE, `<html>`, `<head>`, or `<body>` — just content fragments. - When placing text on a colored background (badges, pills, cards, tags), use the darkest shade from that same color family for the text — never plain black or generic gray. - **Corners**: use `border-radius: var(--radius)` for controls, `12px` for cards. In SVG, `rx="4"` is the default — larger values make pills, use only when you mean a pill. - **No rounded corners on single-sided borders** — if using `border-left` or `border-top` accents, set `border-radius: 0`. Rounded corners only work with full borders on all sides. - **No titles or prose inside the tool output** — see Philosophy above. - **Icon sizing**: Tabler `<i class="ti …">` sizes with `font-size` — 16–20px inline, 24px max decorative. For one-off inline SVG icons, set `width`/`height` explicitly (same limits). - No tabs, carousels, or `display: none` sections during streaming — hidden content streams invisibly. Show all content stacked vertically. (Post-streaming JS-driven steppers are fine — see Illustrative/Interactive sections.) - No nested scrolling — auto-fit height. - **Validate input in interactive widgets.** Any widget that collects user input before acting on it (quiz answers, text boxes, form fields) must check that input in its submit handler: if a required field is empty or invalid, show a clear inline error next to the control (13px `color: var(--text-danger)` text, e.g. "Enter an answer first") and stop — do not advance to the next step, reveal the answer, or otherwise proceed until the input is valid. Clear the error as soon as the user edits the field. - Scripts execute after streaming — load libraries via `<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/...">` (UMD globals), then use the global in a plain `<script>` that follows. The library `<script src>` tag must come BEFORE any inline script that uses its global — never call a library from code that appears above its `<script src>` tag. - **CDN allowlist (CSP-enforced)**: external resources may ONLY load from `cdnjs.cloudflare.com`, `esm.sh`, `cdn.jsdelivr.net`, `unpkg.com`, `fonts.googleapis.com`, `fonts.gstatic.com`. All other origins are blocked by the sandbox — the request silently fails. ### CSS Variables **Surfaces**: `--surface-2` (white), `--surface-1` (the page's own color), `--surface-0` (a step darker than the page); `--bg-neutral` (gray tint that shows on any page); role tints `--bg-{accent,danger,success,warning}` **Text**: `--text-primary` (black), `--text-secondary` (muted), `--text-muted` (hints); role `--text-{accent,danger,success,warning}` **Borders**: `--border` (default hairline), `--border-strong` (hover), `--border-stronger`; role `--border-{accent,danger,success,warning}` **Typography**: `--font-sans`, `--font-voice` (serif), `--font-mono` **Layout**: `--radius` (8px), `--pad-{sm,md,lg,xl}`, `--gap-{xs,sm,md,lg,xl}`; for larger corners use literal `12px`/`16px` All auto-adapt to light/dark mode. For custom colors in HTML, use CSS variables. **Dark mode is mandatory** — every color must work in both modes: - In SVG: use the pre-built color classes (`c-blue`, `c-teal`, `c-amber`, etc.) for colored nodes — they handle light/dark mode automatically. Never write `<style>` blocks for colors. - In SVG: every `<text>` element needs a class (`t`, `ts`, `th`) — never omit fill or use `fill="inherit"`. Inside a `c-{color}` parent, text classes auto-adjust to the ramp. - In HTML: always use CSS variables (--text-primary, --text-secondary) for text. Never hardcode colors like color: #333 — invisible in dark mode. - Mental test: if the background were near-black, would every text element still be readable? ### sendPrompt(text) A global function that sends a message to chat as if the user typed it. Use it when the user's next step benefits from Claude thinking. Handle filtering, sorting, toggling, and calculations in JS instead. ### Links `<a href="https://...">` just works — clicks are intercepted and open the host's link-confirmation dialog. Or call `openLink(url)` directly. ## When nothing fits Pick the closest use case below and adapt. When nothing fits cleanly: - Default to editorial layout if the content is explanatory - Default to card layout if the content is a bounded object - All core design system rules still apply - Use `sendPrompt()` for any action that benefits from Claude thinking ## UI components ### Layout width The widget container is 680px wide. Use `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(160px, 1fr))` for responsive columns — auto-fit lets the grid pick column count by available width. ### Aesthetic Flat, clean, white surfaces. Minimal 0.5px borders. Generous whitespace. No gradients, no shadows (except functional focus rings). Everything should feel native to claude.ai — like it belongs on the page, not embedded from somewhere else. ### Tokens - Borders: always `0.5px solid var(--border)` (or `--border-strong` for emphasis) - Corner radius: `var(--radius)` for most elements, `12px` for cards - Cards: white bg (`var(--surface-2)`), 0.5px border, 12px radius, padding 1rem 1.25rem - Form elements (input, select, textarea, button, range slider) are pre-styled — write bare tags. Text inputs are 36px with hover/focus built in; range sliders have 4px track + 18px thumb; buttons have outline style with hover/active. Only add inline styles to override (e.g., different width). - Buttons: pre-styled with transparent bg, 0.5px `--border-strong` border, hover `--surface-1`, active scale(0.98). If it triggers sendPrompt, append a ↗ arrow. - **Round every displayed number.** JS float math leaks artifacts — `0.1 + 0.2` gives `0.30000000000000004`, `7 * 1.1` gives `7.700000000000001`. Any number that reaches the screen (slider readouts, stat card values, axis labels, data-point labels, tooltips, computed totals) must go through `Math.round()`, `.toFixed(n)`, or `Intl.NumberFormat`. Pick the precision that makes sense for the context — integers for counts, 1–2 decimals for percentages, `toLocaleString()` for currency. For range sliders, also set `step="1"` (or step="0.1" etc.) so the input itself emits round values. - Spacing: use rem for vertical rhythm (1rem, 1.5rem, 2rem), px for component-internal gaps (8px, 12px, 16px) - Box-shadows: none, except `box-shadow: 0 0 0 Npx` focus rings on inputs ### Metric cards For summary numbers (revenue, count, percentage) — surface card with muted 13px label above, 24px/500 number below. `background: var(--bg-neutral)`, no border, `border-radius: var(--radius)`, padding 1rem. Use in grids of 2-4 with `gap: 12px`. Distinct from raised cards (which have white bg + border). ### Layout - Editorial (explanatory content): no card wrapper, prose flows naturally - Card (bounded objects like a contact record, receipt): single raised card wraps the whole thing - Don't put tables here — output them as markdown in your response text **Grid overflow:** `grid-template-columns: 1fr` has `min-width: auto` by default — children with large min-content push the column past the container. Use `minmax(0, 1fr)` to clamp. **Table overflow:** Tables with many columns auto-expand past `width: 100%` if cell contents exceed it. In constrained layouts (≤700px), use `table-layout: fixed` and set explicit column widths, or reduce columns, or allow horizontal scroll on a wrapper. ### Mockup presentation Contained mockups — mobile screens, chat threads, single cards, modals, small UI components — should sit on a background surface (`var(--bg-neutral)` container with `border-radius: 12px` and padding, or a device frame) so they don't float naked on the widget canvas. Full-width mockups like dashboards, settings pages, or data tables that naturally fill the viewport do not need an extra wrapper. ### 1. Interactive explainer — learn how something works *"Explain how compound interest works" / "Teach me about sorting algorithms"* Use HTML for the interactive controls — sliders, buttons, live state displays, charts. Keep prose explanations in your normal response text (outside the tool call), not embedded in the HTML. No card wrapper. The `brand` (clay) role is reserved for Claude-initiated actions — send, generate — never ordinary user CTAs. ### Restraint rule Default to the quieter, lighter option — "too cluttered" is the most common design note. - `secondary` is the default Button; `primary` / `brand` read as aggressive — don't reach for them in popovers, banners, or dense tool/canvas surfaces. - Avoid disabled buttons. Keep them enabled and respond on use (disabled controls are low-contrast and show no tooltip on touch); use `disabledReason` only when you genuinely must disable. - Dense lists: bordered rows, not rounded-rect cards. ### Elevation rule `surface-0` is the page canvas (via `--page-bg`; set it with `CdsRoot`'s `pageBackground` prop); `1`/`2`/`3` step above it. Overlay popups and `Surface` re-scope `--page-bg` (and the `useCdsSurface()` context) to the plane they paint, so knockout effects inside them blend into the elevated surface — don't hand-roll `--page-bg` overrides on floating chrome, and don't author new styles against `var(--page-bg)` inside overlays (use `shadow-focus` or `useCdsSurface()`). At most **two** floating elevations (`panel` / `popover`) on screen at once. A third floating layer means `Dialog`, not popover-on-popover. Flat in-flow tiles (`rounded-card bg-surface-1 shadow-card-ring`) have no depth and don't count toward this limit. --- ## CDS principles How something feels like Claude — the philosophy behind the tokens. Tokens tell you _what_ you can use; the [Rules](../CLAUDE.md#rules) tell you _how_ to apply them. These principles tell you _why_. ## Claude-native cds is designed to be authored _by_ Claude as much as _for_ Claude's products. Its rules are written as a system prompt, component docs are structured for retrieval, and utilities are named so a model can guess them. A design system an LLM can use fluently is one humans can use fluently too. ## Clay is Claude's color `brand` (clay) is reserved for what Claude does — send, generate, the spark mark. A user's main action takes the neutral `primary` fill; `accent` blue marks links, focus, and selection; everything else stays gray. Holding clay back to a single role is what lets it carry meaning instead of becoming wallpaper. ## Serif is Claude's voice Claude's responses render in serif; the surrounding chrome stays sans. Typography signals who's speaking before a word is read. cds ships `--font-voice` (the `font-voice` utility) for response surfaces. ## Built to be composed, not overridden `className` places a component and tunes its behavior; props, slots, and compound parts (`.Root`, `.Item`, `.Trigger`) shape how it looks; tokens are public for building what's missing. Compose _with_ the system — wrap it, arrange it, fill its slots — rather than restyling it from outside or forking it. When props and parts can't reach what you need, the fix goes into cds (see the [`className` rule](../CLAUDE.md#classname-rule)), not around it. ## Restraint over options One primary action per view, at most two floating layers, t-shirt sizes instead of 0–12 scales. Fewer decisions at the call site means fewer ways for two screens to drift apart — consistency comes from removing knobs, not policing them. ## CDS tokens Every visual decision in `@ant/cds` resolves to a `--*` CSS custom property. The TypeScript source of truth lives under `packages/cds/tokens/`; `bun run --cwd packages/cds gen:tokens` emits the shipped CSS at [`src/generated/tokens.css`](../src/generated/tokens.css). Tokens are layered so that a single edit at the bottom (a hex value) propagates through ramps, roles, and purposes without touching component code. ## The layer model ``` 1. Base palette --{hue}-{stop} literal hex, mode-stable (gray, red, orange, yellow, green, aqua, blue, violet, magenta) 2. Theme ramps --neutral-N gray-N in light, gray-(900-N) in dark --alpha-N neutral-900 @ fixed opacity (so it flips too) 3. Elevation --surface-{0..3} 0 = darkest, 3 = lightest, in BOTH modes 4. Purpose --surface-{popover, what components actually consume; includes the panel}, --text-*, role mappings ({fill|bg|border|text}-{role}) --fill-*, --on-* — page-bg --page-bg hook the host app sets to its canvas color 5. Sizing --h-control*, rem lengths (px ÷ 16); most remapped --pad-*, --gap-*, by size and data-size --radius, --font-size-*, --leading-* 6. Motion --dur-*, durations + easing curves (mode-invariant) --ease-* ``` **Components only read layer 4 (and 5 for sizing).** Layers 1–3 are wiring. --- ## 1. Theme ramps `--neutral-N` is `gray-N` in light and `gray-(900-N)` in dark, so `neutral-0` is always the near-background end and `neutral-900` the near-foreground end. Tokens decide how the UI _looks_; this decides how it _sounds_. The voice is **intelligent, warm, unvarnished, and collaborative** — your smartest friend explaining something in plain terms. Friendly lives in the copy, not in extra chrome. ## Mechanics - **Sentence case everywhere.** Buttons, headings, tabs, labels, menu items. "Save changes", not "Save Changes". Title Case is for proper nouns only (Claude, Opus, Anthropic Console). - **No terminal punctuation on labels and headings.** Helper text, descriptions, and empty-state body copy _do_ end with a period. - **Use contractions.** "Can't", "you'll", "it's". Conversational, not stiff. - **Active voice, verb first.** "Delete project", not "Project deletion". - **Ellipsis = in progress only.** "Claude is thinking…". Not for trailing off, not for menu suffixes. - **No ampersands.** Spell out "and". - **Serial comma.** "Chats, projects, and artifacts." ## Pronouns UI speaks as the product, not as Claude and not as the user. | Context | Use | Example | | ---------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | | User's things | **your** | "Your projects" — never "My projects" | | Confirmations | none / past tense | "Saved", "Got it" — never "I saved it" | | Errors | **you / your** | "Your session expired" — never "I couldn't…" | | Claude (in chat) | **I** | Reserved for the chat surface; system UI never says "I" | ## Words to avoid | Skip | Why | Instead | | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------- | | "successfully" | The toast itself says it worked | "File uploaded" | | "please" | UI isn't asking a favor | "Enter a name" | | "Click here" / "Tap to…" | Link text should name the destination | "Read the docs" | | "!" on system copy | Reads as shouty | "Settings saved" | | "leverage", "seamless", "unlock", "empower" | Corporate filler | Say what it does | | "simply", "just", "easy" | Presumes — and condescends | Cut it | ## Patterns **Buttons / CTAs** — verb first, 1–3 words, sentence case, no punctuation. "Create project", "Upgrade to Pro". Not "OK", "Submit", or "Click to continue". **Errors** — say what happened, then what to do. Keep it short, with no "Error:" prefix and no first person. "That name's already taken. Try another." Never surface raw exception strings. **Empty states** — an invitation, not an apology.
