"stop condition" .-> H[["Human escalation"]] ``` - **Step 4b is an automatic check, not a gate:** it fixes `tasks.md` on its own, and only stops for the human when a finding needs a change to the approved `spec.md` or `plan.md`. - **Step 6 is conditional:** it runs only when `plan.md` has E2E candidates approved at Gate 2; otherwise the flow goes straight from 7 to 8. - **Stop conditions** (constitution §3) can interrupt the autopilot at any point: a new external dependency, a breaking API contract change, or a test/build still failing after 3 self-correction attempts. ## Steps Steps 2 and 3 each have an **AI substep (a)** followed by a **human, non-AI substep (b)**: the gate. | # | Step | Description | AI used? | AI, agent, subagent or skill | Deliverable | Human in the loop | |---|------|-------------|----------|------------------------------|-------------|-------------------| | 0a | Constitution | Engineering principles and stop conditions shared by all agents. | No | — | `.specify/memory/constitution.md` | Human writes it once. Only the human changes it. | | 0b | Story intake | The functional user story is pasted verbatim, as the root of traceability. | No | — | `docs/user-stories/US-XX.md` | Human copies it from the business source. Corrections stay visible in the plan's Revisions section and the session log. | | 4a | Tasks | Breaks the plan into tasks tagged `[P]` (parallel), `[CMS]`/`[FE]` (owner) and `US-XX`/`FR-XXX`. | Yes | Orchestrator, skill `autopilot` (Spec Kit `tasks-template.md`) | `specs/.../tasks.md` | None (autopilot). | | 4b | Analyze | Automatic consistency check across `spec.md`, `plan.md` and `tasks.md`: every FR has tasks, no task without an FR, no constitution conflicts. Gaps in `tasks.md` are fixed and analyze reruns (max 3). Implementation starts only with no CRITICAL/HIGH findings. | Yes | Orchestrator, skills `autopilot` + `speckit-analyze` | `specs/.../analysis.md` (one section per run) | None, unless a finding needs a change to the approved spec or plan → human decides (back to Gate 1 or 2). | | 5 | Implementation waves | Executes tasks; `[P]` groups run in parallel subagents, dependent tasks in sequence. Only the unit tests approved at Gate 2 are written, with the code (plus regression tests for later findings). | Yes | Subagents `cms-developer` (Sonnet, skill `strapi-conventions`) and `frontend-developer` (Sonnet, skills `angular-conventions`, `ui-ux-guidelines`) | Code in `cms/` and `frontend/src/`, unit tests `*.spec.ts` | None, unless a stop condition fires. | | 6 | E2E tests — *conditional* | Writes Playwright tests from the spec's scenarios for the approved critical flows only. A spec mismatch is reported as a defect, never "fixed" in the test. | Yes | Subagent `e2e-tester` (Sonnet) | `frontend/e2e/*.spec.ts` | **Runs only if** E2E candidates were approved at Gate 2; skipped otherwise. | | 7 | Verify | Lint, typecheck, unit tests and CMS build after each wave; automatic fixes. | Yes | Orchestrator (Bash: `npm --prefix frontend run verify`, `npm --prefix cms run build`) | Green checks | Human only if still failing after 3 attempts. | | 8 | Review | Independent review of the diff against spec, plan, ADRs, constitution and conventions. Blocker/Major findings go back to the developer agents; round 2 verifies them. | Yes | Subagent `code-reviewer` (Opus — a different model from the implementers) | `specs/.../review.md` (findings, status, resolution commit) | Human only for findings still open after round 2. | | 9 | Commit | Atomic Conventional Commits per verified unit, with `Refs: US-XX` (plus `R-NN` for review fixes). Only the orchestrator commits. | Yes | Orchestrator | Git history | None. | | 10 | **Gate 3 — Handoff review** | Human runs the app, reads the handoff summary and `review.md`, checks the acceptance scenarios by hand. | **No** | — | `review.md` verdict line `Gate 3: Approved — ` | **Human.** Approves, or rejects: feedback becomes new tasks in `tasks.md` → back to 4a. | | 11 | Ready for QA | The increment is handed to QA. | No | — | Branch/PR ready | QA team. | ## Traceability `docs/user-stories/US-XX.md` → `specs/NNN-us-XX-*/spec.md` (FR-XXX) → `docs/adr/NNNN-*.md` (Related: US-XX) → `tasks.md` (US-XX, FR-XXX) → code and tests (`describe('US-XX · FR-XXX …')`) → `review.md` (R-NN) → commits (`Refs: US-XX`). ## Agents and skills | Component | Type | Responsibility | Model | |-----------|------|----------------|-------| | Main session | Orchestrator | Runs Spec Kit skills, holds the gates, runs autopilot, commits | Opus 5.5 | | `cms-developer` | Subagent | Strapi content types, seed, permissions | Sonnet | | `frontend-developer` | Subagent | Angular features and unit tests | Sonnet | | `e2e-tester` | Subagent (conditional) | Playwright tests for approved critical flows | Sonnet | | `code-reviewer` | Subagent | Independent review → `review.md` | Opus | | `autopilot` | Custom skill | Procedure: tasks → analyze → waves → verify → e2e → review → commit | — | | `angular-conventions` | Custom skill | Angular project knowledge | — | | `strapi-conventions` | Custom skill | Strapi project knowledge | — | | `ui-ux-guidelines` | Custom skill | Brand-based UI/UX guidelines: tokens, components, a11y, design options | — | | `speckit-*` | Spec Kit skills | Specify, clarify, plan, tasks, analyze | — | ## Questions ### What would we do differently with a team of 5 developers? _To be completed._ ### Which part of the flow did not work as expected and how was it adjusted? _Journal, filled as it happens:_ - **2026-11-21** — The first flow design started at "the human describes the functionality", skipping the business input. Added step 0b (verbatim story intake) so the flow starts from the functional user story and traceability has a fixed root. - **2026-11-21** — The first design ran the e2e agent on every feature. Changed to conditional: the orchestrator proposes critical candidates at Gate 2 and only approved ones are built, to avoid low-value e2e tests. - **2026-11-21** — The first design had no review step and no named subagents. Added `code-reviewer` with a two-round loop and versioned agent definitions. - **2026-11-22** — The handoff review already worked as a gate (approve/reject paths) but was not named as one, and only Gate 1 corrections were recorded in an artifact. Renamed it Gate 3 and added a Revisions section to `plan.md` for Gate 2 corrections, so every human correction leaves a trace. - **2026-11-22** — Before the first story we noticed that, without a permissions file, every command a subagent runs (npm, git) would stop for human approval, breaking the autopilot. Added `.claude/settings.json` with an allowlist for the flow's commands, and used deny rules to enforce the non-AI zones (user stories, constitution, logs, `.env`) at tool level. - **2026-11-22** — Between tasks (4) and review (8) the only automatic check was verify (7), which tests code but not whether the tasks cover the spec. A missing FR would only be caught by the reviewer, after implementation. Added step 4b: Spec Kit's `analyze` checks FR ↔ task coverage before any code is written, with no extra human gate. - **2026-11-22** — In the first Gate 1 run (US-00), the clarify question and its options were written as plain chat text and got collapsed in the desktop app: the human never saw them. Gate questions are now asked with the interactive question dialog (`AskUserQuestion`), one per call, recommended option first; the question and answer are repeated in text for the log (rule in `CLAUDE.md` › Asking the Human). ### At which points did we decide not to use AI and why? - **Constitution (0a):** the rules that govern the agents must come from the human, not from the agents. - **Story intake (0b):** the business wording must stay untouched to be a reliable source of truth. - **Gates 1, 2 and 3 (2b, 3b, 10):** approval is a human responsibility by definition. - _More to be added as they happen._ adr/ user-stories/

Standard Spec Kit invites a human review after every phase; we cut that to the three points where a human adds the most value — *what* to build (spec), *how* to build it (plan), and whether the result is ready for QA (handoff). Everything between the plan and the handoff runs on autopilot, bounded by explicit stop conditions. Goal: as little friction as possible without losing control. The decision and its alternatives are recorded in `docs/adr/0002-agentic-workflow-spec-kit-and-human-gates.md`. **Governance:** - `.specify/memory/constitution.md` — engineering principles and when agents must stop and ask.
